entries.title: Value Clip
entries.overview: NOTE: The Geometry Clip Sequence LOP should be used in preference to this node in most situations. In USD, a _value clip_ is a way of storing data sets in separate files. * This allows you to split large data across multiple files. For example, simulations or other animated data where the size of each time sample is so large that authoring all time samples to a single file is unwieldy (such as in terms of required network bandwidth). * Value clips are also useful in situations where you may have a library of animation clips which need to be run in a sequence or a loop. Often different primitives can share animation clips, but assemble the clips in different ways to create the appearance of variation. * Value clips allow flexibility in composing layer overrides. USD value resolution stipulates that the first (strongest) layer that contains _any_ timeSample for an attribute is the source of _all_ timeSamples for the attribute. This is often fine, but for huge numbers of timeSamples you may need more flexibility. You should read the USD documentation for value clips to understand how they work and how you can use them: * Value clips in Pixar's USD glossary * Value clips in the USD manual NOTE: * This node provides a way of authoring a value clip composition arc in USD. Future versions of Solaris may have more tools for working with and using value clips at a higher level. * An alternative to using the Value Clip LOP is to use the USD Stitch Clips ROP to author a USD layer file containing a value clip definition that you can reference into a scene. This approach has the benefit that it also creates a topology layer and a manifest layer, which can improve the performance of the value clip composition. * A sequence of .bgeo or similar non-native USD files can be loaded directly as value clips, however you must ensure that each geometry file generate its USD attribute data with the correct time sample. This can be achieved by writing the time value into the geometry file as a detail attribute created by the USD Configure SOP. Or, the time value can be specified by appending arguments to the geometry file path with the suffix /tmp/file.$F4.bgeo.sc:SDF_FORMAT_ARGS:sampleframe=$F.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path of the prim on which to author a reference to the value clip. If the specified primitive does not exist, the node will create it with no primitive type (the primitive type will come from the value clip file).

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the prim at Primitive Path didn't already exist so this node has to create it, the node sets this as the new prim's kind.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of the path in Primitive Path do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.

parameters.label: Clip Set
parameters.description: The name of the clip set the value clip belongs to (multiple clip sets can exist on a single prim).

parameters.label: Clip Primitive Path
parameters.description: The path of a prim within the value clip file that should be mapped onto Primitive Path when accessing values.

parameters.label: Manifest File
parameters.description: The file path to an optional manifest file that specifies exactly which primitives and values should be brought in from the value clip files. Providing this file helps the USD framework optimize value clip resolution. See the USD documentation for more information about the manifest file.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The frame on the current stage at which the value clip resolution should start.

parameters.label: First Clip Start Frame
parameters.description: When this is turned on, it sets a different start time within the value clip files. When this is turned off, the nodes uses the Start Frame parameter as the clip start time.

parameters.label: Clip Time Scale
parameters.description: A scale factor applied to the time samples read in from the clip files.

parameters.label: Loop Until Frame
parameters.description: To create a repeating loop of the specified clip files, turn on this parameter and set it to the end frame of the loop. (USD does not natively support looping of animation or value clips, so this node explicitly authors all provided clips repeatedly until the requested loop end time is reached.)

parameters.label: Loop First and Last Frames Match
parameters.description: When looping an animation and using deformation or transform motion blur, it is important that the first and last frames of the looping animation are identical. In this case, enable this parameter so that the Value Clip LOP will author a "discontinuity" in the clip frames when looping from the end of the animation back to the start. This discontinuity prevents doubling up the display of the shared first and last frame, while also avoiding unexpected motion blur effects. With this option turned off, the clip times metadata for a looping 100 frame clip would be (1, 1), (100, 100), (101, 1), (200, 100). In this data, the first number in each pair is the global stage frame number, and the second number is the frame within the clip that should be displayed for that global frame. So stage frame 1 is clip frame 1. Stage frame 100 is clip frame 100. Then stage frame 101 is back to clip frame 1. There are two problems here. First, if the clip's first and last frames are equal, frame 100 and frame 101 will be identical. But even worse, when rendering with motion blur (using a shutter open/close of +/- 0.5), rendering frame 101 will show data interpolated at frames 100.5 and 101.5. But USD does this by interpolating the _clip metadata_, not the data stored within the clips. So the frame 101.5 data will be as expected (showing data from clip frame 1.5). But the frame 100.5 data will be generated by grabbing the clip data at a frame half way between 100 and 1, which is frame 50.5. This is obviously very unexpected. With this option turned on, the same setup would author clip times of (1, 1), (100, 100), (100, 1), (199, 100). Note that there are two different clip times authored for the single stage time of 100. This is the "discontinuity". But it eliminates both problems mentioned above. Stage frame 100 is clip frame 100, but stage frame 101 is now clip frame 2, eliminating the duplicated data. And for motion blur rendering frame 101, frame 100.5 will use the clip data at frame 0.5 and 1.5, exactly as expected. Note that, if the first and last frames of the clip are not equal, there is no way to get perfect looping, unless you use velocity motion blur which does not require grabbing interpolated data between frames. The first problem mentioned above (the duplicated frame at the end of the loop) will be avoided, but the clip metadata interpolation approach used by USD means sampling frame 100.5 will return data from the middle of the clip, resulting in incorrect motion blurring.

parameters.label: Number of Clips
parameters.description: You can add references to multiple clip files in one node. Set this to the number of clips to reference, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove clips.

parameters.label: Clip File or Sequence
parameters.description: The file path to this value clip file. This path can include number-sign (#) characters to perform numeric substitutions in a loop. For example, on disk there may be multiple files named sim_0001.usd, sim_0002.usd and so on, each containing one frame of animation. In this case you could use sim_####.usd. Numeric substitution only happens if File Sequence count is turned on. See File Sequence Count, File Index Start, and File Index Step below. For example, if you turn on File Sequence Count and set * Clip File or Sequence to sim_####.usd, * File Index Start to 10, * File Index Step to 2, and * File Sequence Count to 3, the node will try to load sim_0010.usd, sim_0012.usd, and sim_0014.usd. If you use numeric substitution, each file must have the same number of frames of animation (File Duration).

parameters.label: File Duration
parameters.description: The number of frames for which this clip file is active. If the Clip File or Sequence path matched multiple files through numeric substitution, each clip file will get this same duration.

parameters.label: File Sequence Count
parameters.description: If you turn this on, the node evaluates the Clip File or Sequence filename with numeric substitution this many times, starting the number at File Index Start and increasing the number each time by File Index Step.

parameters.label: File Index Start
parameters.description: When File Sequence Count is turned on, the node evaluates the Clip File or Sequence multiple times with numeric substitution, starting at this number.

parameters.label: File Index Step
parameters.description: When File Sequence Count is turned on, the node evaluates the Clip File or Sequence multiple times with numeric substitution, incrementing the number by this many each time.

entries.title: Vary Material Assignment
entries.summary: Assign different materials across a number of prims to create variation.
entries.overview: It's often useful to assign different materials across a large number of objects, to create a more natural look. This node lets you assign materials randomly, or "spatially", so clumps of prims tend to get the same material.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect Reselect button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the Reselect button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives. NOTE: This parameter needs to be exposed in order for the transform handles to be context-aware. Without it, the handles may not be positioned properly.

parameters.label: Materials
parameters.description: The material prims to choose from. You can use primitive patterns, including matching all prims in a collection (using /path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>).

parameters.label: Purpose
parameters.description: TBD

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: TBD

parameters.label: Bind Method
parameters.description: TBD

parameters.label: Binding Path
parameters.description: TBD

parameters.label: Collection Path
parameters.description: TBD

parameters.label: Collection Name
parameters.description: TBD

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for random material selection. Changing this changes the "random" choices generated. You can use this to try different variations, or change the random choices over time.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: How to choose materials for each selected prim. Random: Choose materials at random. You can use the Bias ramp to influence the distribution. Spatial Distribution: Assign materials in Voronoi noise-based "clumps", so prims in close proximity often get the same material. Weighted Random: Like Random, but lets you assign weights to each material, so some materials are chosen more often than others.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: When Method is Random, the horizontal axis is divided between the materials to choose from. At the center of a horizontal segment corresponding to a certain material, the height of the ramp is the percentage chance of that material being chosen. Set the Interpolation to Constant. For example, given three materials, to give the second material a 50% chance of being assigned, add a point at position 0.25, with a value of 0.5, set the last point's position to 0.75 with a value of 1. If the probabilities don't add up to exactly 100% the values are normalized. This ramp might be useful to interactively play with material probabilities, however if you want to assign specific probabilities to specific materials, it's much easier to use Method > Weighted Random.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Whether to specify the time at which to measure the prim positions in frames or by seconds.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: Measure the positions of the prims at this frame number.

parameters.label: Integer Frames
parameters.description: Rounds the given frame number to the nearest integer frame, avoiding fractional frame cooking.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: Measure the positions of the prims at this number of seconds along the timeline.

parameters.label: Auto-fill Materials
parameters.description: Creates multi-parm instances for each material selected in the Materials field. If you change the Materials pattern and want to re-do this, click Clear in the multi-parm, then click this button again.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: For each material, whether to assign it a weight.

parameters.label: Material Path
parameters.description: Scene graph path to the material prim. If this material doesn't exist, or isn't listed in Materials, the node ignores it.

parameters.label: Weight
parameters.description: A weighting factor to assign to the material. Materials with higher weights are more likely to be chosen. The node normalizes the weights, so they are all relative to each other. Note that materials listed in Materials but not in the multi-parm are considered to have a weight of 1.

entries.title: Volume
entries.summary: References volume data on disk into a volume prim containing field prims.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a Cache LOP following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time. Sample Current Frame: A single time sample will be generated for the current time. Sample Frame Range If Input Is Not Time Dependent: If the input to this node is time dependent, this node behaves as if it is in Sample Current Frame mode. Otherwise it behaves as if it is in Sample Frame Range mode. Sample Frame Range: The Start/End/Inc parameter is used to generate multiple times at which this node's parameters are evaluated, and a USD time sample is created for each attribute at each one of these times.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When the Sampling behavior is Sample Frame Range, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are @fstart, @fend, and @finc. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times. Specify Manually: The Shutter Open/Close parameter values provide exact offset values relative to the primary sample time. Use Camera Prim: The Camera Prim parameter provides the scene graph path of a camera primitive from which the shutter open and close times are extracted to provide the offset values relative to the primary time sample.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Specify Manually, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.description: When Shutter is set to Use Camera Prim, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the Samples value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the Samples parameter.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: Create the main volume primitive at this scene graph path.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: Set this as the new volume prim's kind. The default is None.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If any parents of the path in Primitive Path do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: Determines the USD specifier set on the volume primitive and any ancestor primitives created by this LOP.

parameters.label: Generate Errors For Missing Files
parameters.description: If any volume files cannot be found or cannot be loaded, this node will generate an error, causing all downstream nodes to also error. Turn off this option to generate warnings instead. This is only recommended in the early stages of a project where the integrity of the output does not need to be validated.

parameters.label: Files
parameters.description: This node can reference multiple files as fields of a single volume. Set this to the number of fields to read, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove field file references.

parameters.label: File Path
parameters.description: The location of the volume file on disk. USD is not capable of representing volumes currently. It can only point to volumes stored as separate files on disk. These files can be BGEO _or_ VDB when working _within_ Houdini and using a Houdini render delegate. If you want to use the volume data with non-Houdini processes, then you'll need to save the volume data as VDB files.

parameters.label: Fields
parameters.description: A space separated list of field names (as they appear in the file) to read. You can use patterns to match multiple names.

parameters.label: Transform Description
parameters.description: Because all USD edits are non-destructive, editing transforms is accomplished adding a xformOp:transform attribute. Each attribute name has a descriptive suffix. For example, if you set this to foo, it authors an attribute named xformOp:transform:foo. The resulting full attribute name must be unique among attributes on the same prim (Houdini will automatically alter the name by adding a number if it's not unique). The default ($OS) uses the node name as the descriptive suffix.

parameters.label: Apply Transform in World Space
parameters.description: (Default on) Apply the given transform as if it was in world space. When this is off, the transform is local. parameters.label: Use XformCommonAPI
parameters.description: The transform specified in the remaining transform parameters will be expressed using a Houdini-defined extension of the USD XformCommonAPI specification.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

entries.title: Align
entries.summary: Transforms a layer to align with another layer.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The definition of the source rectangle to use for alignment. See Data and display windows for more information. Data Window: The data window is where pixels are actually present in the image. A cropped image or overscan image may not match the display window. Display Window: The display window is the idealized location of the real screen and is independent of any overscan or cropping effects.

parameters.label: Justify with
parameters.description: The target to which the source is aligned. Reference Data Window: The reference data window is the actual pixels of the reference. If you're trying to line up two crops, usually the data windows of each are used. Reference Display Window: The display window is the idealized location of the real screen in the reference. Use this option to align to a position of the reference screen. Target Point: Specify a specific point in the space of the reference layer.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The space in which to specify the target. This applies to the size_ref input, which is the reference layer. Image: Use image coordinates that range from -1 to 1 on the display window of the layer. Texture: Use texture coordinates that range from 0 to 1 on the data window of the layer. Pixels: Use absolute pixel locations in the layer. World: Use coordinates in world space that project through the layer's implicit camera.

parameters.label: Target Point
parameters.description: The target point. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

parameters.label: Target Size
parameters.description: The target size. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

parameters.label: Justify X
parameters.description: The side of the source rectangle to use. None: No movement on this axis. Min: Align the minimum of the source rectangle. Center: Align the center of the source rectangle. Max: Align the maximum of the source rectangle.

parameters.label: Justify Y
parameters.description: The side of the source rectangle to use. None: No movement on this axis. Min: Align the minimum of the source rectangle. Center: Align the center of the source rectangle. Max: Align the maximum of the source rectangle.

parameters.label: Goal X/Y
parameters.description: The target side of the alignment. Same: Align to the same side of the target that the source used, so minimum to minimum and center to center. Min: The minimum of the target rectangle is the goal. Center: The center of the target rectangle is the goal. Max: The maximum of the target rectangle is the goal.

parameters.label: Offset by
parameters.description: An additional offset (in image space) from the computed alignment position.

parameters.label: Scale to Fit
parameters.description: Scales the layer so the source rectangle fits inside the target rectangle.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: Scales uniformly in all axes.

parameters.label: Scale Axis
parameters.description: The axis to use to fit.

parameters.label: Scale X
parameters.description: Scales the x-axis to fit.

parameters.label: Scale Y
parameters.description: Scales the y-axis to fit.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The source layer to align.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: An optional reference layer to align to.

outputs.label: result
outputs.description: The source layer transformed to align with the specified target.

entries.title: Align Pixels
entries.summary: Shifts a layer to align pixelwise with another layer.

parameters.label: Snapping
parameters.description: The initial snapping needs to pick a point on the source layer to snap. This point will be mapped as closely as possible, but if there are scales or rotations, other points may end up increasingly distant from their own snapped location. This is also used as the source window for alignment. Data Window: The snapping point is picked from the data window of the source. This is where pixels actually are; so usually includes effects of cropping or overscan. Display Window: The snapping point is picked from the display window of the source. This is the idealized screen location in pixels, so is independent of cropping or overscan.

parameters.label: Side
parameters.description: Which side to locate the snapping point on the snapwindow, in Y.

parameters.label: Side
parameters.description: Which side to locate the snapping point on the snapwindow, in X.

parameters.label: Justify with
parameters.description: The alignment works by aligning a source rectangle with a target rectangle. Reference Data Window: Use the data window of the reference as the target rectangle. Reference Display Window: Use the display window of the reference as the target rectangle. Original Data Window: Use the data window of the source as the target rectangle. Original Display Window: Use the display window of the source as the target rectangle. Target Point: Use a specific point for the target. Since resizing isn't possible, this is just a single point.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The space in which to specify the target. This applies to the size_ref input, which is the reference layer. Image: Use image coordinates that range from -1 to 1 on the display window of the layer. Texture: Use texture coordinates that range from 0 to 1 on the data window of the layer. Pixels: Use absolute pixel locations in the layer. World: Use coordinates in world space that project through the layer's implicit camera.

parameters.label: Target Point
parameters.description: The target point. The Units parameter determines if this is in image, texture, pixel, or world space.

parameters.label: Justify X/Y
parameters.description: Controls which side of the source rectangle is used. None: No movement on this axis Min: The minimum of the source rectangle is aligned. Center: The center of the source rectangle is aligned. Max: The maximum of the source rectangle is aligned.

parameters.label: Goal X/Y
parameters.description: Controls the target side of the alignment. Same: Aligned to the same side of the target that the source used, so minimum to minimum and center to center. Min: The minimum of the target rectangle is the goal. Center: The center of the target rectangle is the goal. Max: The maximum of the target rectangle is the goal.

parameters.label: Offset by
parameters.description: An additional nudge from the computed alignment position. This is in pixels.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: A layer to align.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: An optional reference layer to align to.

outputs.label: result
outputs.description: The source layer shifted to align with the specified target.

entries.title: Auto Stereogram
entries.summary: Generates an image with a 3D illusion.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The sampling frequency of the source image. Higher values increase the amount that the source texture repeats, but a frequency that's too large may generate incoherent noise that you can't resolve.

parameters.label: Depth Range
parameters.description: The range to clamp the values in the depth image to for stability. Incoming depth values must be positive, with larger depths appearing more extruded in the stereogram. You can add a Remap COP before this node to put the depth values into a usable range.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Re-Center
parameters.description: Distorts outwards from the center, producing a symmetric result. When off, this applies the sampling distortion from left to right.

outputs.label: stereogram
outputs.description: The generated auto stereogram.

entries.title: Layer Merge
entries.summary: Combines all inputs.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The method used to determine which pixels in the foreground and background match. See /copernicus/spaces for more information. Image: Match layers by image coordinates. Pixels remain square and match based on the 2D canvas in which the images are embedded, but ignore 3D transformations. Texture: Match the data windows of the two layers. This stretches the layers so they overlap exactly. Pixel: Match the display windows in pixel space. This ensures pixels are the same size, and uses the data window offset to offset the coordinates. World: Use the background layer's camera to project the foreground onto the background. This matches what you expect to see in the 3D viewport.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The method used to combine the pixel values of the layers. Add: Add the input layers' pixel values together. Average: Use the average pixel value of the combined input layers. Multiply: Multiply the input layers' pixel values together. Min: Use the minimum pixel value of the combined input layers. Max: Use the maximum pixel value of the combined input layers. Over: Place the preceeding RGBA values over the following RGBA values. Non-RGBA layers copy the final layer's pixels.

parameters.label: Clip by Data Window
parameters.description: Adds an implied mask that matches the data window of the fg input. This prevents the image from extending into the destination. NOTE: The clipping is sharp.

parameters.label: Crop to Content
parameters.description: Crops the output layer to the size of the source layers' transformed data windows.

inputs.label: source#
inputs.description: The original layer, VDB, or attribute to combine.

outputs.label: combine
outputs.description: The combined source layers, VDBs, or attributes.

entries.title: Bake Geometry Textures
entries.summary: Generates textures by baking between a low-resolution and high-resolution mesh at interactive speeds.

parameters.label: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracer to use. This is an automatic menu that shows only available options based on your hardware. NOTE: OptiX is only available on NVIDIA hardware.

parameters.label: Tracing Mode
parameters.description: The tracing mode that the baker utilizes. Surface Normal: Traditional baking by firing rays bidirectionally from the normals of the low-resolution geometry. Requires a low and high input. Cage Mesh: Use a cage mesh to help improve the texture maps. It's sometimes problematic to determine the direction of the rays from the low-resolution mesh to the high-resolution mesh. When you specify a cage mesh, rays are sent from the position on the cage mesh towards the corresponding position on the low-resolution mesh. When you bake with a cage, the cage must be entirely outside of the high-resolution mesh. NOTE: The low-resolution and cage mesh must have the same topology. Cage meshes are used only when the Tracing Mode is Cage Mesh. Single Mesh (low): Bakes the data of a single mesh, and uses the same mesh for the low-resolution and high-resolution mesh. Requires a low input.

parameters.label: UDIM Override
parameters.description: Select a UDIM to bake, which overrides the UDIM context option.

parameters.label: Face Visibility Culling
parameters.description: The method used to handle secondary rays that interact with the geometry. This can allow floaters on the geometry to be projected onto the low-resolution map without casting a shadow. No Culling: Don't ignore any secondary rays. Backface: Ignore any secondary rays that hit the backfaces of the geometry.

parameters.label: Sample Multiplier
parameters.description: The amount to multiply against the Sample parameters, such as Occlusion Samples and Thickness Samples. This acts as a general quality scale. For example, a Sample Multiplier of 0.5 and Occlusion Samples of 256 bakes occlusion at 128.

parameters.label: Auto Generate Cage
parameters.description: Creates a duplicate mesh of the low-resolution mesh. This automatically generates a cage mesh internally instead of requiring a cage input.

parameters.label: Cage Offset
parameters.description: How far the duplicate mesh peaks out from the normals of the original low-resolution mesh.

parameters.label: Soften Cage
parameters.description: Facets the geometry before applying the Cage Offset. A soft cage isn't faceted and ensures a seamless result across sharp edges, but can cause projection errors and skewed detail as the normals are averaged. An unsoftened cage (which is faceted) can fix this projection skewing, but can cause missing detail capture on sharp edges. TIP: A skew input can apply projection error fixes on the output maps. It works by creating a copy of the cage mesh, but averages and softens its normals by face area. The final ray directions are then blended between the original low-resolution normals and the softened normals based on this mono map.

parameters.label: Normals
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals. Error if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces an error if no normal attribute is present. Warning if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces a warning if no normal attribute is present, but adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Silently Create Missing Normals: Silently adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally.

parameters.label: Tangents
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing tangent attributes. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have tangent attributes. Add MikkT Tangents if Needed: Adds MikkT tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Add Texture UV Tangents if Needed: Adds texture UV tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Error if No Tangent Attributes Present: Produces an error if tangent attributes are missing.

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute to use for UV unwrapping and rasterization. This can be a vertex or point.

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.description: The amount to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-resolution mesh when rays are sent from the low-resolution mesh to the scene. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-resolution mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.

parameters.label: task: Use Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: # Create a piece attribute (such as using a Name node) and assign the same name to primitives on both the low-resolution and high-resolution that you would like to trace purely against each other. If you have a character with a backpack on for example, set the shirt primitives on both the low and high to contain a name attribute of shirt, and the backpack on both the low and high to have the name attribute backpack. # Turn on Match Pieces by Name and set the Piece Attribute to the piece attribute you used to assign the sets. This is name by default. # (Optional) Update Include Pieces with space-separated names. By default, it contains * to use all sets. For example, shirt backpack bakes only shirt and backpack trace sets. If you have a lot of sets, you can exclude a few.

parameters.label: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: Lets you control which primitives are visible when computing ray tracing effects like occlusion and curvature. This matches primitives between the low-resolution and high-resolution geometry and isolates them in their own pocket dimension, which can be used to prevent intersection errors. If a ray hits an object that doesn't belong to the current matched piece, it's ignored. This causes a rebake and changes the bake results. NOTE: This parameter is internally known as Trace Sets.

parameters.label: Piece Attribute
parameters.description: The primitive piece attribute to use to identify the different pieces across the low-resolution, high-resolution, and cage.

parameters.label: Include Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always include in the bake. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching.

parameters.label: Exclude Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always exclude from the bake. This happens after the include pieces are gathered. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching. For example, if your include is * but your exclude is hat, the baker bakes every set available except hat.

parameters.label: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Fills empty areas of the image using colors at the edges of non-empty areas. This is a post-process that fixes darker pixel values at the edges of UV seams, and can produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures. NOTE: This process can be time consuming. For faster iterations, turn this feature on only for the final baking.

parameters.label: Exterior
parameters.description: The method used to set the pixels beyond the edge padding. Unchanged: Leave the pixels unchanged. Black: Set the pixels to black (0). Diffuse Fill: Run a Smooth Fill COP over the region, which smoothly interpolates the pixel values.

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.description: The distance (in image coordinates) to directly copy pixel values into the exterior.

parameters.label: Edge Offset
parameters.description: When reading the original value to copy outwards for edge padding, the value exactly at the edge padding may already have exterior color incorporated. This is the distance (in image coordinates) to backtrack and read clean values for extrapolation.

parameters.label: Exclude Alpha from UV Fill
parameters.description: Turns off UV filling on the alpha map. Adding UV filling to alpha often results in a fully white output.

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.

parameters.label: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Tangent Normal map. When off, the normal output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Rounded Edge Normal map. When off, the edgenormal output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Rounded Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Rounded Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Rounded Edge Normal. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Rounded Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold are assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.description: Whether to record the world space position in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.

parameters.label: World Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the World Normal map. When off, the worldnormal output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: World Normal Space
parameters.description: How to represent the normal map. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Position map. When off, the position output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Position Space
parameters.description: How to represent the position map. Absolute ( Use Actual Position Values ): The position isn't normalized and dependent on object size and world position. Relative ( Use Position Within Bounding Box): The position is normalized relative to its bounding box.

parameters.label: Bounding Box
parameters.description: When the Position is stored, this is how the position is represented. Fit to Bounding Box: The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. Fit to Uniform Box (No Stretching): The shading position is fit to a uniform bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. In this mode, all three axes of the bounding box have the same length.

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Ambient Occlusion map. When off, the occlusion output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Occlusion. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Occlusion Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Occlusion. A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Curvature map. When off, the curvature output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Curvature. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Curvature Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Smaller values (which create smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (which represent greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether the map looks more concave or more convex. Smaller values emphasize concavity, higher values enhance convexity.

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Edge map. When off, the edge output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Edge. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Edge Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded edge.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons with an angle below this threshold are considered smooth and don't appear in the Edge map.

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Cavity map. When off, the cavity output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Cavity. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Cavity Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Limits how far rays can detect nearby geometry. Smaller values (smaller distance) emphasize concavity.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Blends between a full cavity contrast (0) and a flat result (1).

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Thickness map. When off, the thickness output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Thickness. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Thickness Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Invert Thickness Map
parameters.description: Inverts the Thickness map so that thinner areas create darker values and thicker areas create brighter values.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Height map. When off, the height output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Height Space
parameters.description: Height bakes the true displacement between the low-resolution and high-resolution. This distance may be miniscule so the output image can appear nearly entirely black, which may not be useful when used in masking or shaders so may require manual remapping later. Set this to Custom to remap the height map. True Displacement: True displacement values. These may be visually unfriendly results, and for some bake meshes appear completely black if the geometric difference between the low-resolution and high-resolution is small. Custom: Remap the height layer according to inner and outer distance parameters.

parameters.label: Inner Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the inner distance to 0.0.

parameters.label: Outer Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the outer distance to 1.0.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Alpha map. When off, the alpha output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Mask Out High Resolution Mesh
parameters.description: Checks for any valid hits on the high-resolution mesh and creates an alpha mask from this, rather than the low-resolution UV map.

parameters.label: Quick Setups
parameters.description: Add a geometry attribute to bake.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: Turns on the Position map's baking, which bakes the world position values to the RGB components of the layer. When off, the position output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to rasterize. This must match the attribute present on the geometry. This can be a Point, Vertex, or Primitive.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The output type for the rasterized attribute. To be rasterized, an attribute must either be an integer or a float of four or less components. Mono: Mono layer for single float attributes. UV: UV layer for float2 attributes. RGB: RGB layer for float3 attributes. RGBA: RGBA layer for float4 attributes. ID: ID layer for integer attributes.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: low
inputs.description: A mesh that fires rays and has the final texture maps projected onto. The polygons are rasterized based on the mesh's UV coordinates.

inputs.label: high
inputs.description: The mesh to bake.

inputs.label: cage
inputs.description: An optional custom cage geometry. When Tracing Mode is Cage Mesh, rays are fired from the normals of this mesh instead of the low-resolution mesh.

inputs.label: skew
inputs.description: An input map for where to apply skew correction.

outputs.label: normal
outputs.description: The map of the tangent space normals of the high-resolution.

outputs.label: edgenormal
outputs.description: The map of the rounded edge tangent space normals of the high-resolution.

outputs.label: worldnormal

outputs.label: occlusion

outputs.label: curvature

outputs.label: edge
outputs.description: The map of the edge details of the high poly mesh.

outputs.label: cavity

outputs.label: thickness

entries.title: Bake Geometry Textures
entries.summary: Generates textures by baking between a low-resolution and high-resolution mesh at interactive speeds.

parameters.label: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracer to use. This is an automatic menu that shows only available options based on your hardware. NOTE: OptiX is only available on NVIDIA hardware.

parameters.label: Tracing Mode
parameters.description: The tracing mode that the baker utilizes. Surface Normal: Traditional baking by firing rays bidirectionally from the normals of the low-resolution geometry. Requires a low and high input. Cage Mesh: Use a cage mesh to help improve the texture maps. It's sometimes problematic to determine the direction of the rays from the low-resolution mesh to the high-resolution mesh. When you specify a cage mesh, rays are sent from the position on the cage mesh towards the corresponding position on the low-resolution mesh. When you bake with a cage, the cage must be entirely outside of the high-resolution mesh. NOTE: The low-resolution and cage mesh must have the same topology. Cage meshes are used only when the Tracing Mode is Cage Mesh. Single Mesh (low): Bakes the data of a single mesh, and uses the same mesh for the low-resolution and high-resolution mesh. Requires a low input.

parameters.label: UDIM Override
parameters.description: Select a UDIM to bake, which overrides the UDIM context option.

parameters.label: Sample Multiplier
parameters.description: The amount to multiply against the Sample parameters, such as Occlusion Samples and Thickness Samples. This acts as a general quality scale. For example, a Sample Multiplier of 0.5 and Occlusion Samples of 256 bakes occlusion at 128.

parameters.label: Face Culling
parameters.description: Specifies which polygons to ignore when Ray Tracing primary rays. No Culling: Don't ignore any faces. Back Faces: Ignore Primary Rays that hit the back faces of the bake mesh. Front Faces: Ignore Primary Rays that hit the front faces of the bake mesh.

parameters.label: Visibility Culling
parameters.description: The method used to handle secondary rays that interact with the geometry. This can allow floaters on the geometry to be projected onto the low-resolution map without casting a shadow. No Culling: Don't ignore any secondary rays. Back Faces: Ignore any secondary rays that hit the back faces of the geometry. Front Faces: Ignore any secondary rays that hit the front faces of the geometry.

parameters.label: Ray Start (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage input, which stores the Ray Start Positions.

parameters.label: Ray Direction (Vertex)
parameters.description: The vertex attribute that lives on the cage input, which stores the Ray Directions.

parameters.label: Ray Length (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage input, which stores the Ray Lengths.

parameters.label: If Ray Length Missing:
parameters.description: How to handle the ray lengths when the ray length attribute doesn't exist, such as when a Bake Pre-Process node is not used in the workflow. For example, use this parameter when a custom cage already exists. Rays Are Endless: Rays travel infinitely until they hit something. Custom Ray Length: Set a custom ray length.

parameters.label: Custom Ray Length
parameters.description: The length of the rays in world units.

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.description: The amount to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-resolution mesh when rays are sent from the low-resolution mesh to the scene. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-resolution mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.

parameters.label: Normals
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals. Error if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces an error if no normal attribute is present. Warning if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces a warning if no normal attribute is present, but adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Silently Create Missing Normals: Silently adds point normals weighted by vertex angle internally.

parameters.label: Tangents
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing tangent attributes. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have tangent attributes. Add MikkT Tangents if Needed: Adds MikkT tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Add Texture UV Tangents if Needed: Adds texture UV tangents using a Polyframe SOP internally. Error if No Tangent Attributes Present: Produces an error if tangent attributes are missing.

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute to use for UV unwrapping and rasterization. This can be a vertex or point.

parameters.label: Remove UV Z values
parameters.description: Flattens the Z component of float3 UV attributes to 0. Some UV nodes output float3 values by default, which can lead to unexpected results when rasterizing in UV mode.

parameters.label: task: Use Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: # Create a piece attribute (such as using a Name node) and assign the same name to primitives on both the low-resolution and high-resolution that you would like to trace purely against each other. If you have a character with a backpack on for example, set the shirt primitives on both the low and high to contain a name attribute of shirt, and the backpack on both the low and high to have the name attribute backpack. # Turn on Match Pieces by Name and set the Piece Attribute to the piece attribute you used to assign the sets. This is name by default. # (Optional) Update Include Pieces with space-separated names. By default, it contains * to use all sets. For example, shirt backpack bakes only shirt and backpack trace sets. If you have a lot of sets, you can exclude a few.

parameters.label: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: Lets you control which primitives are visible when computing ray tracing effects like occlusion and curvature. This matches primitives between the low-resolution and high-resolution geometry and isolates them in their own pocket dimension, which can be used to prevent intersection errors. If a ray hits an object that doesn't belong to the current matched piece, it's ignored. This causes a rebake and changes the bake results. NOTE: This parameter is internally known as Trace Sets.

parameters.label: Piece Attribute
parameters.description: The primitive piece attribute to use to identify the different pieces across the low-resolution, high-resolution, and cage.

parameters.label: Include Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always include in the bake. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching.

parameters.label: Exclude Pieces
parameters.description: The sets to always exclude from the bake. This happens after the include pieces are gathered. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching. For example, if your include is * but your exclude is hat, the baker bakes every set available except hat.

parameters.label: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Fills empty areas of the image using colors at the edges of non-empty areas. This is a post-process that fixes darker pixel values at the edges of UV seams, and can produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures. NOTE: This process can be time consuming. For faster iterations, turn this feature on only for the final baking.

parameters.label: Exterior
parameters.description: The method used to set the pixels beyond the edge padding. Unchanged: Leave the pixels unchanged. Black: Set the pixels to black (0). Diffuse Fill: Run a Smooth Fill COP over the region, which smoothly interpolates the pixel values.

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.description: The distance (in image coordinates) to directly copy pixel values into the exterior.

parameters.label: Edge Offset
parameters.description: When reading the original value to copy outwards for edge padding, the value exactly at the edge padding may already have exterior color incorporated. This is the distance (in image coordinates) to backtrack and read clean values for extrapolation.

parameters.label: Exclude Alpha from UV Fill
parameters.description: Turns off UV filling on the alpha map. Adding UV filling to alpha often results in a fully white output.

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.

parameters.label: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Tangent Normal map. When off, the normal output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Rounded Edge Normal map. When off, the edgenormal output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Rounded Normal Space
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from -1 to 1. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from 0 to 1. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Rounded Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Rounded Edge Normal. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Rounded Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold are assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.description: Whether to record the world space position in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.

parameters.label: World Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the World Normal map. When off, the worldnormal output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: World Normal Space
parameters.description: How to represent the normal map. Signed (-1 to 1): Signed normals where the x, y, and z components range from -1 to 1. Offset (0 to 1): Offset normals where the x, y, and z components range from 0 to 1.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Position map. When off, the position output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Position Space
parameters.description: How to represent the position map. Absolute ( Use Actual Position Values ): The position isn't normalized and dependent on object size and world position. Relative ( Use Position Within Bounding Box): The position is normalized relative to its bounding box.

parameters.label: Bounding Box
parameters.description: When the Position is stored, this is how the position is represented. Fit to Bounding Box: The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. Fit to Uniform Box (No Stretching): The shading position is fit to a uniform bounding box of the low-resolution mesh. In this mode, all three axes of the bounding box have the same length.

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Ambient Occlusion map. When off, the occlusion output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Occlusion. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Occlusion Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Occlusion. A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Curvature map. When off, the curvature output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Curvature. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Curvature Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Smaller values (which create smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (which represent greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Controls whether the map looks more concave or more convex. Smaller values emphasize concavity, higher values enhance convexity.

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Edge map. When off, the edge output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Edge. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Edge Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded edge.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Polygons with an angle below this threshold are considered smooth and don't appear in the Edge map.

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Cavity map. When off, the cavity output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Cavity. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Cavity Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: Limits how far rays can detect nearby geometry. Smaller values (smaller distance) emphasize concavity.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Blends between a full cavity contrast (0) and a flat result (1).

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Thickness map. When off, the thickness output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing Thickness. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase Thickness Samples to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Invert Thickness Map
parameters.description: Inverts the Thickness map so that thinner areas create darker values and thicker areas create brighter values.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Height map. When off, the height output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Height Space
parameters.description: Height bakes the true displacement between the low-resolution and high-resolution. This distance may be miniscule so the output image can appear nearly entirely black, which may not be useful when used in masking or shaders so may require manual remapping later. Set this to Custom to remap the height map. True Displacement: True displacement values. These may be visually unfriendly results, and for some bake meshes appear completely black if the geometric difference between the low-resolution and high-resolution is small. Custom: Remap the height layer according to inner and outer distance parameters.

parameters.label: Inner Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the inner distance to 0.0.

parameters.label: Outer Distance
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the outer distance to 1.0.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the Alpha map. When off, the alpha output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Mask Out High Resolution Mesh
parameters.description: Checks for any valid hits on the high-resolution mesh and creates an alpha mask from this, rather than the low-resolution UV map.

parameters.label: Quick Setups
parameters.description: Add a geometry attribute to bake.

parameters.label: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: The number of custom attributes to rasterize.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: Turns on the Position map's baking, which bakes the world position values to the RGB components of the layer. When off, the position output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to rasterize. This must match the attribute present on the geometry. This can be a Point, Vertex, or Primitive.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The output type for the rasterized attribute. To be rasterized, an attribute must either be an integer or a float of four or less components. Mono: Mono layer for single float attributes. UV: UV layer for float2 attributes. RGB: RGB layer for float3 attributes. RGBA: RGBA layer for float4 attributes. ID: ID layer for integer attributes.

entries.title: Bake Pre-Process
entries.summary: Sets up rays for baking, with a visualization state.

parameters.label: Normal Mode
parameters.description: The mode of the normals. Geometric Normal: Sets the normals to the incoming existing geometric normals. Smooth Normals: Promotes the normals to averaged point normals, then back to vertex again.

parameters.label: Override
parameters.description: Overrides any existing normals.

parameters.label: Missing Normals
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals. Message and Create Missing Normals: Produces a message if no normal attribute is present, but adds vertex normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Error if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces an error if no normal attribute is present. Warning if Low Res Mesh Missing Normals: Produces a warning if no normal attribute is present, but adds vertex normals weighted by vertex angle internally. Silently Create Missing Normals: Silently adds vertex normals weighted by vertex angle internally.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: Cusp Angle: When computing vertex normals, if normals of vertices around a single point are less than or equal to this angle (in degrees) apart from each other, they will be averaged together, weighted by the vertex angle in each polygon.

parameters.label: Weighting Method
parameters.description: Weighting Method: When set to By Vertex Angle, care is taken when computing normals to try to avoid issues introduced by sliver polygons and to weight contributions to normals by angle, so that triangulation won't change normals significantly. When set to Each Vertex Equally, a faster, but less accurate, approach similar to the approach used by the Facet SOP, is used to compute normals, where each vertex is given equal weight around a point, and less checks are done for ensuring stability. When set to By Face Area, the behavior is similar to Each Vertex Equally_, except that vertices on faces with more area will be given more weight when computing point normals. This is often used to fake the appearance of a smooth bevel for geometry with only a simple chamfer.

parameters.label: Soften Cage Group
parameters.description: The point or primitive group to which you apply softening.

parameters.label: Soften Cage
parameters.description: Facets the geometry in certain ways before applying the cage offset (Ray Start Offset). A soft cage isn't faceted and ensures a seamless result across sharp edges, but can cause projection errors and skewed detail as the normals are averaged. An unsoftened cage (which is faceted) can fix this projection skewing, but can cause missing detail capture on sharp edges.

parameters.label: Soften Mode
parameters.description: The method used to cut up the geometry. By Faces: Split the geometry across faces. By UV Seams: Split the geometry across UV Seams. Requires a UV attribute. By Edge Group: Split the geometry by a custom edge group.

parameters.label: Edge Group
parameters.description: The edge group by which to split the geometry.

parameters.label: Ray Start Offset
parameters.description: How far the duplicate mesh peaks out from the normals of the original low-resolution mesh. This is the ray start position or the 'Cage'.

parameters.label: Ray Start Mode
parameters.description: Uniform: No variable offset. Scale by Attribute: Scale the ray start offset by an attribute value, multiplied against the Ray Start Offset.

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute value by which to scale the Ray Start Offset.

parameters.label: Ray End Offset
parameters.description: How far the duplicate mesh peaks in from the normals of the original low-resolution mesh. This is the ray end position. This is turned into the raylength output attribute by calculating the distance difference between the Ray Start Offset and the Ray End Offset.

parameters.label: Ray End Mode
parameters.description: Uniform: No variable offset. Scale by Attribute: Scale the ray end offset by an attribute value, multiplied against the Ray End Offset. No End: Endless rays. Sets the raylength attribute to a value of -1, which the Bake Geometry Textures COP can recognize as endless rays.

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute value by which to scale the Ray End Offset.

parameters.label: Ray Start (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage output, which stores the Ray Start Positions.

parameters.label: Ray Direction (Vertex)
parameters.description: The vertex attribute that lives on the cage output, which stores the Ray Directions.

parameters.label: Ray Length (Point)
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the cage output, which stores the Ray Lengths.

inputs.label: low
inputs.description: A low-resolution geometry used to construct the cage geometry.

inputs.label: high
inputs.description: A high-resolution geometry used to compare with the cage geometry.

outputs.label: low
outputs.description: The low-resolution geometry with potentially modified normals based on parameter options.

outputs.label: high
outputs.description: The pure passthrough of the high-resolution geometry input.

outputs.label: cage
outputs.description: The cage geometry constructed from the low-resolution geometry, which contains attributes the Bake Geometry Textures COP can use.

entries.title: Bend
entries.summary: Curves images using handles or a captured region.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The method used that lets you bend the image. Corners: Use two tangent handles and one point handle at each corner of the image. Sides: Use a point handle at each corner of the image and the midpoint of each side. Angle: Use a set region to define which area of the image to bend.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Bottom Left
parameters.description: The position in image space of the lower-left corner.

parameters.label: Bottom Right
parameters.description: The position in image space of the lower-right corner.

parameters.label: Top Left
parameters.description: The position in image space of the upper-left corner.

parameters.label: Top Right
parameters.description: The position in image space of the upper-right corner.

parameters.label: Bottom Left U
parameters.description: The position in image space of the lower-left tangent handle in the U-direction.

parameters.label: Bottom Left V
parameters.description: The position in image space of the lower-left tangent handle in the V-direction.

parameters.label: Bottom Right U
parameters.description: The position in image space of the lower-right tangent handle in the U-direction.

parameters.label: Bottom Right V
parameters.description: The position in image space of the lower-right tangent handle in the V-direction.

parameters.label: Top Left U
parameters.description: The position in image space of the upper-left tangent handle in the U-direction.

parameters.label: Top Left V
parameters.description: The position in image space of the upper-left tangent handle in the V-direction.

parameters.label: Top Right U
parameters.description: The position in image space of the upper-right tangent handle in the U-direction.

parameters.label: Top Right V
parameters.description: The position in image space of the upper-right tangent handle in the V-direction.

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.description: The position in image space of the lower-side's midpoint. This handle adjusts the interpolation of the bending effect.

parameters.label: Top
parameters.description: The position in image space of the upper-side's midpoint. This handle adjusts the interpolation of the bending effect.

parameters.label: Left
parameters.description: The position in image space of the left-side's midpoint. This handle adjusts the interpolation of the bending effect.

parameters.label: Right
parameters.description: The position in image space of the right-side's midpoint. This handle adjusts the interpolation of the bending effect.

parameters.label: Bend Angle
parameters.description: The angle in degrees to bend the image.

parameters.label: Capture Origin
parameters.description: The center point of the source capture line (the Capture Direction).

parameters.label: Capture Direction
parameters.description: The normal of the line along which to apply the Bend Angle.

parameters.label: Capture Length
parameters.description: The length in image space of the Capture Direction's vector. Higher values result in a larger region of space that receives the partial transforms. NOTE: This value shouldn't be 0 because then there's nothing to bend.

parameters.label: Deform in Both Directions
parameters.description: Applies the Bend Angle in the direction opposite to the Capture Direction.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The source layer to bend.

outputs.label: bend
outputs.description: The layer with bending applied.
