entries.title: Configure Stamps
entries.summary: Creates stamp/sprite attributes on points with randomization controls and inputs.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed that determines how to generate each random value, such as random Scale, Angle or Color. Changing this value causes each parameter to generate a new random value, which results in a new pattern.

parameters.label: Jitter Layer Mask
parameters.description: Jitter Layer Mask: The amount of the jitter input's UV value to mix in with the Jitter value, which impacts the random position offset. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: Jitter: The amount of random position offset to add to each point's position on the grid.

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the random position offset for the created stamps.

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the scale input's mono value to mix in with the Scale value, which impacts the stamps' scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The stamp scale in image space.

parameters.label: Scale Mode
parameters.description: The method of post-processing to apply to the scale of stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Percent Variance: Apply random variance to the scale. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Scale.

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.description: Stretch Layer Mask: The amount of the stretch input's UV value to mix in with the Stretch X and Stretch Y values, which impacts the XY scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.description: Stretch Mode: The method of post-processing to apply to the non-uniform scale (stretch) of stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale of the X and Y-axes. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y.

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.description: Stretch X: The scale of the stamps along the X-axis that multiplies to the uniform scale.

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.description: Stretch Y: The scale of the stamps along the Y-axis that multiplies to the uniform scale.

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale of the X and Y-axes. This is applied as a post-process. If Stretch X is 1 and Percent Variance is 1, 0 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Stretch X to 2.0 * Stretch X.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.description: Angle Layer Mask: The amount of the angle input's mono value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the degree of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.description: Direction Layer Mask: The amount of the direction input's UV value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the direction of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Angle: The angle in degrees to rotate each stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the angle of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the angles. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values in degrees that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original angle.

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.description: Angle Variance: The amount of random variance to apply to the angles. This is applied as a post-process. For example, a value of 30 makes each stamp have a random offset between -30 degrees and 30 degrees.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: Min Value: The minimum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: Max Value: The maximum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Round To
parameters.description: Snaps all stamps to a specified angle. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Use Sort Layer
parameters.description: Enables the usage of the sort input which adds very small position offsets in the Z axis to control Depth Sorting on Stamp Points.

parameters.label: Color Seed
parameters.description: Color Seed: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp color and alpha.

parameters.label: Color Layer Mask
parameters.description: Color Layer Mask: The amount of the color input's RGB value to mix in with the Stamp Color value, which impacts the stamps' tint. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set how the color applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same color to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the hue, saturation, and value of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a color ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.description: Hue: The amount of random variance to apply to the hue. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 30 for example, the stamps randomly pick a hue offset from the range of 0 to 30.

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: Saturation: The amount of random variance to apply to the saturation. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a saturation from the range of 0 to 0.5.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: Value: The amount of random variance to apply to the value. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a value from the range of 0 to 0.5.

parameters.label: Alpha Layer Mask
parameters.description: Alpha Layer Mask: The amount of the alpha input's mono value to mix in with the Stamp Alpha value, which impacts the stamps' alpha. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stamp Alpha
parameters.description: Stamp Alpha: The amount of black (0) and white (1) by which to multiply the stamp's alpha. Use the dropdown menu to set how the alpha applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same amount of alpha to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the alpha of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a mono ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Alpha Variance
parameters.description: Alpha Variance: The amount of random variance to apply to the alpha. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Stamp Count
parameters.description: In order for the node to properly do stamp selection via the select input, it needs to know how many stamps there are in total. Placing down the Stamp Sprites recipe will link this parameter automatically to the attached Stamp Points Stamps

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Mode: The stamps to place in the image. When no stamps input is wired in, this parameter applies to the default star pattern. Cycle: Loop through all stamps in a repetitive cycle. Random: Randomly choose stamps based on the Select Seed. Layer Select: Use the select input to choose stamps. The parameter uses the first stamp when a pixel value is 0.0 and the last stamp when a pixel value is 1.0.

parameters.label: Select Seed
parameters.description: Select Seed: The seed value for random stamp selection.

inputs.label: points
inputs.description: Geometry containing points to setup attributes on.

inputs.label: jitter
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Jitter Layer Mask parameter and adds jitter offset to the created stamps.

inputs.label: direction
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Direction Layer Mask parameter and controls the direction of the created stamps' angles. For example, wire the Slope Direction COP into this input.

inputs.label: angle
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Angle Layer Mask parameter and rotates the stamps. A pixel value of 0 is 0 degrees and a pixel value of 1 is 360 degrees.

inputs.label: scale
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Scale Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the uniform scale of the stamps.

inputs.label: stretch
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Stretch Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the non-uniform scale of the stamps.

inputs.label: color
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Color Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the color of the stamps.

inputs.label: alpha
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Alpha Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the alpha of the stamps.

inputs.label: sort
inputs.description: An optional layer that controls Z offset for depth-based sorting.

inputs.label: select
inputs.description: An optional layer that, when Mode is set to Layer Sort, chooses which stamps to use. This chooses from either the stamps input or the default star pattern when there's no stamps input.

outputs.label: points
outputs.description: Geometry containing points with relevant Sprite/Stamp attributes.

parameters.label: Signature

parameters.label: Images per Line

parameters.label: Stack Vertically

parameters.label: Stack Horizontally

You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: How much contrast to apply. 1 will leave the image unchanged. Larger values will brighten light areas and darken dark areas, and lower values will do the opposite. 0 will cause all values to be the contrast center.

parameters.label: Contrast Center
parameters.description: The pivot around which contrast will occur.

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: Contrast and offset pair to apply to the red channel.

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: Contrast and offset pair to apply to the green channel.

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: Contrast and offset pair to apply to the blue channel.

parameters.label: Alpha

parameters.label: Clamp Below Zero
parameters.description: Black values will be pushed into negative values, but often negative light isn't reasonable, so this will clamp them at zero.

parameters.label: Clamp Above One
parameters.description: White areas can be pushed beyond one, which is reasonable for HDR images, but if applying contrast to a mask it may be desireable to limit the growth to 1.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: RGBA layers are often premultiplied, so using a fixed pivot that doesn't take the alpha into consideration will cause low coverage areas to be considered dark. This option will implicitly un-premultiply, contrast, and then pre-multiply, so the pivot works as expected.

entries.title: Convolve 3x3
entries.summary: Convolves a layer by a 3x3 kernel.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale all coefficients of the kernel. Use this value to set the normalization constant to make the kernel values integral. This value doesn't apply if Normalize Kernel is on. Use the following dimensions to additionally scale the coefficients by the distance between samples used for the convolution. The samples are the buffer elements in a 3x3 neighborhood around the currently processed buffer element. See /copernicus/spaces for more information about buffer space. (asterisk)1: Don't scale the coefficients. (asterisk)dX: Scale the coefficients by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width. /dX: Divide the coefficients by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width. NOTE: Use this value when building gradient kernels.

parameters.label: Top
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the (x-1, y+1), (x, y+1), and (x+1, y+1) pixels.

parameters.label: Middle
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the (x-1, y), (x, y), and (x+1, y) pixels.

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the (x-1, y-1), (x, y-1), and (x+1, y-1) pixels.

parameters.label: Normalize Kernel
parameters.description: Normalizes the kernel by the sum of all coefficients. This prevents the application of the kernel from brightening or darkening the image. The node doesn't normalize the kernel if the kernel sums to zero (for example, as it does when you use the Outline recipe).

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale all additive values. Use the following dimensions to additionally scale the additive values by the distance between samples used for the convolution. The samples are the buffer elements in a 3x3 neighborhood around the currently processed buffer element. See /copernicus/spaces for more information about buffer space. (asterisk)1: Don't scale the values. (asterisk)dX: Scale the values by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width. NOTE: Use this value when building distance fall-off kernels. /dX: Divide the values by the image space distance between horizontally adjacent samples. This is the buffer element width.

parameters.label: Top
parameters.description: The three values to add to the (x-1, y+1), (x, y+1), and (x+1, y+1) pixels.

parameters.label: Middle
parameters.description: The three values to add to the (x-1, y), (x, y), and (x+1, y) pixels.

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.description: The three values to add to the (x-1, y-1), (x, y-1), and (x+1, y-1) pixels.

parameters.label: Combine Operation
parameters.description: Mixes each active pixel in the 3x3 neighborhood together to create the output. This combination occurs after each pixel is scaled by the coefficent and has added additional values. This parameter considers only the Active Terms that are on. Add: Add the computed pixel values together. Multiply: Multiply the computed pixel values together. Maximum: Use the pixel value with the largest component out of all computed values. Minimum: Use the pixel value with the smallest component out of all computed values.

parameters.label: Active Terms
parameters.description: Controls which pixels in the 3x3 neighborhood are active and contribute to the final result. Terms you turn off aren't read from the input layer, which slightly increases performance. Off terms also don't contribute to the Combine Operation or have their weights included in the normalization.

parameters.label: Clamp Below Zero
parameters.description: Clamps final resulting values below zero to zero before mixing these pixel values into the original image.

parameters.label: Clamp Above One
parameters.description: Clamps final resulting values above one to one before mixing these pixel values into the original image.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Un-premultiplies the RGBA layers before applying the kernel, and then premultiplies the RGBA layers after applying the kernel. Turn this off when you blur the alpha and color (RGB) layers, because blur operations require premultiplied space. NOTE: RGBA layers are usually premultiplied, so applying edge detection to RGB channels reports edges where opacity varies. This lets kernels used for edge detection perform as if the image isn't premultiplied.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer to convolve.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: convolve
outputs.description: The convolved source layer.

entries.title: Convolve Filter
entries.summary: Convolves an image with an arbitrary kernel image using an FFT.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that this node convolves. The input and kernel images are both interpreted with this type. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Normalize Kernel
parameters.description: Divides the kernel by the sum of all its values before convolving, so the values total 1. This keeps the operation from brightening or darkening the image. Turn this off when the kernel is already normalized or when you want the kernel's absolute magnitude to scale the result.

parameters.label: Centered Kernel
parameters.description: Treats the center of the kernel image as its origin, so the convolution does not shift the result. When off, the origin is taken at the corner of the kernel image, which translates the output by half the kernel's size (the raw behavior of a frequency-space convolution).

parameters.label: Padding
parameters.description: When on, extends the image with a border of extra pixels before the transform and crops it back afterward; the value sets the fraction of the image size to add on each side. Because the FFT convolution is cyclic, the kernel otherwise wraps from one edge of the image to the opposite edge, and padding pushes those wrap-around artifacts outside the cropped region. Larger values suppress more wrap-around at the cost of a larger transform.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: How the padded region added around the image is filled. See Border types for more information. Unchanged: Use the filter's incoming border type. Constant: Fill the padded region with a constant value of 0. This is probably the option you want to use if the intent is to avoid tiling of the input kernel. Clamp: Repeat the edge pixels of the image outward. Mirror: Reflect the image across its edges into the padded region. Wrap: Tile the image into the padded region.

inputs.label: input
inputs.description: The image to convolve.

inputs.label: kernel
inputs.description: The kernel image to convolve the input against.

outputs.label: convolution
outputs.description: The convolved image.

entries.title: Copy and Transform
entries.summary: Copies stamps and applies transformations to the copies.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Total Number
parameters.description: The total number of copies to create. This includes the original geometry.

parameters.label: Order
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies the Translate, Rotate, and Scale values.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The location in world space to move the copies' origin to along the x and y axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount of rotation (in degrees) along the z-axis.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount in world space by which to multiply the copies' x and y axes, which compresses (lower values) and stretches (higher values) the copies.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the Scale parameter's x and y values.

parameters.label: Center Pivot on Shape
parameters.description: Centers the pivot point in the bounds of the input stamp. This is useful when your input stamp isn't in the center of the image.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The local pivot point of the copy. For example, if the shape's center point is -0.5x, set this parameter to -0.5 so the node acts like the point's in the center. To do this automatically, turn Center Pivot on Shape on. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Pivot Translate.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: The local pivot rotation (in degrees) of the copy, which rotates the pivot's local coordinate frame.

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together. Over: Render new copies over previous copies. The copies are presorted by their creation, which can be expensive. Under: Render new copies underneath previous copies. The copies are presorted by their creation, which can be expensive. Add: Add the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. Subtract: Subtract the original pixel value from the new overlapping stamp's pixel value. This method works better when you're not subtracting from zero. Multiply: Multiply the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. This method works better when the background starts at a non-zero value. Maximum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the maximum value. Minimum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the minimum value.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Wrap Mode
parameters.description: The wrapping behavior of the stamps. Auto: Wrap copies outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile when the size_ref input image's Border type is Wrap. Off: Don't wrap the stamps. On: Wrap copies outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile. This makes the main tile seamlessly repeat.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: When Wrap Mode is Auto or On, this is the size (in world space) of the region to wrap into. The resultant image periodically repeats in this size.

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp.

parameters.label: Change per Copy
parameters.description: A variable tint for the stamp, which can cause a color change for each copy. This is an additive, not a multiplier. For example, a change of R: 0.1, G: 0.2, B: 0.0 means that each copy becomes more red, but also becomes more green twice as fast.

parameters.label: Color Ramp
parameters.description: Applies a ramp over all copies and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's color. When on, this turns Change per Copy off. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Uniform Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of black (0) and white (1) by which to multiply the stamp's Background Alpha.

parameters.label: Change per Copy
parameters.description: A variable scale for the stamp, which can create an alpha change for each copy. This is an additive, not a multiplier.

parameters.label: Alpha Ramp
parameters.description: Applies a ramp over all copies and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's alpha. When on, this turns Change per Copy off. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The initial background color of the space around the stamps.

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.description: The initial background alpha of the space around the stamps.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: shape
inputs.description: The original layer that contains a stamp to copy and transform.

inputs.label: pointmask
inputs.description: An optional mask layer to select which copies stamp. A copy stamps if its location is in this mask, otherwise it doesn't stamp.

outputs.label: result
outputs.description: The layer with the resulting stamps applied.

outputs.label: id
outputs.description: The ID attribute of the stamp that contributed the most to this pixel or, if that attribute isn't present, the point number.

outputs.label: uv
outputs.description: The UV coordinates of the stamp that contributed the most to this pixel. This is in image space.

entries.title: Crop
entries.summary: Crops a layer to a new size.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Cropping can be seen as cutting out part of an image, throwing out the extra, but leaving it in the same location of your work space. But it can also be seen as a pan & zoom to reframe the desired region to now fit the center of your workspace. Discard Cropped: The cropped region is discarded and the pixels remain unchanged in their location in image space. Discard and Reframe to Crop: The cropped region is discarded, but the pixels that remain are reframed to fill image spaces. Reframe to Crop: The data is unaffected by the crop. Instead, the image is reframed so the cropped range fits the display window. This will appear to have no effect in the 2D viewport.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: Override the border values used when un-cropping an image. Unchanged: Use the input border type. Constant: Treat the border as zero, with the boundary interpolating to black. Clamp: Clamp boundary values, streaking them outwards. Mirror: Reflect along the boundaries. Wrap: Wrap to the opposite boundary. Clip: Define an implicit cut off at the boundary without any bleeding of black values.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Controls how to specify the crop. This controls the range of the values and if they are in respect to the input's display or data window. Image: The cropping region is specified in terms of the display window, with -1 to 1 being the range. A square size will result in a square crop. Texture: The cropping region is specified in terms of the data window, with 0 to 1 being the range. A square size is not necessarily a square crop because the source may not be square. Pixels: The cropping region is specified in pixels directly. NOTE: The cropping is always done in pixels, which may result in rounding if they do not correspond to buffer elements due to the use of pixel scale.

parameters.label: Geometry Units
parameters.description: If a geometry input is used to drive the crop, this controls what the units of the geometry are. Image: The geometry specifies image coordinates, ranging -1 to 1, that are relative to the display window. Texture: The geometry specifies texture coordinates, ranging 0 to 1, that are relative to the data window. Pixels: The geometry specifies pixel coordinates, ranging 0 to resolution. World: The geometry specifies world coordinates. The resulting crop region will respect the 3D transform that the input layer has.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to specify the crop region. Lower Left and Upper Right: Specify the lower-left and upper-right corners of the crop. Lower Left and Size: Specify the lower-left corner and size of the crop.

parameters.label: Lower Left
parameters.description: The lower-left of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Upper Right
parameters.description: The upper-right of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: Adjust the final crop values to have this aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Extract Tile
parameters.description: Divide the cropped region into equal sized tiles, and crop to one of the tiles. Pixel padding is done after the tile determination, so can be used to ensure there is a buffer around the tiles.

parameters.label: Tile Counts
parameters.description: Number of tiles to divide the image into in each axis.

parameters.label: Tile Number
parameters.description: The tile number to extract, starting with 0 at the bottom left and increasing to the right.

parameters.label: Minimum Resolution
parameters.description: The cropped region will be increased to include at least this number of pixels.

parameters.label: Limit Resolution
parameters.description: Lets you set a Maximum Resolution to limit the size.

parameters.label: Maximum Resolution
parameters.description: The cropped region will be clamped to at most this size. This is useful for dynamic cropping to avoid unexpected input from creating overly large textures.

parameters.label: Reset Pixel Origin
parameters.description: Adjusts the pixel coordinates to match the display window. This is useful when reframing the display window, because the location of the (0, 0) pixel may no longer refer to the corner of the display window. This makes pixel coordinates appear to be offset, which can cause confusion if this was unintended.

parameters.label: Left/Right
parameters.description: Additional pixels to pad the cropped image on the left and right.

parameters.label: Top/Bottom
parameters.description: Additional pixels to pad the cropped image on the top and bottom.

inputs.description: A layer to crop.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: bounds
inputs.description: A reference geometry to use for cropping dimensions.

outputs.label: crop
outputs.description: The cropped image.

entries.title: Crystal Noise
entries.summary: Generates a sharp and angular Worley noise type.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source outputs. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. You can use a Clamp COP to enforce the range afterwards.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the noise more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Primary Metric
parameters.description: The distance metric of the internal Worley noises. When Secondary is on, this controls only the first Worley noise. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in jagged shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in jagged diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. entries.title: Curl
entries.summary: Computes the curl of a vector field.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space to compute the curl in. This affects the magnitude of the result. The result may also be affected by anisotropic scaling in the selected space. Image: Compute the curl in Image Space, by normalizing the change in values by the image-space pixel size. Pixel: Compute the curl in Pixel Space, by normalizing the change in values by the pixel size. Local: Compute the curl in Local Space, by normalizing the change in values by the world-space pixel size.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the computed curl by this amount.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivatives used for the curl. A derivative is often computed with adjacent pixels or voxels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives. Increasing this value may remove stepping artifacts from the result.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Determines if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range. Turning this parameter on is useful when building seamless textures with a wrap border type. Turn this off if you want to avoid artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in a clamp border type, as it acts like an extrapolation.

inputs.label: v
inputs.description: The UV layer or Vector VDB that stores the vector field from which to compute the curl.

outputs.label: result
outputs.description: The computed curl. For UV inputs, this is a mono layer. For Vector VDB inputs, this is a Vector VDB.

entries.title: Curvature
entries.summary: Computes the curvature of a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space used to measure the layer's curvature.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to calculate the layer's curvature. Finite Difference: Compute the difference between the current pixel value and its neighboring values. This uses classic definitions of curvature based on derivative values. This method is more stable than Angle Deficit for smooth inputs, such as a parameterization of hemisphere. Angle Deficit: Treat each pixel as a vertex in a polygonal height field. This calculates the sum of the angles formed at each pixel by its neighboring vertices. The angle sum equals 2𝜋 in flat regions, but the sum is less in curved areas and results in an angle deficit that's used to estimate local curvature. This method performs more robustly when the input includes complex or non-uniform variations.

parameters.label: Curvature Type
parameters.description: The curvature type from the input layer to compute. Gaussian: This curvature is positive in both convex and concave regions. It becomes negative at saddle points, where the surface curves in opposite directions (concave in one direction and convex in the other). Gaussian curvature is useful for distinguishing simple convex and concave shapes from regions with saddle-like geometry. Mean: This curvature is positive in convex regions and negative in concave regions. Mean curvature is useful for distinguishing convex, concave, and flat regions. Principal (max): The maximal principal curvature represents the largest normal curvature at a point. Although it's not a direct measure of convexity, it often emphasizes geometrically prominent, outward-curving features. Principal (min): The minimal principal curvature represents the smallest normal curvature at a point. Although it's not a direct measure of concavity, it often emphasizes geometrically recessed, inward-curving features.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The values from the layer's computed Curvature Type to output. Curvature: Outputs the entire computed curvature. Convexity: Outputs the convex regions based on the selected curvature. Concavity: Outputs the concave regions based on the selected curvature.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: When a normal vector field is generated by the Height to Normal COP, its type must be set to match that node. See /copernicus/normals for more information. Signed: Output signed normals, compatible with geometry attributes. Offset: Output offset normals, compatible with normal maps.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Adjusts the scale of the input's pixel values.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Adds contributions from pixels outside of the image to compute curvature at the image boundaries. This depends on the border type, which determines what pixels to read as outside of the image. If the boundary uses wrapping, the result is correct. If the boundary is constant, turn this parameter off to produce correct values near the edges.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The scale of the neighborhood that the node considers for curvature computation at each pixel. A larger neighborhood often yields smoother curvature results.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Adjusts the scale of the output's pixel values.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.description: Normalizes the output result, which makes the output values stay in the 0 to 1 range. Since minor variations between neighboring pixels can result in unexpectedly high curvature values, this improves visualization by revealing the full curvature structure.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.description: The minimum value to clamp the curvature value to.

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.description: The maximum value to clamp the curvature value to.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The mono layer that represents a height field or the RGB layer that represents a normal field.

outputs.label: curvature
outputs.description: The layer that stores the curvature values.

entries.title: Curve 3D
entries.summary: Lets you interactively draw Bézier curves using tools similar to 2D illustration programs, as well as polylines and NURBS.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: Type of curve primitives to create. Polygon: Create a polyline. NURBS Curve: Create a NURBS curve. Bezier Curve: Create a Bézier curve.

parameters.label: Order
parameters.description: The order of the NURBS or Bézier curve. Higher order curves give more control vertices and smoother curve interpolation between on-curve knots. However, you should generally use the default order (4) unless you have a reason for needing higher-order curves. Note that changing the Order changes the interpretation of all existing curves to use the new order value. The drawing mode is optimized for cubic Bézier curves (Order set to 4, the default). For higher-order Bézier curves, the drawing interface is the same as for cubic Bézier curves, but after you drag out the tangent handles, the node creates _more than one_ tangent handle on the trailing side of the point. It creates the extra control points in line, so they have the same shape as a cubic Bézier would, but after you're finished drawing you can use the Edit mode to move the extra control points independently. For NURBS, the drawing interface is always the same: placing points by clicking.

parameters.label: Reinterpret Curves as Current Type and Order
parameters.description: When on, all existing curves are converted by reinterpretting the curve points as the current Primitive Type and Order. When converting curves to NURBs or Bezier, the last point on the curve may be repeated to fully define the curve. When off, only newly created curves are given the current Primitive Type and Order.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The mode that the tool is currently in. Select/Edit Mode: Modifies existing curves. Draw Mode: Puts down new points. Auto-Bezier Draw Mode: Put down new points when creating Bezier curves. Points are created as Auto Points. Tangents are optimized to create a bezier curve continuous in the first and second derivatives. Previous points are optimized until it either reaches back to the start of the curve, or a non-auto point. Orient Mode: Create an orient attribute along curves by specifying target up vectors at specified anchor points.

parameters.label: Delete Selected Points
parameters.description: Removes the selected point(s), if any.

parameters.label: Join Selected Points
parameters.description: Joins two selected vertices together into a single vertex. If the two selected vertices are on the same curve, the result is one closed curve. If the vertices are from different curves, the result is one curve instead of two.

parameters.label: Cut Curves at Selected Points
parameters.description: Cuts the curve at each selected point. After the cut, each selected point becomes an end point. Any branches are also split prior to cutting curve vertices.

parameters.label: Add Segment Between Selected Endpoints
parameters.description: Joins the two selected vertices with a straight line. If the two selected vertices are on the same curve, the result is one closed curve. If the vertices are from different curves, the result is one curve instead of two, with a segment added between the end vertices.

parameters.label: Delete Segments Between Selected Points
parameters.description: Removes any selected segments, possibly splitting curves around selected segments.

parameters.label: Fuse Branch
parameters.description: Fuse all selected points into a single branch point containing all the vertices from the selected points.

parameters.label: Split Branch
parameters.description: Split the selected branch points to create separate points for each vertex of the branched point.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Corner
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a corner point.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Smooth
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a smooth point, possibly snapping handles to be aligned.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Balanced
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a balanced point, possibly snapping handles to be aligned.

parameters.label: Retract Tangents at Selected Points
parameters.description: Collapses the bezier handles down into a sharp bezier corner point.

parameters.label: Expand Tangents at Selected Points
parameters.description: Expands out the bezier handles to be intractable, if the selected point is collapsed.

parameters.label: Make Segments Between Selected Points Straight
parameters.description: Collapses the handles on the ends of the selected segments, converting the segment into a straight line.

parameters.label: Close Selected Curves
parameters.description: Closes all curves with at least one point selected.

parameters.label: Create Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Turns the selected corner points into rounded corners.

parameters.label: Remove Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Turns the selected rounded corners into ordinary corners.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Auto
parameters.description: Makes selected points into auto points. Bezier curves are automatically computed to interpolate any auto points.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Manual
parameters.description: Makes selected auto points into non-auto points and freezes the local interpolated curve so that it can be manually edited.

parameters.label: Reverse
parameters.description: Reverse selected curves.

parameters.label: Reset Operations
parameters.description: Resets all modeling operations that have been done. Resets the output geometry to the input geometry.

parameters.label: Snap Tangents when Fusing Ends in Draw Mode
parameters.description: Whether to snap the final tangent when fusing curves together or closing curves by clicking on the end point of another curve or the opposite end point of the same curve. Dragging out the tangent while fusing doesn't snap the tangents.

parameters.label: Approximate Shape on Delete
parameters.description: Approximates the previous curve shape on a point delete.

parameters.label: Approximate End Tangents
parameters.description: Prioritizes keeping the end derivatives of a segment when approximating the previous curve shape on a point delete.

parameters.label: Soft Transform Radius
parameters.description: The soft transform radius when soft transforms are on. Soft transforms are used when doing operations that manually move anchor points, including dragging points in edit and draw mode, dragging segments in polygons or NURBs curves, or bezier segments adjacent to rounded corners or auto points. This radius is relative to the distance along the backbone polygon of the given curve. For Polygons this is equivalent to the surface distance along the curve. For NURBS Curves this is equivalent to the distance along the control polygon of the curve. And for Bezier Curves, this is equivalent to the distance along the polygon that results from reinterpreting the curve as a polygon. In particular, in this polygon, auto points and rounded corners are collapsed to a single point, which can result in distances along the curve being slightly different than expected when looking at a curve.

parameters.label: Corner Points Group
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the corner points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the corner points from this node.

parameters.label: Smooth Points Group
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the smooth points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the smooth points from this node.

parameters.label: Auto Points Group
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the auto points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the auto points from this node.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name to place in the name attribute on all created geometry. Defaults to the name of the SOP ($OS).

parameters.label: X Axis
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the X Axis of the orientations created on points in the Orient Mode. When active, geometry showing the x axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.

parameters.label: Y Axis
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the Y Axis of the orientations created on points in the Orient Mode. When active, geometry showing the y axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.

parameters.label: Z Axis
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the Z Axis of the orientations created on points in the Orient Mode. When active, geometry showing the x axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.

parameters.label: Orient
parameters.description: The name of the orient attribute to create. The orient attribute created in the Orient Mode is stored in this attribute. When active, guide geometry showing the orient attribute is present in the viewport. In the state parameters, you can toggle drawing the orient guide geometry, as well as control the density and scale of guide gnomons.

parameters.label: Tangent Type
parameters.description: The method used to determine the implicit curve tangent. This tangent is used to parallel transport the orient attributes from the target points along the curves.

parameters.label: Align with Curve Tangent
parameters.description: When on, aligns orient attribute values with the curve tangent. When off, orient attribute values on target points are aligned with the value in Tangent.

parameters.label: Target Orientations
parameters.description: The target orientations specified on points along curves. When determining the orient attribute, these target orientations are placed on curves, and a parallel transport is used between target points to create an orient attribute that smoothly blends between target orientations. For any curves that do not have any target orientations, a default orient is placed on the first point of the curve, achieved by rotating the vector (0,0,1) onto the curve tangent.

parameters.label: Enable Target Orientation
parameters.description: Toggles this target orientation.

parameters.label: Point
parameters.description: The point to place the target orientation on.

parameters.label: Up
parameters.description: The target up vector. Target up vectors are made perpendicular to the curve tangent if Align with Curve Tangent is on, and are otherwise made perpendicular to the specified Tangent vector.

parameters.label: Tangent
parameters.description: The target tangent vector. When Align with Curve Tangent is off, this parameter is available to set alongside the Up vector, allowing you to fully specify the orientation of this target Point, without being constrained by the curve tangent.

parameters.label: Active Points
parameters.description: Points used in the current operation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The amount to translate the selected points or the selected handle end point by.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount to rotate (in degrees) the selected points with respect to the pivot.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the selected points with respect to the pivot.

parameters.label: Corner Points
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the corner points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through Corner Points Group, to pick up the corner points from previous nodes.

parameters.label: Smooth Points
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the smooth points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through Smooth Points Group, to pick up the smooth points from previous nodes.

parameters.label: Auto Points
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the auto points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through Auto Points Group, to pick up the auto points from previous nodes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.description: The position of the pivot, before any further translations.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.description: Specifies the axis to align the transform handle with. Upon finishing any operation with the transform handle, it snaps back to this rotation to begin a new edit. Is specified as three angles in degrees representing the amount to rotate around each axis.

parameters.label: Fixed Pivot
parameters.description: Whether to keep the pivot position the same when selecting new points. If off, the pivot resets to the center of the bounding box of the selected points on a selection change.

parameters.label: View Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Whether to view rounded corners. When off, rounded corners are all shown with a radius of 0.0. The topology of created curves is not changed when this toggle is off.

parameters.label: Round Corner Points
parameters.description: A string parameter encoding the rounded corners and their radii.

parameters.label: Round Corner Radius
parameters.description: Sets the radius of the selected rounded corners.

parameters.label: Bake Selected Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Convert selected rounded corners into regular bezier segments.

parameters.label: Show Rounded Corner Widget
parameters.description: Whether to show a widget to modify rounded corner radii.

parameters.label: Show Rounded Corner Labels
parameters.description: Whether to show labels for the radii on the rounded corner widgets. These labels are off if Show Rounded Corner Widget is off.

outputs.label: curves
outputs.description: The set of curve primitives. Set its type with the Primitive Type parameter.

entries.title: Curve Animate 3D
entries.summary: Lets you interactively draw and animate Bézier curves using tools similar to 2D illustration programs, as well as polylines and NURBS.
entries.overview: This node's interactive state lets you draw and edit cubic Bézier curves using tools similar to 2D illustration programs like Illustrator, Sketch, and InkScape. This is useful for drawing artistic curves by hand. For example, tracing images, drawing logos, drawing profile curves to extrude, and revolve. Image:/images/nodes/sop/curve_bezier.jpg This node also includes an Auto-Bézier point type, similar to Illustrator's Curvature tool, which lets you guide a curve by placing edit points without having to worry about tangents. Image:/images/nodes/sop/curve_auto.jpg You can also draw polylines, non-cubic orders of Bézier curves, and NURBS. However, when you are drawing these other types, you click to place each point and Houdini interprets the point according to the curve type, without the special support for drawing tangents you get when drawing cubic Bézier curves. :col: Image:/images/nodes/sop/curve_nurbs.jpg :col: Image:/images/nodes/sop/curve_polyline.jpg

parameters.label: Stashed Geometry
parameters.description: A geometry data parameter storing the current curve geometry and animation.

parameters.label: Reset All Changes

parameters.description: The plane that points are placed on and drags are computed with respect to. Axis Aligned: Use the XY, YZ, or XZ plane that is most orthogonal to the view direction. View Plane: Use the plane normal to the view direction.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: The type of primitive to create when creating new curves in draw mode.

entries.title: Scatter on Curves
entries.summary: Scatters input stamps along an input curve using randomization controls.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the node outputs. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.description: The distribution mode for how to scatter the stamps along the curve. Distance: Scatter stamps equidistant from each other based on a set distance. Scatter: Scatter stamps randomly based on a density input or the Max Count. By Count: Scatter stamps randomly based on a specific count.

parameters.label: Segment Length
parameters.description: When Distribution is Distance, this is the maximum segment length of resulting edges.

parameters.label: Maximum Segments
parameters.description: When Distribution is Distance, this is the maximum number of edges.

parameters.label: Treat Input Curve As
parameters.description: How to inteprolate the input curves. Straight: Directly interpolate maintaining the straight lines. Subdivision: Smooth the curves with a subdivision approach. This will not interpolate the original points. Interpolating: Smooth the curves with a bicubic approach, this will interpolate the original points but oscillate.

parameters.label: Density Layer Mask
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter, this is the amount of the density input's mono value to mix in with the Density value. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter, this is the amount to scale the density of the points. This parameter doesn't apply when Max Count is on.

parameters.label: Max Count
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter or By Count, this is the amount of points to generate.

parameters.label: Relaxation
parameters.description: When Distribution is Scatter or By Count, this relaxes points by pushing them away from each other to avoid clumping. More relaxation iterations result in further separation between the points. Relaxation is done gradually to avoid chaotic behavior and allow control over how much relaxation takes place.

parameters.label: Scatter Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for all randomization that deals with stamp placement. This includes jitter, density, angle and direction, scale, and stretch.

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the scale input's mono value to mix in with the Scale value, which impacts the stamps' scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps in image space. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the scale of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Scale.

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale. This is applied as a post-process. If Scale is 1 and Scale Variance 1 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Scale to 2.0 * Scale.

parameters.label: Min Scale
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Scale
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Scale. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Apply Scale along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Cut Curves by Relative Arc Length
parameters.description: Solves for the actual location halfway along the curve as measured by distance. This is useful since curves have a parameterization that doesn't match the actual distance along the curve. For example, a curve of 0.5 isn't halfway along the curve but halfway along its parameterization.

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.description: The start point in image space of the curve.

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.description: The end point in image space of the curve.

parameters.label: Smoothing
parameters.description: The amount of smoothing to apply to the curve.

parameters.label: Mirror Stamps
parameters.description: Creates a mirrored version of the stamps on the other side of the curve. Use the dropdown menu to set the mirror's behavior. Treat Independently: Apply randomization and scattering separately. NOTE: This mode's angle mirroring isn't done as a post-process, so any randomization breaks the mirroring of the angle across the curve. Use Values from Original: Takes the mirrored curve and copies all values and looks from the original to the mirrored copy. This occurs after the randomization and scattering. Use Values from Mirrored Copy: Takes the original curve and copies all values and looks from the mirrored to the original copy. This occurs after the randomization and scattering.

parameters.label: From Curve
parameters.description: The amount to perpendicularly offset the stamps from the tangent of the curve.

parameters.label: Mirrored From Curve
parameters.description: The amount to perpendicularly offset the mirrored stamps from the tangent of the curve.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random position offset to add to each stamp's position on the grid.

parameters.label: Offset along Curve
parameters.description: The amount to offset the stamp placement along the curve.

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the angle input's mono value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the degree of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value. NOTE: For the stamp input, the incoming stamp's upward direction is taken as its forward position and points along the curve in default behavior. The following example shows this behavior using an upward facing arrow as the stamp input. :fig: Image:/images/nodes/cop/curve_scatter_anglelayer.jpg #display: half

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the direction input's UV value to mix in with the Angle value, which impacts the direction of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Angles Relative to Curve Direction
parameters.description: Accounts for the curve's usual direction when calculating the angle.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle in degrees to rotate each stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the angle of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the angles. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values in degrees that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original angle.

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the angles. This is applied as a post-process. For example, a value of 30 makes each stamp have a random offset between -30 degrees and 30 degrees.

parameters.label: Min Angle
parameters.description: The minimum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Angle
parameters.description: The maximum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Angle. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Increment per Stamp
parameters.description: The amount of angle increase for each stamp along the curve. For example, if Increment per Stamp is 10 and your curve has 36 points, each stamp progressively rotates more and the end stamp makes a full rotation.

parameters.label: Round to Multiples
parameters.description: Snaps all stamps to a specified angle. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the stretch input's UV value to mix in with the Stretch X and Stretch Y values, which impacts the XY scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.description: The method of post-processing that applies to the non-uniform scale (stretch) of the stamps. Uniform: No post-processing. Variance: Apply random variance to the scale of the X and Y-axes. Min/Max: The minimum and maximum range of values that each stamp randomly picks from, and then multiplies against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y.

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the X-axis in image space.

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the Y-axis in image space.

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale of the X and Y-axes. This is applied as a post-process. If Stretch X is 1, Stretch Y is 0, and Stretch Variance is 1, 0 for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from 0.5 * Stretch x to 2.0 * Stretch x.

parameters.label: Min Stretch
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Stretch
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original Stretch X and Stretch Y. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Stretch along Curve
parameters.description: Applies two ramps along the curve to scale stamps along the X and Y-axes.

parameters.label: Stretch X along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale along the X-axis. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Stretch Y along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale along the Y-axis. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together. Depth-Sorted Over: Presort the points by their depth. The node renders the farthest points first, so closer points paint over them. This option can be expensive since it requires sorting. Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over: Apply a non-linear weighting that approximates depth-sorting without the need for sorting. Add: Add the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. Subtract: Subtract the original pixel value from the new overlapping stamp's pixel value. This method works better when you're not subtracting from zero. Multiply: Multiply the overlapping pixel values of the stamps together. This method works better when the background starts at a non-zero value. Maximum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the maximum value. Minimum: Compare the stamps along with the background color and use the minimum value.

parameters.label: Use Sort Layer
parameters.description: Multiply the Depth-Sorted Over or Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over sort values by the sort input's value.

parameters.label: Apply Sort along Curve
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve to sort the stamps. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Color Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp color and alpha.

parameters.label: Color Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the color input's RGB value to mix in with the Stamp Color value, which impacts the stamps' tint. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set how the color applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same color to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the hue, saturation, and value of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a color ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information. Ramp along Curve: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's color. The curve of the ramp determines which colors apply to the stamps. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the hue. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 30 for example, the stamps randomly pick a hue offset from the range of 0 to 30.

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the saturation. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a saturation from the range of 0 to 0.5.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the value. This is applied as a post-process. If set to 0.5 for example, the stamps randomly pick a value from the range of 0 to 0.5.

parameters.label: Alpha Layer Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the alpha input's mono value to mix in with the Stamp Alpha value, which impacts the stamps' alpha. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stamp Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of black (0) and white (1) by which to multiply the stamp's alpha. Use the dropdown menu to set how the alpha applies to the stamps. Uniform: Apply the same amount of alpha to each stamp. Variance: Apply random variance to the alpha of the stamps. Random from Ramp: Pick randomly from a mono ramp. See Ramp parameters for more information. Ramp along Curve: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's alpha. The curve of the ramp determines how much alpha applies to the stamps. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Alpha Variance
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the alpha. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The initial background color of the space around the stamps.

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.description: The initial background alpha of the space around the stamps.

parameters.label: Selection Mode
parameters.description: The stamps to place in the image. When no stamps input is wired in, this parameter applies to the default star pattern. Cycle: Loop through all stamps in a repetitive cycle. Random: Randomly choose stamps based on the Select Seed. Layer Select: Use the select input to choose stamps. The parameter uses the first stamp when a pixel value is 0.0 and the last stamp when a pixel value is 1.0.

parameters.label: Limit Selection
parameters.description: Limits the maximum number of stamps that the node uses.

parameters.label: Select Seed
parameters.description: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp selection.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Wrap Mode
parameters.description: The wrapping behavior of the stamps. Auto: Wrap points outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile when the size_ref input image's Border type is Wrap. Off: Don't wrap the stamps. On: Wrap points outside of the main tile (whose size is controlled by Tile Size) back into the tile. This makes the main tile seamlessly repeat.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: When Wrap Mode is Auto or On, this is the size (in image space) of the region to wrap into. The resultant image periodically repeats in this size.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: curve
inputs.description: The curve along which to scatter stamps. NOTE: You must wire in a curve input to use this node.

inputs.label: density
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Density Layer Mask parameter and performs rejection sampling on the created stamps.

inputs.label: direction
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Direction Layer Mask parameter and controls the direction of the created stamps' angles. For example, wire the Slope Direction COP into this input.

inputs.label: angle
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Angle Layer Mask parameter and rotates the stamps. A pixel value of 0 is 0 degrees and a pixel value of 1 is 360 degrees.

inputs.label: scale
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Scale Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the uniform scale of the stamps.

inputs.label: stretch
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Stretch Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the non-uniform scale of the stamps.

inputs.label: color
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Color Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the color of the stamps.

inputs.label: alpha
inputs.description: An optional layer that's scaled by the Alpha Layer Mask parameter and multiplies the alpha of the stamps.

inputs.label: sort
inputs.description: An optional layer that controls depth-based sorting.

inputs.label: select
inputs.description: An optional layer that, when Selection Mode is set to Layer Select, chooses which stamps to use. This chooses from either the stamps input or the default star pattern when there's no stamps input.

inputs.label: stamps
inputs.description: An optional layer that provides stamps. Wire in a cable to use up to 8 stamps.

outputs.label: result
outputs.description: The layer with the stamping applied.

outputs.label: id
outputs.description: The ID attribute of the stamp that contributed the most to this pixel or, if that attribute isn't present, the point number.

outputs.label: uv
outputs.description: The UV coordinates of the stamp that contributed the most to this pixel. This is in image space.

entries.title: Defocus
entries.summary: Defocuses an input layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.description: The focal length (zoom) of the camera.

parameters.label: Focus Distance
parameters.description: The distance from the camera at which objects are in focus. Objects outside of this distance are blurred. TIP: Enter the viewer state and click on the area of the layer you'd like to be in focus.

parameters.label: F-Stop
parameters.description: The F-Stop of the camera. The f-stop determines the blurriness of the defocus.

parameters.label: Focus Plane Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the focus mask to smooth the transition between in and out of focus. NOTE: The focus mask is a mono layer that determines what areas of the image are in or out of focus.

parameters.label: Focus Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the focus mask. See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The maximum radius (in pixels) of the bokeh effect for out of focus areas. This can be expensive for a large radius since a lot of scattering is done.

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The aperture mask is normalized so the bokeh doesn't change the total brightness, but it can be useful to boost the result to gain or lose total luminance.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: The resolution to resample the aperture layer to, which speeds up filtering of the aperture layer.

parameters.label: Resample Input
parameters.description: The amount to resample the input layer before computing the bokeh layer. This speeds up computing at the slight cost of quality.

parameters.label: Color Correct
parameters.description: Applies color correction on the image's out of focus areas.

parameters.label: Brightness threshold
parameters.description: The threshold that a pixel's luminance value must be above for the pixel to brighten.

parameters.label: Brightness Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the brightness mask, which smooths the transition between pixels in and out of the threshold.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: The amount to brighten the pixels within the Brightness threshold.

parameters.label: Saturation Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold that a pixel's luminance value must be above for the pixel to desaturate.

parameters.label: Saturation Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the saturation mask, which smooths the transition between pixels in and out of the threshold.

parameters.label: Saturation Scale
parameters.description: The amount to desaturate the pixels within the Saturation Threshold. Bright pixels tend to be slightly desaturated.

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The gamma of the out of focus areas.

parameters.label: Depth Blend
parameters.description: Applies depth to blend the original layer with the out of focus layer.

parameters.label: Min
parameters.description: The amount to remap the minimum depth of the mask that blends the original layer with the out of focus layer.

parameters.label: Max
parameters.description: The amount to remap the maximum depth of the mask that blends the original layer with the out of focus layer.

inputs.label: bokeh
inputs.description: An optional mono mask that provides the shape to spread pixels into. For example, a white star causes the bokeh to appear star-like. If not provided, a circular bokeh is used.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.
