entries.title: Fractal Sample
entries.summary: Generates a fractal of the source input that you can randomize.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Maintain Tileable
parameters.description: Clamps or rounds certain parameter values so they maintain tileability. For example, Lacunarity clamps to integers and Angle rounds to 90 degrees. NOTE: This parameter doesn't create tileability. The original source input must tile in order for this option to maintain tileability.

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The amount of times to scale add together the octaves.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the octave for each iteration, which is rounded to an integer value if Maintain Tileable is enabled.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive octave.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: In order to keep results 0 centered, this parameter can be used to select your midpoint which will be subtracted from each sample inside the fractal loop.

parameters.label: Offset with Bias
parameters.description: After the main sample is done and adjusted internally by weight and gain, you can then offset the output value by the same bias value, which will offset your output range. This is especially useful in Maximum blend mode, where your base value is very high up.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: The method used to combine the octaves. Max Octaves determines the amount of octaves. Add: Adds each octave onto the next. Subtract: Subtracts each octave from the next. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the preceeding octave and the following octave. Over: Places the preceeding octave over the following octave. This mode is only valid when the input is RGBA.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filtering method used for sampling the source layer. Consider using one of the area filters (Box and later) if the distortion shrinks large regions and you notice noise. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed that determines how to generate each Jitter, Angle (when Random), and Random Flip X/Y. Changing this value causes each parameter to generate a new random value, which results in a new pattern.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount in image space of random position offset to add to each octave.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle in degrees to rotate each octave. Use the dropdown menu to set how the angle applies to the octaves. Per Octave: Each octave gets an increment of the Angle. If Angle is set to 30 degrees for example, the third octave has 90 degrees applied. Random: Each octave has a random angle chosen from within the range of the Angle. If Angle is set to 30 degrees for example, each octave has a random rotation between -30 and 30 degrees.

parameters.label: Random Flip X
parameters.description: Randomly flips each octave on the X-axis.

parameters.label: Random Flip Y
parameters.description: Randomly flips each octave on the Y-axis.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.

parameters.label: Complement

parameters.label: Bias

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg

parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.

entries.title: Function
entries.summary: Applies a mathematical function to a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the incoming layer.

parameters.label: Shift
parameters.description: The amount to add to the incoming layer after it's been multiplied by the Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Function Class
parameters.description: The functions to expose in this node. Arithmetic: Expose simple mathematical operations. Powers: Expose exponential and logarithmic functions. Trigonometry: Expose trigonometric and hyperbolic functions.

parameters.label: Arithmetic
parameters.description: When Function Class is Arithmetic, this is the mathematical operation to use. Absolute: Returns the absolute value of each channel. Sign: Returns the sign of each channel. Negative values return -1, 0 values return 0, and positive values return 1. Normalize: Normalizes the input layer by dividing each channel by the magnitude of the incoming vector. Negate: Negates each channel, which multiplies them by -1. Reciprocal: Returns the reciprocal of each channel, which divides a value of 1 by the channel's value. Floor: Returns the largest integer that is less than or equal to the channel's value. Round: Rounds each channel to the closest integer. Ceil: Returns the smallest integer that's greater than or equal to the channel's value. Modulus: Returns the fractional part of each channel's values.

parameters.label: Power
parameters.description: When Function Class is Powers, this is the exponential or logarithmic function to use. Square Root: Returns the square root of each channel. pow(x, E): Raises each channel to the power of the Exponent value. pow(b, x): Raises the Base value to the power of the channel's value. exp(x): Raises e (2.17128128) to the power of each channel's value. Base-Log: Returns the logarithm of each channel with respect to the Base value. Natural Log: Returns the natural logarithm of each channel (for base e).

parameters.label: Trigonometry
parameters.description: When Function Class is Trigonometry, this is the trigonometric or hyperbolic function to use. Sin: Returns the sine of each channel. Cos: Returns the cosine of each channel. Tan: Returns the tangent of each channel. Arc Sin: Returns the arc sine of each channel. Arc Cos: Returns the arc cosine of each channel. Arc Tan: Returns the arc tangent of each channel. To get the equivalent of atan2(), the UV to Polar COP node can be used. Hyperbolic Sin: Returns the hyperbolic sine of each channel. Hyperbolic Cos: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of each channel. Hyperbolic Tan: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of each channel.

parameters.label: Base
parameters.description: When Arithmetic is Modulus or Power is pow(b, x) or Base-Log, this is the base to use.

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.description: When Power is pow(x, E), this is the exponent to use.

parameters.label: Angle Units
parameters.description: When Function Class is Trigonometry, this is the unit to use for the trigonometric function. Radians: Interpret the pixel values as radians. For example, this interprets a pixel value of 1 as one radian. Degrees: Interpret the pixel values as degrees. For example, this interprets a pixel value of 1 as one degree. Circles (2pi): Interpret the pixel values as circles. For example, this interprets a pixel value of 1 as one circle (which is 2 pi radians or 360 degrees).

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer or vdb to apply the function to.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: function
outputs.description: The original layer or vdb with the function applied.

entries.title: Gamma
entries.summary: Applies gamma correction to a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The gamma correction factor to use. The common sRGB conversion is 2.2. By default this is an encoding gamma, so the color values are raised to the inverse of this exponent.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Switches from an encoding gamma to a decoding gamma. This does the opposite operation by inverting the gamma exponent.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Un-premultiplies the RGBA layers before applying the contrast and then premultiplies the RGBA layers. RGBA layers are often premultiplied, so using an exponentiation that doesn't consider the alpha causes low coverage areas to be considered dark. This parameter makes the exponentiation work as expected.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The layer, VDB, or attribute to apply gamma correction to.

inputs.label: gamma
inputs.description: An optional layer, VDB, or attribute that provides a per-pixel gamma correction. This value is multiplied with the Gamma parameter and then inverted if Invert is on.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: gamma
outputs.description: The layer, VDB, or attribute with gamma correction.

entries.title: Geometry Attribute from Layer
entries.summary: Samples layers with a geometry's attribute to create attributes from those layers.

parameters.label: Class
parameters.description: The class of the Position Attribute and Attributes. Primitive: A unit of geometry. See /model/primitives for more information. Point: A point in space as defined by four numbers (X, Y, Z, W). See /model/points for more information. Vertex: A point where lines meet. See /model/points for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space that the Position Attribute uses to sample the layers. Texture: Use texture space, which is 0 to 1 in the data window of the input. This provides normalized coordinates that're independent of the source's aspect ratio. For example, use this space when looking up into a latitude and longitude map. Image: Use image space, which is -1 to 1 in the display window of the input. This preserves square pixels for non-square aspect ratios. This space is invariant to cropping or overscanning. World: Use world space, which is a 3D location in the modelling space.

parameters.label: Position Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute that samples the layers relative to the geometry. Use a float3 attribute for world space. You can use a float2 attribute for texture and image space, though the node takes the xy component if you use a float3 attribute.

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.description: The number of attributes to insert onto the geometry.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name to use for the attribute created from the sampled layer. Use the dropdown menu to choose which data type to sample, which determines the new attribute's type. Input: Automatically determines the type of attribute to create from the current attrib# input. ID: Takes an ID layer and creates an int attribute. Mono: Takes a mono layer and creates a float attribute. UV: Takes a UV layer and creates a float2 attribute. RGB: Takes an RGB layer and creates a float3 attribute. RGBA: Takes an RGBA layer and creates a float4 attribute.

parameters.label: Do Nothing if Unwired
parameters.description: The node doesn't sample this attribute and insert it onto the geometry when the input is a null or unwired.

inputs.label: geometry
inputs.description: The geometry from which to read the position attribute and insert attributes onto.

inputs.label: attrib#
inputs.description: The layer to sample and create attributes from. The amount of attributes and their details are based on the Attributes information.

outputs.label: geometry
outputs.description: The original geometry with the new attributes.

parameters.label: Precision

NOTE: This option is only possible with integer volumes and ID layers. 16: Set the precision to 16-bits. 32: Set the precision to 32-bits.

entries.title: Geometry to Layer
entries.summary: Converts a volume, VDB, or camera primitive into a layer or VDB.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: The layer's storage precision. This controls how many bytes of storage each channel of the layer requires. More bytes allow for larger integer values or more accuracy for floating point values, but require more memory. 8: The channel uses 8-bits and defaults to quarter-precision. 16: The channel uses 16-bits and defaults to half-precision. 32: The channel uses 32-bits and defaults to full-precision.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See Border types for more information.

parameters.label: Slice
parameters.description: The plane to slice along when you convert a 3D volume. XY Plane: Slice the volume along the X and Y axes. YZ Plane: Slice the volume along the Y and Z axes. ZX Plane: Slice the volume along the Z and X axes.

parameters.label: Densify VDBs
parameters.description: Active regions of VDBs with constant values are collapsed into tiles to use less memory. However, as the GPU can't just-in-time unpack tiles; if one wants to do random writes the VDB has to be fully converted to leaves. This option will fully densify the VDB prior to converting. NOTE: This will move the VDB back to the CPU, and possibly require a massive amount of memory, so care should be used.

parameters.label: Set Imports from Geometry
parameters.description: Imports the volumes, VDBs, or camera primitives from the incoming geometry and populates the Outputs with the volumes', VDBs', or camera primitives' names and data types. When a volume, VDB, or camera primitive doesn't have a name attribute, Primitive Name is set to the volume's, VDB's, or camera primitive's primitive number.

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: The number of outputs for the node, which are the number of volumes, VDBs, or camera primitives from the incoming geometry to convert. The Set Imports from Geometry parameter creates a node output for each volume, VDB, or camera primitive.

parameters.label: Primitive Name
parameters.description: The name of the volume, VDB, or camera primitive to convert. You can also set this to a primitive index. Use the dropdown menu to set the volume's, VDB's, or camera primitive's data type. When blank, it looks for a volume, VDB, or camera primitive with a primitive number that corresponds to the multiparm index. For example, the first multiparm index looks for primitive 0 by default. TIP: Enter vel.* in Primitive Name and set its data type to RGB to collate volume triples (such as vel.x, vel.y, and vel.z) into a single RGB layer. This also works when slicing 3D volumes.

parameters.label: Optional
parameters.description: If the specified volume or camera primitive can't be found, fall back to the layer defined by the size_ref input and the Default Value parameter. If the specified VDB cannot be found, fall back to the vdb_ref input.

parameters.label: Default Value
parameters.description: When Optional is on for an ID, Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA type, this is the value to use for the layer.

inputs.label: geometry
inputs.description: The geometry with volumes, VDBs, or camera primitives to convert into a layer.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: NOTE
inputs.description: The node uses size_ref only for layers that have the Optional parameter on.

inputs.label: vdb_ref
inputs.description: The VDB topology to use for VDBs that have the Optional parameter on and are missing from the source. This topology will be copied into the output (activation masks, size, etc). If different type it is reset to zero values, otherwise unchanged. NOTE: The fall back is not densified even if Densify VDBs is set. Pre-densify if that is needed.

entries.title: Glow
entries.summary: Adds glow to an image based on its luminance.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of 1 means this node uses only the new value. The default value is 1. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Glow Threshold
parameters.description: Any pixel with a luminance value above this threshold has the glow effect. This lets you apply glow to only high luminance parts of your source layer. The default value is 0.75. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Glow Threshold.

parameters.label: Output Glow Only
parameters.description: Outputs only the glow effect, which displays a preview of the effect. Turn this on if you want to make the glow a separate AOV or configure the glow further before you composite it on top of the source layer. TIP: Turn this parameter on and use the Blend COP to put the glow back over the original image. Wire the original image into the bg input and the Glow COP into the fg input of the Blend COP. You can then set the Blend COP's Mode and Mask parameters to configure how the glow effect mixes with the original image.

parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: The amount of brightness to apply to the glow effect. Higher values increase the brightness to lighten and expand the glow effect. Lower values decrease the brightness to dim and shrink the glow effect. The default value is 2.

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: The amount of saturation to apply to the glow effect. Higher values increase the saturation to make the hue of the glow effect more intense. Lower values decrease the saturation to make the hue of the glow effect less intense, which results in an absence of hue (grayscale). High luminance parts of a layer are often desaturated. The default value is 1.

parameters.label: Tint
parameters.description: The tint (color) to apply to the glow effect. The default value is 1, 1, 1.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter that the Blur COPs in the node's subnetwork use. Gaussian (default): Image:/images/nodes/cop/glow_only_gaussian.jpg Box: Image:/images/nodes/cop/glow_only_box.jpg

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement that the Blur COPs in the node's subnetwork use to determine the size of the glow effect's radius. Image (default): Use image space to configure the size of the glow effect's radius. Pixels: Use pixels to configure the size of the glow effect's radius.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the glow effect's radius in image space or pixels, which the Units parameter determines. Higher values expand the circumference of the radius to enhance the smooth blur of the glow effect. Lower values contract the circumference of the radius to remove blurring and sharpen the glow effect. When Units is Image, the default value is 0.05. When Units is Pixels, the default value is 3.

parameters.label: Scale Size
parameters.description: Anistropic scaling of the size of the glow effect.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer to which you apply the glow effect.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: glow
outputs.description: The source layer with the glow effect added. If Output Glow Only is on, this instead outputs only the glow effect.

entries.title: Grunge Aurora
entries.summary: Generates a pattern resembling an aurora display.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the pixel value (originally in the 0 to 1 range). The node applies this before the Center adjustment. Values in the generated layer cover the range from C-A to C+A, where C is Center and A is Amplitude. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. Use Post Processing options to clamp the output.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output pixel values, applied as an offset. Values in the generated layer cover the range from C-A to C+A, where C is Center and A is Amplitude. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. Use Post Processing options to clamp the output.

parameters.label: Mask Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the pixel values before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the values more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the basic element of the generated pattern. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire pattern in image coordinates.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of the pattern. The pattern periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canonical image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Distortion Strength
parameters.description: The amount of vertical distortion to apply to each pixel along the X-axis. Higher values vertically reshape the straight input lines into irregular contours.

parameters.label: Distortion Size
parameters.description: The roughness of the distortion for pixels along the X-axis. Higher values result in smoother, more coherent edges with less waves. Lower values result in rougher edges with more waves.

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: The weight of samples along the trajectory, which are averaged as each pixel is distorted. This ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking, which affects the vertical profiles. For example, moving Point 1 from its default left position (evaluating to 0) to the right increases the separation between the streaks. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: The maximum number of steps that are allowed when applying distortion. Increase this value if you notice stepping artifacts in the result.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

outputs.label: grunge
outputs.description: The generated aurora pattern.

parameters.label: Secondary Roughness

parameters.label: Cracks Mask
parameters.description: The visibility of the cracks layer (vertical lines) in the pattern. Higher values darken and reveal the lines so they stand out more from the rust. Lower values fade and hide the lines until they disappear.

parameters.label: Cracks Size
parameters.description: The scale of the cracks layer (relative to the current Element Size) in the pattern. Higher values zoom in on the lines so each line covers more of the pattern, which decreases the overall amount of cracks. Lower values zoom out on the lines so each line covers less of the pattern, which increases the overall amount of cracks.

parameters.label: Seed

parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast

entries.title: Heat Distort
entries.summary: Distorts the input layer to simulate heat around fire and other mirage effects.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Distortion
parameters.description: The overall strength of distortion that scales the Base Distortion and Detail Distortion noises.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the distortion that scales the Base Distortion and Detail Distortion noises. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle of distortion. A value of 0 corresponds to the positive X direction in image space.

parameters.label: Accurate Distortion
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/distort#cfl

parameters.label: Streak Blur
parameters.description: Combines the pixel values along the direction of distortion by averaging the samples together. This smears the image along the distortion direction.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Adjusts the distortion's overall strength by the current timestep. The timestep is usually 1/$FPS, but in a sub-stepped simulation it represents the current step size.

parameters.label: Base Distortion
parameters.description: Adds large scale distortion for the heat haze. This controls the generic shape of the heat waves. Turn on Detail Distortion to add finer detail.

parameters.label: Distortion Scale
parameters.description: The strength of the base distortion, which controls the generic shape of the heat waves. The Distortion parameter scales this amount.

parameters.label: Element Size Scale
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the base distortion that's scaled by Element Size. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.

parameters.label: Detail Distortion
parameters.description: Adds small scale distortion for the heat haze. This controls the finer details of the heat waves. Turn on Base Distortion to control the overall shapes.

parameters.label: Distortion Scale
parameters.description: The strength of the detail distortion, which controls the finer details of the heat waves. The Distortion parameter scales this amount.

parameters.label: Element Size Scale
parameters.description: The size (in image coordinates) of the detail distortion that's scaled by Element Size. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.

parameters.label: Cutoff
parameters.description: Lower this value to make the detail distortion appear where there is less base distortion. By default, the detail noise is only prominent where there is strong base distortion.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount of detail in the distortion. Higher values increase how fine the distortion details are.

parameters.label: Blur Source
parameters.description: Blurs the source input relative to the strength of distortion. This increases how realistic the heat haze effect is.

parameters.label: Blur Scale
parameters.description: The size of the source blur effect's radius in image space. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the blur size.

parameters.label: Chromatic Aberration
parameters.description: Distorts the RGB channels of the image separately with different amounts. This creates colorization along the distortion unique to the chromatic aberration effect.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale all three channels.

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the red channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the red channel expand outwards and become more apparent.

parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the green channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the green channel expand outwards and become more apparent.

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale the blue channel. Higher values increase the offset between the channels, making the blue channel expand outwards and become more apparent.

parameters.label: Time Offset
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that's added to the start frame.

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: The interval length (in seconds) of the noise's pulse in the third dimension. Lower values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while higher values decrease this rate.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: Adds directional movement to the heat distortion. This is useful when the heat haze is moving along a constant direction, such as a mirage that moves upwards.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The angle of distortion. A value of 0 corresponds to the positive X direction in image space.

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.description: How fast the heat haze moves in the given direction. Higher values increase the speed of the heat haze's movement.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer to distort.

inputs.label: effect
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel scaling amount of the distortion.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: distort
outputs.description: The distorted layer.

entries.summary: Clamps height values to a minimum and/or maximum value.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of clipped height to mix with the original height.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Lower Limit and Upper Limit parameters with the minimum and maximum values of the input height layer.

parameters.label: Lower Limit
parameters.description: When enabled, clamps height values that are below the limit. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click the layer in the viewport to set the Lower Limit.

parameters.label: Upper Limit
parameters.description: When enabled, clamps height values that are above the limit. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click the layer in the viewport to set the Upper Limit.

parameters.label: Clamped Values
parameters.description: The value that replaces the clamped values. Replace with Limit Value: Clamped values are replaced by the value they went over or under. For example, when clamping between 0 and 1, -1 becomes 0 and 2 becomes 1. Soft Clip: Clamped values are smoothly transitioned across a Soft Clip Range to avoid hard edges.

parameters.label: Soft Clip Direction
parameters.description: The direction to smoothly transition the clamped values. Soft Clip Outside Range: Transition of the clamped values below the Lower Limit and above the Upper Limit, extending the effects of clamping. Soft Clip Inside Range: Transition of the clamped values above the Lower Limit and below the Upper Limit, narrowing the effects of clamping.

parameters.label: Soft Clip Range
parameters.description: A smoothing range for the transition from the limit value to the original values.

entries.title: HeightField Erode
entries.summary: Simulates hydraulic and thermal erosion at a specific scale to create more realistic terrain.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Turns on simulation, so the node updates with the Playbar. When turned off, the node simulates a fixed number of erosion iterations.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: When Simulate is off, the number of erosion timesteps to simulate. This controls the duration of the erosion process.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, clears the entire simulation cache. ((Ctrl))-click to also reset to the start frame.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, how many iterations of the simulation to run per frame. Higher values create stronger erosion effects, but also take longer to simulate.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: Turns on caching of the simulation. If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: How many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 5 to cache frames 5, 10, 15, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to turn off checkpointing.

parameters.label: Feature Size
parameters.description: The width of erosion features, in meters. Higher values will create wider channels, slopes, and deposits. Lower values will create sharper features. The smallest possible feature size is 3x the input terrain's pixel size. Features will be clamped to this size.

parameters.label: Spread Iterations
parameters.description: How many iterations of material transport to simulate in each frame. The number of iterations, together with the Feature Size, control the distance that eroded material can be transported within a single frame.

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomize the erosion process. With each new value, the distribution of erosion features changes.

parameters.label: Erodability
parameters.description: How prone the terrain is to hydro and thermal erosion. You can use the erodability input to vary the softness of the terrain.

parameters.label: Flow Force
parameters.description: The force of hydro erosion. With 0 you turn off hydro erosion.

parameters.label: Bank Angle
parameters.description: Controls the angle of channel walls. Higher values will create steeper channels that appear to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a jagged appearance.

parameters.label: Rainfall Coverage
parameters.description: The amount of rainfall to simulate each frame as a proportion of the terrain's surface. This controls the intensity of hydro erosion in each frame. You can use the rainfall input to vary the rainfall across the terrain.

parameters.label: Slope Influence
parameters.description: Controls how closely streams will follow the slope of the terrain. Higher values will result in winding channels. Lower values will result in straighter channels.

parameters.label: Erosion Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream erodes and accumulates material from the terrain.

parameters.label: Deposition Rate
parameters.description: Controls how quickly sediment is deposited once the stream's transport capacity is exceeded.

parameters.label: Removal Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream's accumulated sediment decays. Higher values will _reduce_ the amount of deposited sediment, allowing hydro erosion to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a rocky appearance.

parameters.label: Evaporation Rate
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream's sediment capacity decays. Lower values will create more prominent channels that persist across longer distances with a rocky appearance. Higher values will create smaller local depressions with a soil-like or sandy appearance.

parameters.label: Weathering Force
parameters.description: The force of thermal erosion. With 0 you can turn off thermal erosion.

parameters.label: Cut Angle
parameters.description: The angle that thermal erosion will cut until. A lower angle will make the cuts flatter, and allow for more thermal erosion to take place.

parameters.label: Repose Angle
parameters.description: The angle at which the thermal erosion debris will remain in place without sliding.

inputs.label: height

inputs.description: An optional debris layer to update with the simulation.

inputs.label: sediment
inputs.description: An optional sediment layer to update with the simulation.

inputs.label: flow

inputs.description: An optional mask to vary the amount of rainfall.

outputs.label: sediment

entries.title: HeightField Mask by Feature
entries.summary: Creates a mask based on different features of the heightfield.

parameters.label: Smooth Radius
parameters.description: The blur radius in local space used to smooth the input heightfield before the features are measured.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: When more than one feature is being measured, you can choose a compositing operation to combine each feature's mask. Add: Add the feature masks together. Multiply: Multiply the feature masks together. Average: Compute the average value of the feature masks. Minimum: Compute the minimum value of the feature masks. Maximum: Compute the maximum value of the feature masks.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: When enabled, inverts the resulting mask values.

parameters.label: Mask by Slope
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the slope of the heightfield.

parameters.label: Min Slope Angle
parameters.description: Mask areas with slope greater than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Max Slope Angle
parameters.description: Mask areas with slope less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Slope Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the Min Slope Angle to the Max Slope Angle.

parameters.label: Mask by Height
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the height.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Min Height and Max Height parameters with the minimum and maximum values of the input height layer.

parameters.label: Min Height
parameters.description: Mask areas with height greater than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Max Height
parameters.description: Mask areas with height less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Height Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the Min Height to the Max Height.

parameters.label: Mask by Curvature
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the maximum curvature.

parameters.label: Max Curvature
parameters.description: Mask areas with absolute curvature less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Curvature Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from negative Max Curvature to the positive Max Curvature.

parameters.label: Mask by Direction
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the heightfield's slope direction.

parameters.label: Goal Angle
parameters.description: Define an angle and all surfaces facing that direction get masked. 0 degrees is in the direction of increasing pixels along the height layer's width.

parameters.label: Angle Spread
parameters.description: Mask areas with this amount of variance from the Goal Angle. The range of directions is the Goal Angle minus/plus the Angle Spread.

parameters.label: Direction Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range, from the Goal Angle minus the Angle Spread, to the Goal Angle plus the Angle Spread.

parameters.label: Mask by Occlusion
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the heightfield's ambient occlusion.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Click to fill in the Minimum Occlusion and Maximum Occlusion parameters with the minimum and maximum ambient occlusion of the input height layer.

parameters.label: Minimum Occlusion
parameters.description: Mask areas with ambient occlusion greater than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Maximum Occlusion
parameters.description: Mask areas with ambient occlusion less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The scale applied to input height values before computing ambient occlusion. Higher values exaggerate the amount of occlusion and small variations in height appear more pronounced.

parameters.label: Occlusion Ramp
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the Minimum Occlusion to the Maximum Occlusion.

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.description: The distance in local space to send rays to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values extend the reach of the rays, producing more precise results, but at the cost of longer calculation times. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.description: How many steps (in buffer space) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values create less steps and therefore calculate faster, but may miss thin features since the steps are more spread out. Lower values create more steps, which are closer together.

parameters.label: Sample Count
parameters.description: The amount of rays to send to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values increase the number of rays sent and provide more accurate measurements, but at the cost of longer calculation times. Lower values decrease the number of rays sent.

parameters.label: Sample from Hemisphere
parameters.description: Divides the point's calculated angle by 90 degrees instead of 180 degrees.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: The heightfield to generate a mask from.

outputs.label: mask
outputs.description: The resulting mask composed of the measured features.

entries.title: HeightField Slump
entries.summary: Simulates loose material sliding down inclines and piling at the bottom.

parameters.label: Slump Mode
parameters.description: The method used to slump the input debris layer. Smooth: Slump the debris using smooth diffusion. This models liquid-like transport mechanisms. Granular: Slump the debris using chunky slumping with randomization. This models granular flow transport mechanisms. Rainfall: Slump the debris by suspending and transporting the debris in streams. This models hydraulic erosion transport mechanisms.

parameters.label: Debris Scale
parameters.description: The scale factor applied to the debris layer before simulating the slumping processes. This allows you to convert a mask into a depth of debris. If the debris input is unwired, the simulation begins with a constant depth of debris set by this Debris Scale.

parameters.label: Spread Iterations
parameters.description: How many iterations of material transport to simulate.

parameters.label: Repose Angle
parameters.description: The maximum slope, measured in degrees from the horizontal, at which loose solid material will remain in place without sliding.

parameters.label: Spread Rate
parameters.description: Controls how fast material spreads across the terrain in each iteration.

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.description: The seed used to randomize the slumping process.

parameters.label: Flow Force
parameters.description: When Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, controls how strongly streams erode the debris.

parameters.label: Rainfall Coverage
parameters.description: When Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the amount of rainfall to simulate each frame as a proportion of the terrain's surface.

parameters.label: Slope Influence
parameters.description: When Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, controls how closely streams will follow the slope of the terrain. Lower values will result in straighter channels. Higher values will result in winding channels.

parameters.label: Erosion Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream erodes and accumulates material from the terrain.

parameters.label: Deposition Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream deposits its excess accumulated sediment.

parameters.label: Removal Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream's accumulated sediment decays. Higher values will _reduce_ the amount of deposited sediment, allowing hydro erosion to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a rocky appearance.

parameters.label: Evaporation Rate
parameters.description: When the Slump Mode is set to Rainfall, the rate at which a stream's sediment capacity decays. Lower values will create more prominent channels that persist across longer distances with a rocky appearance. Higher values will create smaller local depressions with a soil-like or sandy appearance.

parameters.label: Remove Debris from Input Height
parameters.description: Before simulating the slumping process, remove the input debris from the input height.

parameters.label: Add Debris to Output Height
parameters.description: After simulating the slumping process, add the slumped debris to the input height.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: The height layer to slump debris across.

inputs.label: debris
inputs.description: An optional debris layer scaled by the Debris Scale which sets the initial depth of debris. When unwired, the debris layer has a constant value of 1.

outputs.label: height
outputs.description: The output height layer, potentially combined with the slumped debris.

outputs.label: debris
outputs.description: The resulting slumped debris.

outputs.label: flow
outputs.description: A UV layer containing the flow of slumped material.

entries.title: HeightField Strata
entries.summary: Adds sedimentary layering patterns to a HeightField.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of strata noise to mix into the input height layer.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: Specifies how the strata layer is combined with the input height layer. Add: Adds the foreground to the background. Subtract: Subtracts the foreground from the background. Multiply: Multiplies the background by the foreground. Difference: Takes the absolute difference between the foreground and the background. Maximum: Takes the maximum of the foreground and background. Minimum: Takes the minimum of the foreground and background.

parameters.label: Output Strata Only
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs only the strata layer, instead of blending the strata with the input height layer.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The multiplication factor for the strata noise applied by the node before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output strata noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the strata noise more extreme.

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the strata noise. Simplex: Create Perlin noise on a simplex grid. Perlin: Create Perlin noise on a regular grid. This type of noise generates more natural results. Worley Cellular F1: Create Worley noise using its distance to the closest Worley point. This generates a cell-like pattern. Worley Cellular F2-F1: Create Worley noise using the difference between its second closest and closest points. This generates a cell border-like noise. White (Random): Create white noise where each noise element is given a constant, but random value. Alligator: Create Alligator noise to produce a bumpy output that resembles alligator skin. Sparse Convolution: Create a type of value noise that smoothly blends values on a regular grid. This type of noise generates natural results that are smoother than Perlin noise.

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, you can define different metrics for computing the distance to a point. Euclidean: Use the length of the line segment between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in circular shapes. See Euclidean distance for more information. Manhattan: Use the sum of the differences between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in diamond shapes. See Taxicab geometry for more information. Chebyshev: Use the maximum difference between the two axial points to define the distance between the two points. This can result in square shapes. See Chebyshev distance for more information.

parameters.label: Worley Jitter
parameters.description: When Noise Type is Worley Cellular F1 or Worley Cellular F2-F1, this is the amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. NOTE: Values greater than 1 may produce artifacts as they can jitter past the search radius

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement to control the strata noise pattern. See /copernicus/spaces for more information.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size of the basic element of the strata noise in image or local coordinates (determined by the Space). You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anisotropic noise.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: An offset for the entire noise function in image or local coordinates (determined by the Space parameter).

parameters.label: Strata Size
parameters.description: The thickness of the strata.

parameters.label: Strata Offset
parameters.description: The offset of the strata.

parameters.label: Tilt
parameters.description: The angle of the strata in degrees. When set to zero, the layers are perpendicular to the height. If increased, the layers cut across the height.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The rotation of the strata about the Origin.

parameters.label: Origin
parameters.description: The center of rotation of the strata in image or local coordinates (defined by the Space parameter).

parameters.label: Add Layers
parameters.description: When enabled, adds numerous additional Layers of strata noise, with randomly varying orientations.

parameters.label: Layers
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the number of additional layers of strata noise to add.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the amount to scale the amplitude of each successive strata noise.

parameters.label: Tilt Variance
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the maximum amount in degrees to vary each additional strata from the set Tilt.

parameters.label: Rotate Variance
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the maximum amount in degrees to vary each additional strata from the set Rotate.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: When Add Layers is enabled, the random seed used to vary the orientation of the additional strata layers.

parameters.label: Base Height Influence
parameters.description: Controls how much the baseheight input affects the pattern of the strata.

parameters.label: Fractal Type
parameters.description: How to accumulate successive layers of noise to create finer-scale details. None: Don't add any additional layers of noise. Sharp: Add sharp layers of noise. Dampened: Add dampened layers of noise. Terrain: Add smoother layers of noise resembling terrain. Hybrid Terrain: Add smooth layers of noise that are sharpened at the peaks resembling rocky terrain.

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The number of times the noise is scaled and layered on top of itself.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration.

parameters.label: Octave Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the noise for each iteration.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: The height layer to add strata to.

inputs.label: baseheight
inputs.description: An optional layer of additional height to deform the strata patterns.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: height
outputs.description: The resulting height blended with the strata.

entries.summary: Imagines a sphere for each pixel and determines how occluded that sphere is based on its surroundings.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The scale applied to input height values before computing ambient occlusion. Increasing the scale exaggerates the amount of occlusion, which enables small variations in height to appear more pronounced.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space used to interpret the height's steepness.

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.description: The distance (in the given Space) to send rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values increase the distance you send the rays and provide more accurate measurements, but may slow cooking. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.description: How many steps (in buffer space) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values create less steps and therefore cook faster, but may miss thin features since the steps are more spread out. Lower values create more steps, which are closer together.

parameters.label: Sample Count
parameters.description: The amount of rays to send to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values increase the amount of rays sent and provide more accurate measurements, but may slow cooking. Lower values decrease the amount of rays sent.

parameters.label: Sample from Hemisphere
parameters.description: Divides the point's calculated angle by 90 degrees instead of 180 degrees.

parameters.label: Remap Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the output ambient occlusion values. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.

inputs.label: layer
inputs.description: The original height layer from which to calculate the ambient occlusion.

outputs.label: occlusion
outputs.description: The ambient occlusion layer.

entries.title: Height to Caustics
entries.summary: Creates caustic patterns on the ground from a refractive height layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The output layer type to generate. RGB enables the Dispersion parameters. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: Local: Use the height layer's local space for the light direction or position. World: Use world space for the light direction or position.

parameters.label: Enable Tile
parameters.description: Wrap ray hit positions back into the output image when they land outside the image bounds.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.description: Use a directional light. When this is off, the node uses a point light.

parameters.label: Light Azimuth
parameters.description: The horizontal angle of the directional light.

parameters.label: Light Altitude
parameters.description: The vertical angle of the directional light above the horizon.

parameters.label: Light Position
parameters.description: The position of the point light in the selected space.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Multiplies the final caustic intensity.

parameters.label: Index of Refraction
parameters.description: The index of refraction of the medium. The default value of 1.33 approximates water.

parameters.label: Height Offset
parameters.description: The value to add to the input height before tracing rays.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The value to multiply the input height by before tracing rays.

parameters.label: Compute Derivative outside Image
parameters.description: Allows the internal derivative calculation for the height surface to read outside the image bounds. This affects the surface normals used for refraction.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The kernel size for the internal derivative calculation on the height surface.

parameters.label: Ground Center
parameters.description: The base height of the ground. When no ground input is wired, this is the height of the flat ground plane.

parameters.label: Ground Offset
parameters.description: The value to multiply the wired ground height by before adding Ground Center.

parameters.label: Ray Trace Iterations
parameters.description: The number of Newton iterations used to approximate where refracted rays intersect the ground height layer.

parameters.label: Compute Derivative outside Image
parameters.description: Allows the internal derivative calculation for the ground layer to read outside the image bounds. This affects the ray-ground intersection solve.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The kernel size for the internal derivative calculation on the ground layer.

parameters.label: Photon Jitter Radius
parameters.description: The radius used to jitter photon samples during accumulation. Larger values create softer caustics with fewer grid artifacts. This has no effect when Photon Iterations is 1.

parameters.label: Photon Iterations
parameters.description: The number of photon accumulation passes to run for each pixel. Higher values reduce noise and improve denoising quality, but take longer to cook.

parameters.label: Denoise Iterations
parameters.description: The number of denoising iterations to apply after photon accumulation.

parameters.label: Denoise Mask
parameters.description: Controls where denoising is applied based on the caustic intensity mask. Higher ramp values apply stronger denoising in the corresponding intensity range.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Perturbation: Uses a fast approximation that perturbs the refractive result into color bands. This is faster than Spectrum, but is less physically accurate. Spectrum: Samples wavelengths using the selected material's dispersion model. This can create more vivid dispersion, but is slower.

parameters.label: Material
parameters.description: The transparent material used for spectral dispersion. This is available when Method is Spectrum. Water: Uses water-like dispersion. Glass: Uses glass-like dispersion, which is stronger than water. Diamond: Uses diamond-like dispersion, which produces the strongest color separation.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.description: The background color composited behind the RGB caustics.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The amount of color dispersion. Higher values increase the separation between wavelengths.

parameters.label: Number of Colors
parameters.description: When Method is Perturbation, this controls the number of color bands used for photon distribution. When Method is Spectrum, this controls the number of wavelength samples per photon iteration. Higher values create smoother spectral dispersion, but take longer to cook.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: The height layer representing the refractive surface of the transparent medium.

inputs.label: ground
inputs.description: An optional height layer representing the ground that receives the caustics. If this input is not wired, the node uses a flat ground plane.

outputs.label: caustics
outputs.description: The generated caustic pattern on the ground.

entries.title: Height to Normal
entries.summary: Converts a height layer to a normal layer.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The method used to store the normals (see Normals for more information). Signed (-1 to 1): Output signed normals, compatible with geometry attributes. Offset (0 to 1): Output offset normals, compatible with normal maps.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The amount to globally scale the height before computing normals. Higher numbers create steeper normals.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Derivatives at the boundary read outside of the image. When off, derivatives at the boundary are restricted to the image range. Turning this parameter on is useful when building seamless textures with a wrap border type. Turn this off if you want to avoid artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in a clamp border type, as it acts like an extrapolation.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivative, which might remove stepping artifacts from the derivative. A derivative is often computed with adjacent pixels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: A mono layer that represents a heightmap.

outputs.label: normals
outputs.description: The RGB layer that stores the normals of the heightmap in either Signed or Offset format.

entries.title: Height to Shadow
entries.summary: Creates shadows using a virtual light source.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space in which to interpret light position, direction, and normal parameters. Local: Uses the image's local space. World: Uses world space.

parameters.label: Height Map Scale
parameters.description: The scale to apply to height values before computing shadow occlusion.

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.description: The distance (in the given Space) to send rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values increase the distance you send the rays and provide more accurate measurements, but may slow cooking. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.description: How many steps (in buffer space) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values create less steps and therefore cook faster, but may miss thin features since the steps are more spread out. Lower values create more steps, which are closer together.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The light source profile to use. Disk: Sets the virtual light source as a disk, which distributes lights over the area of a disk. This corresponds to an area light as used in rendering engines. Sphere: Sets the virtual light source as a sphere, which distributes lights along the outside surface of a sphere. This corresponds to a sphere light as used in rendering engines. Directional: Sets the virtual light source as a directional light, which emits a point light source at infinity. This corresponds to a directional light as used in rendering engines.

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.description: When the light source is Disk, ignores light from the back side of the disk.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius in image space of the light source. This parameter is available for Disk and Sphere light sources.

parameters.label: Angular Size
parameters.description: The angular radius in degrees of the Directional light source.

parameters.label: Use
parameters.description: The coordinates to use to control the position of Disk and Sphere light sources. Spherical: Use spherical coordinates, which use distance and two angles to define a point. Cartesian: Use Cartesian coordinates, which are the X, Y, and Z locations along the axes.

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.description: When Use is Azimuth/Altitude/Distance, this is the distance in image space between the origin and the light source.

parameters.label: Altitude
parameters.description: When Use is Azimuth/Altitude/Distance, this is the angle in degrees of the light source relative to the XY-plane.

parameters.label: Azimuth
parameters.description: When Use is Azimuth/Altitude/Distance, this is the angle in degrees of the light source relative to the X-axis on the XY-plane.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: When Use is Position, this is the 3D position of the light source.

parameters.label: Light Normal
parameters.description: The normal direction of the Disk light source.

parameters.label: Use
parameters.description: The coordinates to use to control the direction of a Directional light source. Azimuth/Altitude: Uses two angles to define the light direction. Direction Vector: Uses a 3D direction vector.

parameters.label: Azimuth
parameters.description: When the directional Use parameter is Azimuth/Altitude, this is the angle in degrees of the light direction relative to the X-axis on the XY-plane.

parameters.label: Altitude
parameters.description: When the directional Use parameter is Azimuth/Altitude, this is the angle in degrees of the light direction relative to the XY-plane.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: When the directional Use parameter is Direction Vector, this is the 3D light direction.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: The original height layer from which to calculate shadows.

outputs.label: shadow
outputs.description: The shadowed layer.

entries.title: Histogram
entries.summary: Builds a histogram from a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The type of histogram to output. Colored Bars: Output the histogram as a horizontal ramp. Each vertical line is colored by how many pixels in the source fall in that bucket range. If alpha is in the source, this affects the bars and can result in clipping. Separate Bars: Output the histogram as separate horizontal bars for each channel. Each bar is grayscale, where red is the bottom bar and alpha (if present) is the top bar. Graph: Control how high to draw the bar instead of controlling the bar's intensity. Each channel is done independently, which results in a mixture of red, green, blue, and alpha bars overlapping.

parameters.label: Buckets
parameters.description: The number of buckets to divide the range into. Finer buckets provide a more accurate graph. NOTE: The Histogram node bases the height or intensity of a bar on the percentage of total pixels that fall into the bucket.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.description: The value at which to start the histogram. This is usually 0 for black. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Minimum.

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.description: The value at which to end the histogram. This is usually 1 for white. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Maximum.

parameters.label: Outside Values
parameters.description: The method used to manage pixel values that lie outside of the histogram range. Discarding and clamping are done per-channel, so the totals of each channel may not be the same if you use Discard. Discard: Ignore values outside of the range so they don't contribute to the histogram. Clamp: The values outside of the range contribute to either the first or last bucket. This method causes the buckets to have extreme values, but can help you determine how much the window has cropped out.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The amount to scale the percentage of total pixels that fall into the bucket. This is often a small percentage, so increasing that value enhances the chart's legibility.

parameters.label: Channel Scope
parameters.description: The RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. NOTE: The number of bars or channels don't change, so unscoped channels have zero contributions. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: A layer or vdb for which to build the histogram.

inputs.label: active
inputs.description: A layer or vdb that specifies a region of pixels to use for the histogram. Only pixels where the active layer is greater than or equal to 0.5 contribute to the histogram.

outputs.label: histogram
outputs.description: The layer of the same type and size as the source, but with a histogram written to it according to the Mode parameter.

outputs.label: counts
outputs.description: The layer that stores the raw bucket values. Its width is the number of buckets and its height is 5. The first four rows (from the bottom) are the red, green, blue, and alpha histogram counts. The last row contains the total number of processed pixels in the 0th column.
