entries.title: HSV Adjust
entries.summary: Converts between RGB and HSV color spaces, or modifies HSV.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The operation that this node performs. Hue/Sat/Val Adjust: Modify the hue, saturation, and value of the pixels. Convert RGB to HSV: Convert the RGB space into the HSV space. Convert HSV to RGB: Convert the HSV space into the RGB space.

parameters.label: Hue Shift
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to shift the hue around the HSV cone. This changes all colors to different hues. Gray pixels aren't affected.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Mode
parameters.description: When a hueshift input is wired in, this is how to shift the source layer's hue values. Min/Max: Remap the incoming hueshift to set 0 and 1 to specific degrees. Width: Remap the incoming hueshift to set the width between 0 and 1 to a specific distance in degrees.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Min
parameters.description: When Hue Shift Mode is Min/Max, this is the degree to remap 0 to on the hue wheel. A value of 0 represents no shift. For example, when set to -60 the hue is shifted by -60 degrees where the input equals 0. The node interpolates for values between this setting and the Hue Shift Max.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Max
parameters.description: When Hue Shift Mode is Min/Max, this is the degree to remap 1 to on the hue wheel. A value of 0 represents no shift. For example, when set to 88 the hue is shifted by 88 degrees where the input equals 1. The node interpolates for values between this setting and the Hue Shift Min.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Width
parameters.description: When Hue Shift Mode is Width, this is the distance in degrees to remap the width between 0 and 1 to on the hue wheel. A value of 0 represents no shift. For example, when set to 40 this remaps 0 to -20 and 1 to 20.

parameters.label: Keep Luminance
parameters.description: Maintains the perceptual luminance of the pixel when hues shift since some hues appear brighter than others.

parameters.label: Saturation Scale
parameters.description: The amount to increase (>1) or decrease (<1) the color saturation of the image. This multiplies the saturation.

parameters.label: Saturation Shift
parameters.description: The amount to shift the color saturation of the pixels. Higher values add to the saturation while lower values subtract from the saturation. Shifting is normally used only to reduce the saturation, otherwise grayscale elements suddenly take on a random color.

parameters.label: Value Scale
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the value (brightness) of the pixel. This multiplies the brightness.

parameters.label: Value Shift
parameters.description: The value (brightness) to add to all pixels. Higher values add to the brightness while lower values subtract from the brightness.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Treats RGBA as premultiplied, which multiplies the red, green, and blue channels by the alpha channel.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer to which you apply the HSV effect.

inputs.label: hueshift
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel hue amount that's scaled by the Hue Shift Min, Hue Shift Max, and Hue Shift Width parameters.

inputs.label: saturation
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel saturation amount that's scaled by the Saturation Scale and Saturation Shift parameters.

inputs.label: value
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel brightness amount that's scaled by the Value Scale and Value Shift parameters.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: hsv_adjust
outputs.description: The layer with the HSV effect applied.

entries.title: Hyperbolic Tile
entries.summary: Generates hyperbolic polygon tiles for texture patterns.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times that the base regular polygon's pattern repeats within the boundary of the Poincaré disk. Each copy reflects and inverts the previous copy's pattern.

parameters.label: Polygons
parameters.description: The amount of sides to give the base regular polygon.

parameters.label: Rectanglize
parameters.description: Changes the Poincaré disk's boundary to the image space square instead of a circle. Choose a mapping type from the dropdown menu to set how the pattern within the Poincaré disk's boundary maps outwards to occupy the entire image space square. Conformal: Preserves the angles of the tiles. Each corner of the square is a singularity of this mapping, so artifacts may appear near the corners. :fig: Image:/images/nodes/cop/hyperbolic_conformal.jpg Elliptic Grid: Uses an elliptic grid to map the Poincaré disk to the square. This creates curved radial grid lines in the square region. NOTE: Though this mapping type minimizes distortion in the diagonal regions of the square, it can cause additional stretching near the corners. :fig: Image:/images/nodes/cop/hyperbolic_elliptic_grid.jpg Squircle: Uses squircular mapping from the Poincaré disk to the square. This stretches the radial direction uniformly in a straight manner. NOTE: The diagonal regions of this mapping type have more distortion than the Elliptic Grid type. However, the overall appearance may appear more uniform because the distortion is more evenly distributed. :fig: Image:/images/nodes/cop/hyperbolic_squircle.jpg Equal Area: Uses a map that preserves the area up to the constant ratio. This can make the base polygon include additional sides and vertices. :fig: Image:/images/nodes/cop/hyperbolic_equal_area.jpg

parameters.label: Stretch to Fit
parameters.description: When Rectanglize is on and the size_ref has a rectangle input, this option stretches the square to fill the given rectangular region.

parameters.label: Flattening
parameters.description: The amount to flatten circular arcs in the base polygon. When set to 0, the base polygon fits within the Poincaré disk. Higher values expand the circular arcs in the base regular polygon out towards the image's border to flatten them. They can't be entirely flat because straight lines must pass the center of the Poincaré disk to define the hyperbolic regular polygons.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The length of straight lines in the base polygon. This parameter corresponds to the radius of the Poincaré disk when Flattening is 0.

parameters.label: Tile Fitting
parameters.description: Fills the image to tiles when the uv output is used. A value of 0 makes the image appear as a square within each tile. Increasing the value to 1 stretches the image to fill the entire tile area.

parameters.label: Poincaré Disk Mask
parameters.description: Displays only the pattern that's within the boundary of the Poincaré disk. This parameter doesn't apply if Rectanglize is on.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

outputs.label: tiles
outputs.description: The checkerboard type tiled layer.

outputs.label: id
outputs.description: The layer storing the ID values.

outputs.label: uv
outputs.description: The layer storing the UV values.

outputs.label: mask
outputs.description: An ID layer storing the ID of the UV layer and the background.

entries.title: ID to Mask
entries.summary: Creates a mask from an ID layer based on filtering parameters.

parameters.label: ID Pattern
parameters.description: The group syntax to use to filter IDs. If this is blank, the node filters all IDs. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the IDs you want to select to set the ID Pattern.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask that the node generates.

parameters.label: Keep by Range
parameters.description: Filters IDs based on a range.

parameters.label: Range Type
parameters.description: Specifies the range that determines how to filter the IDs. Start and End (default): Set a range that starts and ends with a specific ID. The range includes the start and end ID. Start and Length: Set a range that starts with a specific ID and ends once the range includes a specific number of IDs.

parameters.label: Start ID
parameters.description: When this parameter is on and the Range Type is Start and End, this is the ID at the start of the range. For example, a value of 0 means the range includes IDs greater than and equal to 0. The default value is 0. When this parameter is off, there is no limit for the start of the range.

parameters.label: End ID
parameters.description: When this parameter is on and the Range Type is Start and End, this is the ID at the end of the range. For example, a value of 100 means the range includes IDs less than and equal to 100. The default value is 100. When this parameter is off, there is no limit for the end of the range.

parameters.label: Range Offset
parameters.description: When Range Type is Start and End, this is the value to add to the Start ID and End ID parameters. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Start ID
parameters.description: When Range Type is Start and Length, this is the ID at the start of the range. For example, a value of 0 means the range includes IDs greater than and equal to 0. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: When Range Type is Start and Length, this is how many IDs to include in the range. The default value is 5.

parameters.label: Select/of
parameters.description: The number of IDs to select out of every block of IDs. For example, set Select to 1 and of to 2 so the filter selects half of the integer values. The Offset parameter impacts whether the selected values are odd or even. The default values are 1 of 2.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The start of the range filter, which is measured relative to the start of the range. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Keep by Chance
parameters.description: Filters by selecting a subset of IDs by random chance.

parameters.label: Probability
parameters.description: The chance (percentage) that the group includes the ID. For example, a value of 0.1 means that the group includes about 10% of the IDs. The default value is 0.5.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed that determines which elements to include. Changing this value causes each ID to generate a new random value, which results in a new pattern. The default value is 30.

parameters.label: Keep within Mask
parameters.description: When you have a mask input, this filters by keeping a subset of IDs within a mask layer.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: When you have a mask input, pixels in the mask layer that have a value greater than this threshold are considered when masking. The default value is 0.5.

inputs.label: id
inputs.description: The original ID layer to convert.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: mask
outputs.description: The output mask layer.

entries.title: ID to SDF
entries.summary: Computes a signed distance field from changes in ID values.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the sign. Since an ID field is two-sided and has no inside or outside, its values usually have a positive distance. Inverting therefore changes this to a negative distance.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times to compute the distance to changes in ID values. A value of 1 is sufficient when there's a uniform speed field, but you may need higher values for the distances to fully propagate if the speed has complex variations.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of the blocks to break the layer up into. This parameter helps balance the serial and parallel components of the algorithm. This shouldn't affect the behavior when the algorithm's converged. The default values should be sufficient.

inputs.label: id
inputs.description: The ID layer. The node computes the distance to changes in ID values.

outputs.label: sdf
outputs.description: The signed distance to the nearest border where ID values changed.

entries.title: Illegal Pixel
entries.summary: Detects and then fixes or highlights illegal pixels in images.

parameters.label: Illegal Pixels
parameters.description: The method used to fix or flag illegal pixels. Often, fixing is used when you want to continue with the image as-is and flagging is used to debug the shader. Fix by Blending Surrounding Pixels: Replace a bad pixel by blending the surrounding pixels together. This method is best for small numbers or isolated pixels. Fix by Zeroing: Clear the NANs so that downstream operations behave. This method doesn't visually correct the image. Show with Highlight: Show bad pixels by highlighting them based on the Highlight Color value. Show by Isolating: Show bad pixels by highlighting them and clearing all correct pixels.

parameters.label: Highlight Color
parameters.description: When Illegal Pixels is Show with Highlight, this is the color in which to highlight the bad pixels.

parameters.label: Detect
parameters.description: The type of illegal pixels to find. NaN Values: Find only NaN values. Infinite Values: Find only infinite values. NaN and Infinite Values: Find both NaN and infinite values. Custom: Find values according to a custom Rule.

parameters.label: Rule
parameters.description: The custom rule to use. Less Than: Flag pixels less than the comparison value. Less Than or Equal: Flag pixels less than or equal to the comparison value. Greater Than: Flag pixels greater than the comparison value. Greater Than or Equal: Flag pixels greater than or equal to the comparison value. Equal: Flag pixels equal to the comparison value.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer with illegal floating point values you want to detect.

outputs.label: clean
outputs.description: The layer with fixed or highlighted illegal floating point values.

entries.title: Integrate Volume
entries.summary: Integrates a VDB along camera rays.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. The output is mono when the input's a Float VDB. The output is RGB when the input's a Vector VDB, accumulating each channel separately along the view ray. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Move to Origin
parameters.description: Moves the output layer to the origin.

parameters.label: Depth Conversion
parameters.description: Convert the mindepth and maxdepth inputs to distances from the camera from this kind of input. Distance: Doesn't modify the inputs since they're already distances. Depth: The inputs are depths. These are distances projected along the forward direction of the camera, like you can get from Node:cop/rasterizegeo. Height: The inputs are heights. These are displacements from the imaging plane toward the camera position.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The value to compute along each view ray. Integral: Integrate the input field along the view ray. This adds up the value in the VDB, sampled along the view ray. Transmittance: Calculate the transmittance along the view ray. This treats the input volume as optical density. Minimum: Find the minimum value along the view ray. If not hit, this is infinity. Maximum: Find the maximum value along the view ray. If not hit, this is -infinity.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to scale the density. The node applies this scale after it linearly maps and applies the ramp to the density.

parameters.label: Min
parameters.description: The lower bound of the interval to linearly map to (0, 1). For each sample of the VDB, the node linearly maps the Density interval to (0, 1).

parameters.label: Max
parameters.description: The upper bound of the interval to linearly map to (0, 1). For each sample of the VDB, the node linearly maps the Density interval to (0, 1).

parameters.label: Ramp Mode
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp. No Ramp: Don't apply the map. This turns off the ramp. Clamped Ramp: Clamp the remapped values to 0 and 1, respectively. Periodic Ramp: Wrap the remapped values around at 0 and 1.

parameters.label: Density Ramp
parameters.description: The map to apply to the density after it's linearly remapped to (0, 1). See Ramp parameters for more information.

parameters.label: Seed Jitter with Time
parameters.description: Makes the sample location jittering depend on time.

parameters.label: Sample Jitter Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter sample locations. When 0, sample locations are always at the centre of ray slices. When 1, sample locations can be drawn from anywhere along their respective ray slice. There is never more than one sample drawn per ray slice.

parameters.label: Stratification Jitter Scale
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter ray slice locations. This is a single offset applied to each view ray, not per sample. When 0, the start of ray slice #0 coincides with the ray origin. When 1, the start of ray slice #0 varies from backward and forward along the ray by half the step length.

parameters.label: Integration Step Size
parameters.description: The length of ray slices. This is the expected distance between samples when samples are jittered.

parameters.label: Max Step Count
parameters.description: Used to prevent the OpenCL kernel from running forever or timing out. You shouldn't need to change the 4096 value unless rastering a very deep volume.

parameters.label: Transmittance Cutoff
parameters.description: When Operation is Integral or Transmittance, this is the transmittance of the accumulated portion of the ray after which to stop raymarching. A value of -1 turns this off, which may be necessary to calculate the integral of a field that doesn't represent an optical density. This is an optimization for when a very dense region of the volume is encountered, where almost none of the light from behind this region reaches the camera so you can stop raymarching early to save time. Due to rounding error, it's possible for the accumulated transmittance to reach 0 despite this not being physically possible, and this is seen when rasterizing very dense volumes.

inputs.label: camera_ref
inputs.description: An optional camera layer that provides a position and a projection from world space to image space (see /copernicus/spaces), as well as an imaging plane. This determines the view ray for each output pixel. NOTE: If there's no camera_ref layer, the node uses the default orthographic projection (-1 to 1), which moves forward along the Z-axis like Node:cop/rasterizegeo.

inputs.label: density
inputs.description: The density VDB to integrate, which is either a Float or Vector VDB.

inputs.label: vieworigin
inputs.description: Instead of using the camera_ref input, this layer provides a ray origin for each output pixel.

inputs.label: viewdir
inputs.description: Instead of using the camera_ref input, this layer provides a ray direction for each output pixel.

inputs.label: mindepth
inputs.description: The raymarch minimum depth boundary.

inputs.label: maxdepth
inputs.description: The raymarch maximum depth boundary.

outputs.label: result
outputs.description: The computed integral, transmittance, minimum, or maximum value (based on the set Operation). Each output pixel corresponds to a view ray.

entries.title: Invert
entries.summary: Inverts a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Invert By
parameters.description: The method used to invert the values. Complement: The pixel value x is set to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for images in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values. To resolve this, you can use a Clamp COP. Negate: The pixel value x is set to - x. This is useful for switching a value's sign. Reciprocal: The pixel value x is set to 1 / x.

inputs.label: source

inputs.label: mask

entries.title: Knit
entries.summary: Generates a grid of knitted fabric stitches.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Loads a predefined collection of settings for a particular style of knit. Choosing a preset overwrites the parameters below. Image:/images/nodes/cop/knit_presets.jpg

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed for all of the node's randomization, including Jitter and the Variance and Min/Max modes of Scale, Stretch, and Angle. Changing it produces a new random arrangement.

parameters.label: Rows
parameters.description: The number of rows of stitches in the grid.

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.description: The number of columns of stitches in the grid.

parameters.label: Row Offset
parameters.description: Staggers each successive row sideways by this amount, in image space. Use a small offset to break up the regular grid.

parameters.label: Column Offset
parameters.description: Staggers each successive column by this amount, in image space.

parameters.label: Jitter Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the jitter input layer affects the result. Disabled when nothing is connected to the jitter input.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random positional offset added to each stitch, in image space. Higher values scatter the stitches off their grid positions.

parameters.label: Jitter Type
parameters.description: Toggles per-component jitter controls. Per-Component Controls: Reveals Jitter Scale so you can scale the jitter independently along each axis instead of uniformly.

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.description: Per-axis multipliers for the Jitter amount, biasing the random offset more along X or Y. Visible when Jitter Type has per-component controls enabled.

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.description: Controls how much the scale input layer affects each stitch's size. Disabled when nothing is connected to the scale input.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The base size of each stitch, in image space. Lower values leave gaps between stitches; higher values pack them closer together.

parameters.label: Scale Mode
parameters.description: How each stitch's scale is chosen. Uniform: Every stitch uses the same Scale. Variance: Randomly varies each stitch's scale around Scale by up to Scale Variance. Min/Max: Randomly picks each stitch's scale between Min Value and Max Value.

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.description: The maximum random deviation from Scale when Scale Mode is Variance.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The smallest random scale when Scale Mode is Min/Max.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The largest random scale when Scale Mode is Min/Max.

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the stretch input layer affects the per-stitch stretch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the stretch input.

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.description: How each stitch's stretch is chosen. Uniform: Every stitch uses the same Stretch X and Stretch Y. Variance: Randomly varies each stitch's stretch around Stretch X/Stretch Y by up to Stretch Variance. Min/Max: Randomly picks each stitch's stretch between Min Value and Max Value.

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.description: The horizontal stretch factor for each stitch. Values above 1 widen stitches; below 1 narrow them.

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.description: The vertical stretch factor for each stitch. Values above 1 lengthen stitches; below 1 shorten them.

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.description: The maximum random X and Y deviation from Stretch X/Stretch Y when Stretch Mode is Variance.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The smallest random X and Y stretch when Stretch Mode is Min/Max.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The largest random X and Y stretch when Stretch Mode is Min/Max.

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the angle input layer rotates each stitch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the angle input.

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.description: Scales how much the direction input layer orients each stitch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the direction input.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: The base rotation applied to every stitch, in degrees.

parameters.label: Angle Mode
parameters.description: How each stitch's rotation is chosen. Uniform: Every stitch uses the same Angle. Variance: Randomly varies each stitch's angle around Angle by up to Angle Variance. Min/Max: Randomly picks each stitch's angle between Min Value and Max Value.

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.description: The maximum random deviation, in degrees, from Angle when Angle Mode is Variance.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.description: The smallest random angle, in degrees, when Angle Mode is Min/Max.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.description: The largest random angle, in degrees, when Angle Mode is Min/Max.

parameters.label: Round to Multiples
parameters.description: When the toggle is on, snaps each stitch's final angle to the nearest multiple of this value, in degrees. Applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Knit Shape Type
parameters.description: The style of stitch the node generates. Purl: A bumpy purl stitch, shaped by the bulge and wrinkle controls below. Knit: A V-shaped knit stitch built from interlocking fibers, shaped by the weave and fiber controls below.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: The width of each purl stitch. Larger values round out the shape, while smaller values make it more compact and pinched at the ends.

parameters.label: Bulge Scale
parameters.description: How far the purl stitch bulges outward in height.

parameters.label: Softness
parameters.description: Softens the edges of the stitch, blurring the transition between the stitch and the gaps around it.

parameters.label: Wrinkles
parameters.description: The strength of the fine wrinkles added across the stitch surface.

parameters.label: Wrinkle Size
parameters.description: The size of the wrinkle detail. Smaller values produce finer wrinkles.

parameters.label: Edge Bend
parameters.description: How much the stitch bends along its edges. Negative values bend it the opposite way.

parameters.label: Edge Bend Bias
parameters.description: Shifts the balance of the Edge Bend across the stitch, weighting the bend more toward one end than the other. At 0 the bend stays concentrated on one side; higher values push it toward the opposite side, distributing the curvature more evenly.

parameters.label: Bulge Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the cross-sectional bulge profile of the stitch, controlling how its height falls off from the center toward the edges.

parameters.label: Height Ramp
parameters.description: Remaps the height profile of the stitch along its length.

parameters.label: Double Knit
parameters.description: Generates a second interlocking strand for each stitch, producing a denser double-knit weave.

parameters.label: Invert Knit
parameters.description: Flips the over/under direction of the knit stitch.

parameters.label: Weave Width
parameters.description: The width of each knit stitch.

parameters.label: Weave Height
parameters.description: The height of each knit stitch. This is the in-plane vertical extent of the stitch shape, not its out-of-plane depth.

parameters.label: Weave Radius
parameters.description: The thickness of the yarn that forms each knit stitch.

parameters.label: Fiber Strength
parameters.description: The strength of the fine fiber detail added along each strand.

parameters.label: Fiber Cycles
parameters.description: The number of fiber twist cycles along each strand.

parameters.label: Fiber Twist
parameters.description: The direction and amount of twist in the fiber detail. Negative values twist the opposite way.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: jitter
inputs.description: An optional layer that drives per-stitch positional jitter, scaled by the Jitter Layer Mask parameter.

inputs.label: direction
inputs.description: An optional layer that orients each stitch, scaled by the Direction Layer Mask parameter.

inputs.label: angle
inputs.description: An optional layer that rotates each stitch, scaled by the Angle Layer Mask parameter.

inputs.label: scale
inputs.description: An optional layer that resizes each stitch, weighted by the Scale Layer Mask parameter.

inputs.label: stretch
inputs.description: An optional layer that stretches each stitch, scaled by the Stretch Layer Mask parameter.

inputs.label: color
inputs.description: An optional RGB layer that tints each stitch, passed through to the color output.

inputs.label: alpha
inputs.description: An optional mask layer controlling the per-stitch opacity.

inputs.label: flip
inputs.description: An optional layer that flips stitches between knit and purl.

outputs.label: height
outputs.description: A mono layer with the height, or relief, of the knit, suitable for displacement or for feeding the Height to Normal COP.

outputs.label: color
outputs.description: An RGB layer with the per-stitch color, derived from the color input when connected.

outputs.label: id
outputs.description: An ID layer giving each stitch a unique value, useful for randomizing color or masking individual stitches downstream.

outputs.label: uv
outputs.description: A UV layer giving per-stitch texture coordinates for mapping detail onto each stitch.

entries.title: Kuwahara Filter
entries.summary: Applies the Kuwahara filter, which creates painterly effects.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to compute the filter. NOTE: The Kuwahara filter requires access to k^2 pixels for every pixel, where k is the kernel diameter, which means large kernels can become expensive. Approximate: Rather than computing the standard deviations and means for each pixel, generate it in a single pre-pass. This speeds up computation but causes variations in radius, which affects neighboring pixels. Exact: Compute the filter exactly for each pixel. GPUs often make this practical even for large radii.

parameters.label: Luminance
parameters.description: The common standard deviation for quadrant selection. When the node processes more than one channel, the filter still picks the same source quadrant for all channels. SGI Luminance: This is a historical luminance computation used in Houdini, which is believed to originate with SGI. lum = 0.3086 * red + 0.6094 * green + 0.0820 * blue NTSC Luminance: The standard NTSC luminance computation, which is a common luminance option. lum = 0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue HDTV Luminance: The HDTV standard luminance from BT 709. lum = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue Average: An average of the channels. Maximum Channel: The maximum of the channels. Minimum Channel: The minimum of the channels. Magnitude / Length: The length of the vector formed by taking the channels as components. For a mono input, this is the absolute value. Hue: Convert to HSV and return the hue channel. Saturation: Convert to HSV and return the saturation channel. Value: Convert to HSV and return the value channel. Red: Extract the red, or x, channel. Green: Extract the green, or y, channel. Blue: Extract the blue, or z, channel. Alpha: Extract the alpha, or w, channel.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius (in pixels) of each of the four regions on which to perform blur. The radius offsets the four regions so they don't overlap.

parameters.label: Blur Scale
parameters.description: When computing the average of a region, this is the amount to scale the size of the region. Lower values select a sharper source area, but use the larger area to determine the standard deviation. Higher values increase the blur effect but don't affect which quadrant is picked.

parameters.label: Blend to Blur
parameters.description: A value of 0 picks the average from the region with the smallest standard deviation. A value of 1 averages the averages, which effectively performs a larger blur. Inbetween values adjust the weighting, increasing the weight of areas with large standard deviations.

parameters.label: Separation
parameters.description: The amount to scale the offset of the four regions, which is determined by the Radius. A value of 0 makes all the regions sample the same location, causing this to be a box blur. Values over 1 make the regions sample dislocated areas of the image.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original source layer to filter.

inputs.label: radius
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel scale for the size of the filter that's scaled by the Radius parameter.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: blur
outputs.description: The filtered output layer.

entries.title: Laplacian
entries.summary: Computes the Laplacian of the source layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The space to compute the Laplacian in. This affects the magnitude of the result. Image: Compute the Laplacian in Image Space, by normalizing the change in values by the image-space pixel size. Pixel: Compute the Laplacian in Pixel Space, by normalizing the change in values by the pixel size. Local: Compute the Laplacian in Local Space, by normalizing the change in values by the world-space pixel size.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the source values before computing the Laplacian.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Determines if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range. Turning this parameter on is useful when building seamless textures with a wrap border type. Turn this off if you want to avoid artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in a clamp border type, as it acts like an extrapolation.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivatives used for the Laplacian. A derivative is often computed with adjacent pixels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives. Increasing this value may remove stepping artifacts from the result.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The layer from which to compute the Laplacian.

outputs.label: laplacian
outputs.description: The computed Laplacian. For multi-channel inputs, the Laplacian is computed for each channel.

entries.title: Lattice Deform
entries.summary: Applies grid-based deformation to a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The interpolation method to use between the grid and image. Linear: The deformation follows the grid exactly. Smooth: Use non-uniform rational b-spline (NURBS) interpolation to produce fluid deformation across the grid.

parameters.label: U
parameters.description: The point density in the U-direction when NURBS curves convert into polygons.

parameters.label: V
parameters.description: The point density in the V-direction when NURBS curves convert into polygons.

parameters.label: Cells per Column
parameters.description: The number of grid cells in each column. This value is always one less than the Columns value.

parameters.description: The provided resolution fits the display window. This further expands or erodes the data window to allow overscanning or cropping effects.

parameters.description: The amount to adjust the top and bottom of the data window.

parameters.description: The precision of the layer. NOTE: 16-bit floats lack enough precision for nice derivatives, so you may want to use 32-bit for height workflows. 8-bit: The layer uses 8-bit precision. This is supported only for ID layers. 16-bit: The layer uses 16-bit precision, which uses twice the amount of memory as 8-bit. 32-bit: The layer uses 32-bit precision, which uses twice the amount of memory as 16-bit.

parameters.label: Use Fixed Point Storage
parameters.description: Stores 8-bit unsigned and 16-bit signed floating point values as fixed point values. This clamps 8-bit fixed point values to the 0 to 1 range and 16-bit fixed point values to the -1 to 1 range. This parameter applies to only non-ID layers. Storage types are propagated through the network, so nodes often use the same storage type as their inputs. Fixed point storage offers more consistent precision for the same amount of storage compared to floating point, but can only represent values in a limited range. TIP: Hold ((MMB)) on the node to use the node info window to check the storage type of each layer.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The behavior of the layer when operations read outside of its data window. See Border types for more information. Constant: Treat the border as zero, with the boundary interpolating to black. Clamp: Clamp boundary values, which streaks them outwards. Mirror: Reflect along the boundaries. Wrap: Wrap to the opposite boundary.

parameters.label: Pixel Scale
parameters.description: The number of pixels that fit across one buffer element. This allows for fast proxy cooking without changing measurements specified in pixels. For example, a value of 2 means a 640x480 image has only 320x240 buffer elements to store the data.

parameters.label: Identity Transform
parameters.description: Resets the layer to the canonical space. This moves the layer to the origin, aligns it with the XY plane, and resets its camera properties to the canonical orthographic projection.

entries.title: Layer to Points
entries.summary: Creates points based on a layer.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to create the points from a layer. All Pixel: Create a point for each pixel in the input. Non-Zero Pixels: Create a point if the pixel isn't zero. Count per Pixel: Each pixel stores how many points to create, so create that many points per pixel. Unique Values: Create a point for each unique value in the input layer. If the input layer's integer values are 1, 1, 5, 3, 23, 3, and 5 for example, then the unique values are 1, 5, 3, and 23. This means the node makes four points. This option is useful in workflows such as with the Segment by Connectivity COP where you want to create a point for each segment. Count from First Pixel: The first pixel in the layer stores how many points to create, so create that many points. Count from Last Pixel: The last pixel in the layer stores how many points to create, so create that many points.

parameters.label: Layer Attrib
parameters.description: The name of the integer attribute to set with the value of the pixel that generated the point. This stores the original pixel's value. This parameter is useful when you want to know the original value, such as for non-zero or unique values.

parameters.label: Index Attrib
parameters.description: The name of the integer attribute that stores the raw offset (x + y * xres) of the source pixel in the input layer's buffer. This lets you know where the point came from.

parameters.label: Set Positions
parameters.description: Initializes the position attribute with the pixel location. When off, the position attribute is zero. TIP: Zero attributes don't require memory, so turn this off for optimization if you don't care about the position.

parameters.label: Ignore Minus One
parameters.description: Ignores the layer value -1 when computing unique values. A value of -1 in an ID layer often means an invalid ID, so ignoring it ensures that points are created for only valid IDs. When off, -1 is generated with the unique values.

parameters.label: Point Attributes
parameters.description: The amount of additional point attributes, which are available in later OpenCL nodes. This lets you define the default attributes of the geometry.

parameters.label: Low Order Barrel (k1)
parameters.description: Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>1</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Mid Order Barrel (k2)
parameters.description: Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>2</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: High Order Barrel (k3)
parameters.description: Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>3</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Low Order Inverse (k4)
parameters.description: Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>4</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: Mid Order Inverse (k5)
parameters.description: Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>5</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

parameters.label: High Order Inverse (k6)
parameters.description: Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion. The k<sub>6</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV.

entries.title: Light
entries.summary: Lights a layer given a light direction and normals.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The type of the input normal. Signed (-1 to 1): The input normal layer ranges from -1 to 1 and likely comes from geometry. Offset (0 to 1): The input nomral layer ranges from 0 to 1 and likely comes from a normal map. See Normals for more information.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.description: Directional lights are considered at infinity. All the light rays will be parallel. When points are used as a source, the direction from the points to the origin is the direction of the light. Non-directional lights are point lights emanating from the 3d location.

parameters.label: Light Direction
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, this is the direction pointing to the source light. The magnitude doesn't matter. The default value is 0, 0, 1.

parameters.label: Light Position
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, this is the center of the light when not directional.

parameters.label: Light Radius
parameters.description: Point lights have a singularity at their location, so if a point light is inside a volume it will become infinitely bright at that location. This regularizes the falloff by treating the light to be approximately a sphere of this radius. This will be multiplied by the pscale attribute on points.

parameters.label: Light Color
parameters.description: The color of the light. The default value is 1, 1, 1.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.description: The linear brightness of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: An exponential brightness of the light. Each 1 value higher is 2 times the brightness.

parameters.label: Environment Map Offset
parameters.description: Angle to rotate the environment map around the Y-axis.

parameters.label: Diffuse
parameters.description: A tint for the diffuse colour of the material. The incoming source layer will be multiplied by this to determine the diffuse contribution. Setting to zero can allow the extraction of the pure reflective or specular components.

parameters.label: Specular
parameters.description: A specular color for the material. This will be multiplied by the light color to form the specular color in light models that have specular, such as Phong.

parameters.label: Metallic
parameters.description: The amount of metallicity of the material. Increasing metallicity will lower the diffuse value and replace it with a reflected color.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The lighting model to shade with. Lambertian: An ideal matte surface. Wrapped Diffuse: An extension of the Lambertian model, but allowing the specification of the terminator position. This allows the light to "wrap" around the surface and light the back half - this is useful for non-physical effects, especially for toon-shading pipelines where the light is further processed. Phong: The Phong Reflection model, developed by Bui Tuong Phong, is a simple breakdown of light into a specular and diffuse component. The exponent controls how sharp the specular effect is.

parameters.label: Terminator
parameters.description: Where the terminator of the Wrapped Diffuse should lie. -1 will make it entirely black, 0 will be at the half way part and so match Lambertian shading, and 1 will wrap all the way to the far side of the object.

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.description: The tightness of the specular lobe in the Phong model.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: A layer to perform lighting on.

inputs.label: normal
inputs.description: An RGB layer providing the surface normal. Its normal type, offset or signed, must match the normal type of this node.

inputs.label: pos
inputs.description: Instead of using the location of the source pixel in world space; this RGB input's value is used.

inputs.label: metallic
inputs.description: A scale multiplier to the metallic value, the metallic parameter likely should be set to 1 for this to have an effect

inputs.label: vieworigin
inputs.description: Instead of using the source input, this layer provides a ray direction for each output pixel. This is required for Phong and metallic shading.

inputs.label: points
inputs.description: An optional Geometry whose points will be treated as light sources. For positional lights their positions are used, otherwise their direction to the origin is used as a direction. When wired the corresponding direction or position parameters will be unused.

inputs.label: envmap
inputs.description: An optional RGB layer storing the environment map in polar coordinates.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: lit
outputs.description: The final lit layer.

parameters.description: A string that describes a configuration for the video source. The configuration must be supported by the video source in order to be used. Since the configuration is dependent on the source, the source parameter must be specified before the configuration. The format is: {format}:{xres}x{yres}@{framerate}

parameters.label: Connect to Source
parameters.description: When enabled, a connection is established to the video source. When disabled, the connection is terminated. The value of this parameter is not saved in the hip file due to privacy concerns and must therefore be re-enabled whenever opening the hip file.

parameters.label: Live Stream
parameters.description: When Connect to Source is on, this turns on live streaming to provide an interactive, non-deterministic streaming mode. It streams independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Stream doesn't save the results like other streaming types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Stream

entries.title: Logic
entries.summary: Applies logic operations to ID layers.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: For ID layers, if the final mask is greater than 0.5, the new value is used. Otherwise the original value is used. The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Function Class
parameters.description: Selects the high-level category of logic functions to perform. Logic: Expose boolean logic operators. Comparison: Expose comparison operators. Bit Shift: Expose bit shifting operators. Bit Twiddle: Expose bit-twiddling operators that enable low-level control of individual bits.

parameters.label: Logic
parameters.description: Boolean logical functions. In logical mode, 0 is false and any other value is true. In bitwise mode, the individual bits are processed independently. A: Output the A input. B: Output the B input. And: True if A and B are both true. Or: True either A or B are true. Exclusive Or: True only if A or B are true, but not both.

parameters.label: True If
parameters.description: Equal to each other (==): True if the A and B are equal. Not equal to each other (!=): True if the A and B are unequal. A greater than B (>): True if A is greater than B. A greater than or equal to B (>=): True if A is greater than or equal to B. B greater than A (<): True if B is greater than A. B greater than or equal to A (<=): True if B is greater than or equal to A.

parameters.label: Bit Shift
parameters.description: This shifts the bits of the A input. Shift Right Arithmetic: Shift the bits right by the B value. The sign of the number will be preserved. Shift Right Logical: Shift the bits right by the B value. Zeros will be shifted in from the left, so the number will be treated as unsigned. Shift Left: Shift the bits left by the B value. Rotate Right: Rotate the bits right by the B value. Bits that fall off the right side will be moved to the left. Rotate Left: Rotate the bits left by the B value. Bits that fall off the left side will be moved to the right.

parameters.label: Bit Twiddle
parameters.description: Specific operations to manipulate individual bits. Is Bit Set: True if the Bth bit in A is set. Set Bit: Outputs A with the Bth bit set. Clear Bit: Outputs A with the Bth bit cleared. Toggle Bit: Outputs A with the Bth bit toggled. Count Set Bits: Output the number of set bits in A. Leading Zeros: Output the number of leading zeros in A. (A * B) >> 32: Multiply A and B together and shift right by 32. This returns the high component of the multiplication that normally is lost due to overflow.

parameters.label: Operate Bitwise
parameters.description: Boolean operations will operate per-bit rather than logically.

parameters.label: All Bits Set for True
parameters.description: A true result normally is 1, and a false 0. This instead will have the true value have all the 1s set, which usually is -1. This is useful for masking operations.

parameters.label: Not A
parameters.description: Complement the value of A before doing the operation.

parameters.label: Not B
parameters.description: Complement the value of B before doing the operation.

parameters.label: Not Result
parameters.description: Complement the result of the operation.

parameters.label: Default B Value
parameters.description: If B is unwired, this is the value used for B.

inputs.label: A
inputs.description: An ID layer or integer VDB or attribute for the A input.

inputs.label: B
inputs.description: An ID layer or integer VDB or attribute for the B input.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: A Mono layer or integer VDB or attribute for whether to output the result of the operation or the original A value.

outputs.label: logic
outputs.description: An ID layer or integer VDB or attribute with the result of the logic operation.

entries.title: LOP Network
entries.summary: The top level container node for networks of LOP nodes.
entries.overview: This node contains a network of LOP nodes used to generate a USD scene.

parameters.label: Expansion Effect
parameters.description: Controls how the scene graph tree expansion state affects the display of the scene in the viewport. All expansion effect modes require that your scene graph be authored with a valid model hierarchy, expressing prim kinds at every level down to the component level. If the model hierarchy doesn't exist or is invalid, the scene graph tree expansion will have no effect. Once a component prim is visible in the scne graph tree, the viewport will render the component's full geometry. The expansion effect does not operate on individual meshes inside a component. Do Nothing: The expansion state has no effect on the viewport. Visibility: Prims not exposed in the scene graph tree are marked as invisible. This mode works with any render delegate, but provides no visual feedback at all for the invisible prims. Bounding Box Draw Mode: Prims not exposed in the scene graph tree are drawn as bounding boxes. Not all render delegates respect the USD draw mode setting, and so may do nothing in this mode. Expanding a scene graph tree branch in this mode, if the newly exposed prims are groups, will cause a separate bounding box to be drawn for each child prim to replace the single larger bounding box that encapsulates the entire parent prim.

parameters.label: Modified Prim Count To Start New Layer
parameters.description: Having active layers with large numbers of opinions can result in slower than expected interactivity when editing a LOP network. Setting this parameter will cause all LOP nodes inside this network to automatically create a new active layer if their input node modifies more than the specified number of prims (as determined by looking at the node's Last Modified Prims).

parameters.label: Favorite Primitives
parameters.description: Specifies a list of primitives that should appear in the Favorites folder of the scene graph tree. This parameter does not support primitive pattern syntax. It must be a simple list of full primitive paths.

parameters.label: Resolver Context Asset Path
parameters.description: This file path is used to create the asset resolver context of any USD stage created by a LOP node inside the network, unless the LOP node explicitly specifies a different resolver context asset path.

parameters.label: Number of Resolver Context Strings
parameters.description: The resolver context can be configured using multiple separate strings. Each string is used to configure one resolver. One string (with no URL prefix specified) is sent to the default resolver used for all asset paths that are not in URL format. Other strings can be paired with a URL prefix to configure the resolver associated with that prefix. If there is at least one non-empty resolver context string value provided, this takes precedence over any resolver context asset path, and the resolver context for the LOP stage will be created using the ArResolver::CreateContextFromStrings method instead of ArResolver::CreateDefaultContextForAsset. Enable: Individual resolver context configuration strings can be enabled or disabled with this toggle. URL Prefix: This string value will be sent to the resolver responsible for the specified URL prefix. If no prefix is provided, this string value will be sent to the default resolver. Value: The string value sent to the resolver determined by the URL Prefix.

parameters.label: Number of Variant Selection Fallback Rules
parameters.description: Configures what variant selection fallback values to use for specific variant sets when no explicit variant selection opinion is provided on a prim. These fallbacks are applied on top of any global variant selection fallbacks configured using the USD library plugin mechanism. Variant selection fallbacks set with a Configure Stage LOP will be higher priority than these LOP Network settings. Enable: A specific variant set fallback setting can be disabled with this toggle. Variant Set Name: Name of the variant set to configure. Fallback Selections: A space or comma separated list of variant selection values to attempt to use on this variant set when no explicit variant selection opinion is available.

parameters.label: Insertion Point Descriptor
parameters.description: Indicates the descriptor used to find the insertion point on the current cook path.

parameters.label: Render Gallery Source
parameters.description: The path to the render gallery database for this LOP Network. This value is not used until the render gallery is opened within this LOP Network.

entries.title: Mask Combine
entries.summary: Combines several mask layers from an input cable into a single mask.

parameters.label: Starting Value
parameters.description: The starting mask value that the first layer blends onto. The layers in Mask Layers are combined onto this value in order.

parameters.label: Mask Layers
parameters.description: Each entry in this list combines one wire from the input cable onto the running mask. The layers are processed from top to bottom.

parameters.label: Wire Name
parameters.description: Turns the layer on or off. When off, the layer is skipped and doesn't contribute to the combined mask.

parameters.label: Wire Name
parameters.description: The name of the wire in the input cable to combine. A valid layer must be either Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA type.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: How this layer is combined with the running result. See the Blend COP for full descriptions of each mode (the running mask and the current layer are the background and foreground blend inputs, respectively). Blend: Replaces the running result with this layer. Add: Adds this layer to the running result. Subtract: Subtracts this layer from the running result. Multiply: Multiplies the running result by this layer. Divide: Divides the running result by this layer. Screen: Acts as a saturating add, much like adding photographs. Hypot: Takes the length of the vector formed by this layer and the running result. Difference: Takes the absolute difference between this layer and the running result. Exclusion: A lower contrast version of Difference. Sharpen: Increases the contrast of the running result using this layer as the mid-point contrast value. Maximum: Takes the maximum of this layer and the running result. Minimum: Takes the minimum of this layer and the running result. Overlay: Switches between Multiply and Screen based on the value of the running result. Areas below 0.5 multiply and areas above 0.5 screen. SoftLight: Applies a smooth contrast to the running result according to the value of this layer. HardLight: Switches between Multiply and Screen based on the value of this layer. Areas below 0.5 multiply and areas above 0.5 screen. Dodge: Lightens the running result according to this layer's value. Burn: Darkens the running result according to this layer's value.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of this layer to mix into the running result. Higher values mix in more of the layer. A value of 1 applies the blend fully.

parameters.label: Conversion
parameters.description: How a multi-channel wire (such as UV, RGB, or RGBA) is reduced to a mono value before blending. Channel Extract: Uses a single channel of the wire as the mask. Channel Mix: Combines the channels using a weighted sum. Light Direction: Treats the wire as a normal map and computes the mask from how much each normal faces a given light direction.

parameters.label: Channel to Extract
parameters.description: The channel to use as the mask when Conversion is Channel Extract.

parameters.label: X Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Red (x) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: Y Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Green (y) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: Z Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Blue (z) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: W Weight
parameters.description: The weight of the Alpha (w) channel when Conversion is Channel Mix.

parameters.label: Normalize Weights
parameters.description: Divides the channel mix by the sum of the weights so the result keeps the same overall range. Turn this off to use the weights as raw multipliers.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: How the normal values are encoded when Conversion is Light Direction. Signed (-1 to 1): The channels store normal components directly in the -1 to 1 range. Offset (0 to 1): The channels store normal components remapped into the 0 to 1 range, as is common for normal maps.

parameters.label: Light Direction
parameters.description: The direction the light comes from when Conversion is Light Direction. Normals facing this direction produce higher mask values.

parameters.label: Terminator
parameters.description: Shifts the boundary between the lit and unlit sides of the surface when Conversion is Light Direction.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Blurs the layer before it's blended in, softening its edges.

parameters.label: Layer Remap
parameters.description: Remaps this layer's values through a ramp before blending, letting you reshape its contrast or invert it.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Combined Mask Remap
parameters.description: Remaps the combined mask through a ramp, letting you reshape the final result after all layers are blended.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

inputs.label: layers
inputs.description: The cable carrying the layers to combine. The Mask Layers list picks named wires from this cable.

outputs.label: mask
outputs.description: The combined output mask.

entries.title: Mask from Curves
entries.summary: Creates a mask from 2D curves.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The output type. Mask: Output a mask with white inside the curves and black outside the curves. SDF: Output the distance from the closed curves as a signed distance field (SDF).

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the outgoing mask or SDF, which reverses the inside sense of the curves. This does not affect the id values.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: Applies a postprocess blur to the mask output that softens the edges.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The units to use for blurring the mask. Image: Specify the blur in image space. Pixels: Specify the blur in absolute pixels.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the mask blur in image space or pixels, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Conversion Quality
parameters.description: How well to convert NURBs and Bezier into polygons. Higher values result in smoother conversions but require more time.

parameters.label: Resample
parameters.description: Resamples the incoming polygons so they have equal-spaced points. This can reduce dense geometry or add smoothness to low resolution curves.

parameters.label: Segment Length
parameters.description: The size in world space to resample each edge of the input curves.

parameters.label: Treat Polygons As
parameters.description: Set the new points along an implicit curve. Refining a polygon normally has little effect on the smoothness of the curve since the new points lie on the edges. Straight Edges: New points lie along the original curve's edges. Subdivision Curves: New points treat the original curves as control points of a B-spline. Interpolating Curves: New points follow a B-spline that interpolates the original points. This helps keep the size of the curve, but might introduce overshoots and oscillations.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: The layer onto which to render the curves. If the curves aren't on the layer directly, they're projected by the layer's camera.

inputs.label: curves
inputs.description: The geometry with the curves to rasterize. If the curves are open, the node first closes them.

outputs.label: mask
outputs.description: The layer with a black and white mask of the rendered curves or with an SDF that stores the distance to the curves. This is set by the Output Type parameter.

outputs.label: id
outputs.description: The ID layer that stores which curve number contributed to the pixel. -1 is used where no curve contributed. NOTE: The Blur parameter may have non-zero mask values with no IDs.

entries.title: Mirror
entries.summary: Mirrors an image based on an arbitrary number of planes.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The method you use to specify and configure the number of mirror planes. Number and Offset (default): Set the total number of mirror planes and the angle between and offset of each plane. Custom Mirror Planes: Add a custom number of mirror planes and a custom angle and offset for each plane.

parameters.label: Number of Planes
parameters.description: When Mode is Number and Offset, this is the total number of mirror planes to apply. The Angle parameter values are cumulative. The default value is 1.

parameters.label: Mirrors
parameters.description: When Mode is Custom Mirror Planes, this is the number of mirror planes to apply. The node sequentially performs mirroring, applying the Angle and Offset parameters from the first to the last in the list. The default value is 1.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: When Mode is Number and Offset, this is the angle (in degrees) between each mirror plane. When Mode is Custom Mirror Planes, this is the angle (in degrees) of the mirror plane. Positive values mirror the left side of the image. Negative values mirror the right side of the image. When Mode is Number and Offset: * This parameter's value is cumulative. For example, setting this parameter to 20 and Number of Planes to 3 equates to having three planes respectively set to 20, 40, and 60 degrees. * You can set this parameter as an expression (such as -180/ch("numberplanes")) for procedural radial symmetry to make sure you always output a circle. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: When Mode is Number and Offset, this is the amount (in image space) of perpendicular offset from the origin. When Mode is Custom Mirror Planes, this is the amount (in image space) to perpendicularly offset the mirror plane along the image. Positive values move the mirror plane towards the right side of the image. Negative values move the mirror plane towards the left side of the image. The default value is 0.

parameters.label: Reverse Mirror Plane Direction
parameters.description: Flips the Mirror Plane. For example, an angle of 180 is equal to an angle of 0 with Reverse Mirror Plane Direction on.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer to which you apply the mirrors.

outputs.label: mirror
outputs.description: The mirrored source layer.

entries.title: Mono
entries.summary: Converts a layer, VDB, or attribute into a mono, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The method used to combine the source channels into the final value. The standard channel extension rules apply unless specified otherwise. NOTE: Some luminance methods assume a source color space. No implicit conversion is done from your scene_linear to this space. SGI Luminance: This is a historical luminance computation used in Houdini, which is believed to originate with SGI. lum = 0.3086 * red + 0.6094 * green + 0.0820 * blue NTSC Luminance: The standard NTSC luminance computation, which is a common luminance option. lum = 0.299 * red + 0.587 * green + 0.114 * blue HDTV Luminance: The HDTV standard luminance from BT 709. lum = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue Average: An average of the channels. Maximum Channel: The maximum of the channels. Minimum Channel: The minimum of the channels. Magnitude / Length: The length of the vector formed by taking the channels as components. For a mono input, this is the absolute value. Hue: Convert to HSV and return the hue channel. Saturation: Convert to HSV and return the saturation channel. Value: Convert to HSV and return the value channel. Red: Extract the red, or x, channel. Green: Extract the green, or y, channel. Blue: Extract the blue, or z, channel. entries.title: Neural Cellular Automata Core
entries.summary: Runs a neural cellular automata model to evolve cell states.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The NCA model preset to use. This sets the model file path and any other parameters stored in the recipe simultaneously.

parameters.label: Initialize Cells
parameters.description: Outputs an initialized cell state without running the NCA model. Use this to create the starting state for a cellular automata simulation. NOTE: This parameter helps provide the correct input cable when running the model in a block.

parameters.label: NCA Model File
parameters.description: The path to an ONNX model file for the NCA.

parameters.label: Reload Model
parameters.description: Forces a reload of the ONNX model file.

parameters.label: Model Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times the NCA model is applied per cook. Higher values evolve the cell state further but take longer to compute. TIP: When growing textures on meshes with adjacency information, use the Neural Cellular Automata Block recipe with this parameter set to a low value. Make use of the block's own iterations or simulate over time to make sure the adjacency information is used frequently to update the solve between model iterations.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: A seed value that controls the stochastic update mask.

parameters.label: Update Rate
parameters.description: The fraction of cells to update each iteration, in the range 0.1 to 0.9. Lower values update fewer cells per step, producing a more gradual evolution. Use the seed to change the random number generation, affecting which cells get updated. This can be used to generate variations of the overall pattern.

parameters.label: Update Mask Type
parameters.description: Controls how the update mask is applied to each cell. Amplitude-Weighted: The update is scaled by the incoming 0-1 mask, but the likelihood of an update is still only controlled by the seed. This produces smoother gradual evolution. Probabilistic: The update is always applied fully, but the 0-1 mask drives the probability of an update occurring in the first place. This creates noisier evolution, but pronounces the cell-based underlying structure.

parameters.label: Cell Rotation
parameters.description: Applies a rotation in turns to the cell perception kernel, where a value of 1 is a full rotation (360°). This is added on top of the per-cell rotation coming from the rotation input.

parameters.label: Cell Scale
parameters.description: Applies a scale to the cell perception gradient. This is multiplied with the per-cell scale coming from the scale input. The final scale is clamped to the range 0.2 to 1 to avoid exploding gradients. You can use values above 1 to multiply a small input scale mask up towards the upper bound of the valid range, but the values are limited by the internal clamping.

parameters.label: World Space Direction
parameters.description: When an adjacency cable is connected, this is the world space direction vector used as an up vector when computing the cell rotation adjacency information. With the default value of (0,1,0), the pattern on the geometry matches the pattern on a 2D layer in the origin when looking along the Z axis.

parameters.label: Size Ref Scale
parameters.description: A scale factor applied to the size_ref input resolution to determine the working resolution of the NCA. Lower fractions reduce memory usage and computation time. 1/1: Full resolution. 1/2: Half resolution. 1/4: Quarter resolution. 1/8: Eighth resolution.

parameters.label: Execution Provider
parameters.description: Determines which ONNX execution provider to use for inference. By default, the node attempts to pick the best available provider and prefers to use GPU acceleration. Automatic:

parameters.label: Device ID
parameters.description: This parameter can be used to specify which GPU to use for inference when multiple GPUs are available. It has no effect when using CPU inference.

inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.description: The input cell state to evolve.

inputs.label: updatemask
inputs.description: An optional mask that controls cell updates each iteration.

inputs.description: An optional per-cell rotation map.

inputs.label: scale
inputs.description: An optional per-cell scale map.

inputs.label: adjacency

outputs.description: The evolved cell state.

parameters.label: Model

This automatically matches the decoder to the model used by the upstream Node:cop/neural_cellularautomatacore. NOTE: This is the default setting. In this mode, the node looks for the decodemodel string layer property to know from where it should load the decoder ONNX model file. parameters.description: The factor by which to upsample the cell states before decoding. 1x: No upressing, just decoding 2x: 2 times the input resolution. 4x: 4 times the input resolution. 8x: 8 times the input resolution.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter used when upsampling the incoming cell states. See Filters for more information. Point: Sets the pixel value to the pixel value of the nearest neighbor. Bilinear: Sets the pixel value through bilinear interpolation. Box: Sets the pixel value through a box filter, done by sampling all pixels within a box on the original image's matching pixel. Bartlett: Sets the pixel value through interpolating according to a triangular window or a Bartlett window, taking each pixel as a sample of this signal. Catmull-Rom: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Catmull-Rom spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter. Mitchell: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Mitchell-Netravali filter. B-spline: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the B-spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter.

This controls the range of the values and whether they're in respect to the input's display or data window. Image: Specify coordinates in terms of the display window, with a range of -1 to 1. Texture: Specify coordinates in terms of the data window, with a range of 0 to 1. Pixels: Specify coordinates in pixels as integers.
