entries.title: Phasor Noise
entries.summary: Generates phasor noise, which resembles a wave pattern.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source outputs. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See Type info for more information.

parameters.label: Rotate Channel
parameters.description: When Signature is any channel except Mono, this is the amount to rotate the noise in the additional channels. Each layer is rotated by a different angle offset. When set to 0, the output image is equivalent to when the Signature is Mono. For example, when Signature is RGBA, the node generates four separate phasor noises that each have a unique rotation.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the Center adjustment. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 0.25. NOTE: Layers can store negative numbers and values above 1, so this may result in out-of-bounds values. You can use a Clamp COP to enforce the range afterwards.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of 0.5 makes a pixel value of 0.5 become 1.

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the Amplitude and Center parameters. You can use this parameter to make the noise more extreme without exceeding the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: Sets the type of noise and, when set to Phasor Wave, the periodic function (wave type). Phasor Wave: Consists of the Sine, Rectangle, and Saw profiles. These provide consistent wave patterns across the entire surface. Phasor Noise: Defined by the Gabor Noise. It has a sharper shape than the Gabor Noise. Gabor Noise: The result of summing the phasor kernel values. This means overlapping kernel regions either amplify or cancel each other out. These overlapping areas create softened gray, ripple patterns. Intensity Field: The set of intensity values that define the Phasor Wave and Gabor Noise, which outputs soft ripple patterns with varying wave widths. This type can create more organic, natural-looking forms than the other noise types. When set to Phasor Wave, you can choose one of the following periodic functions: Sine: Sets the periodic function as the sine function. This creates smooth contrast transitions between the top and bottom peaks. Rectangle: Sets the periodic function as a rectangular function. This creates distinct black-and-white regions, resulting in vivid, cartoon-like wave patterns. Saw: Sets the periodic function as a sawtooth function. This creates a linear contrast transition from the top to bottom peak, sharply emphasizing both extremes.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: The size of the wave's width in the noise. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter. WARNING: This parameter can output undesired results if you use values outside the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio. NOTE: If on, values for parameters like Element Size are rounded or clamped to make them valid. This is because these types of parameters must meet certain conditions for the noise to be tileable.

parameters.label: Wave Bias
parameters.description: When Type is Phasor Wave, this is the peak position of each periodic function. When a bias input is wired in, that value is used instead of the Wave Bias.

parameters.label: Blending Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the phasor kernels. Higher values increase the radius of the phasor kernels so they overlap more, while lower values decrease their radius so there is more space between each kernel.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The seed that the random number generator uses. Change this parameter to generate a new position for the kernels.

parameters.label: Kernels
parameters.description: The number of disk-shaped local regions where the primary sine and cosine waves are defined.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the input image. Blurring results in a softened bias boundary.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The strength of bias blending. When set to 0, this displays the original noise and doesn't apply bias blending.

parameters.label: Blur
parameters.description: The amount to blur the input image. Blurring results in a softened scale boundary.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The strength of scale blending. When set to 0, this displays the original noise and doesn't apply scale blending.

parameters.label: 3D Noise
parameters.description: Evaluates the noise in a 3D space. Use these parameters to control the third dimension, while the first two dimensions are the location in the image.

parameters.label: Animate
parameters.description: Implicitly adds time to the third coordinate.

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: The interval length (in seconds) of the noise's pulse in the third dimension. Lower values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while higher values decrease this rate.

parameters.label: Time Offset
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that's added to the start frame.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) by which to multiply the start frame. Higher values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while lower values decrease this rate.

parameters.label: Loop Length (sec)
parameters.description: This is the time (in seconds) at which to repeat the noise. This clamps other options to enforce periodic behavior. Turn this on to generate animations that seamlessly loop. When off, the animation generally doesn't repeat after any amount of time.

parameters.label: Rotate Pattern
parameters.description: The amount to rotate the phasor kernels. When Uniform, this sets a uniform initial angle for each phasor kernel. When Set Varying, this lets you set Rotation Varying to randomize the initial angle of each phasor kernel. NOTE: Each phasor kernel has a certain angle. As kernels are rotated, the noise pattern is rotated. Since kernel intersections change depending on the rotation, it behaves differently from a standard image rotation.

parameters.label: Rotation Varying
parameters.description: When Rotate Pattern is Set Varying, this is the randomized initial angle of phasor kernels. When set to 0, the value displays uniformed initial angles.

parameters.label: Use Secondary Rotation
parameters.description: Sets secondary phasor kernels at the same location of the initial phasor kernels.

parameters.label: Rotate Pattern
parameters.description: The amount to rotate the additional phasor kernels. When Uniform, this sets a uniform initial angle for each secondary phasor kernel. When Set Varying, this lets you set Rotation Varying to randomize the initial angle of each secondary phasor kernel.

parameters.label: Rotation Varying
parameters.description: When Rotate Pattern is Set Varying, this is the randomized initial angle of the secondary phasor kernels. When set to 0, the value displays uniformed initial angles.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of -2 becomes 2. NOTE: This parameter doesn't impact the output when there's only positive values.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value x to 1 - x. NOTE: This method works for values in the 0 to 1 range. For images outside of this range, using Complement results in negative or out of range values.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) towards zero (if Bias is less than 1) or one (if Bias is greater than 1). A bias value of 0.5 doesn't affect the values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around 0.5) together, while values around 0 and 1 are pulled apart. A gain value of 0.5 doesn't affect the noise values. Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than 1 increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than 1 stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if Contrast is less than 1) or away from (if Contrast is greater than 1) medium grey values (around 0.5). NOTE: This is not the same as Noise Contrast, which appears in some noise nodes and applies contrast during the noise function.

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

inputs.label: pos
inputs.description: An optional UV layer with a value that's used instead of the pixel's image coordinates for the noise.

inputs.label: time
inputs.description: An optional layer with a value that each pixel uses for the time.

inputs.label: bias
inputs.description: An optional layer with a value that's used for the peak position of each periodic function of the Phasor Wave noise type. When wired in, this value is used instead of the Wave Bias. Use the Bias parameters to blur this value.

inputs.label: scale
inputs.description: An optional layer with a value that's multiplied by the Element Size. Use the Scale parameters to blur this value.

inputs.label: direction
inputs.description: An optional UV layer to set the initial angle of phasor kernels.

outputs.label: noise
outputs.description: The computed noise.

entries.title: Pixelate
entries.summary: Increases the size of pixels to pixelate an input layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The method used to determine the amount of pixel blocks. Block Size: Set the size of each pixel block to determine how many appear along the X and Y-axes. Number of Blocks: Set the amount of pixel blocks that can appear along the X and Y-axes.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: When Mode is Block Size, this is the unit of measurement used to determine the Block Size. Image: Sets the block size to use image space units. Pixels: Sets the block size to use pixels.

parameters.label: Block Size
parameters.description: The size in image coordinates or pixels of the resulting pixel block, which determines how many blocks appear along the X and Y-axes. You can turn on the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button to adjust this further using the Element Scale parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.description: When the Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms Per-Component Controls button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for the pixel block.

parameters.label: Number of Blocks
parameters.description: The amount of pixel blocks that can appear along the X and Y-axes across the image space. NOTE: The node outputs less blocks than the set amount if the input layer doesn't expand across the entire image space.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size (in image space) by which to multiply the input layer's original pixels before they're pixelated.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to offset the input layer's pixels before quantizing their position.

parameters.label: Pre-Blur
parameters.description: Blurs the input layer's pixels before they're pixelated.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: The unit of measurement that the Blur COP in the node's subnetwork uses to determine the size of the blur effect's radius. Image: Sets the blur radius to use image space units. Pixels: Sets the blur radius to use pixels.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the blur effect's radius in image space or pixels, which the Units parameter determines.

parameters.label: Scale Size
parameters.description: The amount to scale the blur effect's radius.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The layer to pixelate.

inputs.label: effect
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel scaling amount of the Block Size parameter.

inputs.label: offset
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel addition to the Offset parameter.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: pixelate
outputs.description: The pixelated source layer.

outputs.label: blockid
outputs.description: An ID layer that contains a unique ID for each pixel block.

entries.title: Planar Inflate
entries.summary: Inflates a 2D SDF into a height layer.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: Controls the final height profile of the inflated region. Higher positive values create a fuller, more raised shape. Negative values invert the height direction.

parameters.label: Pre Scale
parameters.description: The base inflation amount before the height is solved. Higher values increase the strength of the inflation source.

parameters.label: Noise Scale
parameters.description: The amount of wrinkle and mound noise to add to the inflation source.

parameters.label: Use Wrinkle
parameters.description: Adds fine phasor-noise wrinkle detail to the inflated surface.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the wrinkle pattern. Lower values create smaller, tighter wrinkles.

parameters.label: Boundary Blend
parameters.description: The amount to blend the wrinkle scale near the SDF boundary. Higher values make the wrinkle pattern respond more strongly to the boundary.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The random seed for the wrinkle pattern.

parameters.label: Use Mounds
parameters.description: Adds broader fractal-noise mound detail to the inflated surface.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the mound pattern. Lower values create smaller mounds.

parameters.label: Max Octaves

entries.title: Prefix Sum
entries.summary: Computes the prefix sum of a layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The direction of the scan. +X: Scan along positive X, which is horizontally from left to right. -X: Scan along negative X, which is horizontally from right to left. +Y: Scan along positive Y, which is vertically from bottom to top. -Y: Scan along negative Y, which is vertically from top to bottom. +X+Y: Scan in a meandering path from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner. This means the steps alternate between moving in the positive X direction and then in the positive Y direction. Linear: Scan from the left to right and bottom to top, starting from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner. This means each horizontal scanline is aggregated before moving on to the next one.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The operation to apply to the elements of the sequence. Add: Add all elements of the sequence together. Minimum: Return the smallest element in the sequence. Maximum: Return the largest element in the sequence. Count: Return the number of elements in the sequence.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scale the prefix sum by the pixel size. This ensures the summation is independent either of resolution or during proxy cooking. This parameter applies to only non-integer summation. The scale factor changes depending on whether X or Y passes of the prefix sum are present. It's scaled by the horizontal factor if there's an X pass, the vertical factor if there's a Y pass, or the horizontal and vertical factors if there's both an X and Y pass. None: Don't perform scaling. Pixel: Divide the values by the pixel scale. This means the values remain the same when proxy-resolution cooking is used. Texture: Divide the values by the texture size of a buffer element. This causes a constant pixel value of 1 for the data window to sum to 1. This is often an anistropic scale for non-square images. See /copernicus/spaces for more information. Image: Divide the values by the image size of the buffer elements. This causes a constant pixel value of 1 for the image to sum to 2. This summation is independent of the data window, so it stays the same when a tile is cropped out. See /copernicus/spaces for more information.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer from which to compute the prefix sum.

inputs.label: active
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel active map that determines which values to take into account when computing the statistics. Values over 0.5 are active while values below 0.5 are inactive.

outputs.label: prefixsum
outputs.description: The prefix sum of the original layer.

entries.title: Pyro Advect
entries.summary: Advects VDBs by Velocity.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: A global scale on the velocity values.

parameters.label: Ambient Velocity
parameters.description: A constant global velocity that the VDBs are also moved by, in addition to the values in the velocity VDB. This can be used as a wind effect, since it allows the wind to alter speed without affecting local dynamics.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the velocity values by the timestep.

parameters.label: Trace Method
parameters.description: Controls the integration scheme used for a single trace step through the velocity field. This setting determines how closely the smoke follows turbulent flows and how well the simulation preserves detail over time. Options in this menu are listed in order of increasing accuracy and computational cost. Forward Euler: Predicts the next position based on its current velocity using a straight line. This is a 1st-order accurate method that has the fastest computation time, but it introduces more numerical diffusion, making the smoke look blurrier and can flatten turbulent flows. Average of Two: Predicts the future position, looks at the velocity there, and averages it with the current velocity. It is a step up from Euler, which helps smoke maintain its volume and shape during simple rotations. Explicit Midpoint: Samples the fluid velocity at a half-step forward to determine the full-step move. This is better at capturing vorticity (swirling). It prevents particles from spiraling outward away from the center of a vortex. Runge-Kutta 3: A 3rd-order method that takes three samples of the velocity field to calculate the path. Use this when you need high-fidelity "wispy" smoke details without the full performance hit of RK4. Runge-Kutta 4: A 4th-order method that samples the velocity field four times to find the most accurate "curve" through the fluid. This is essential for complex, turbulent simulations. It minimizes energy loss, ensuring that small eddies and swirls don't disappear prematurely.

parameters.label: Path Tracing
parameters.description: A single trace step is often not enough to preserve sharp details, wispy tendrils, and small vortices through turbulent or fast-moving velocity flows. When this is turned on, multiple trace steps (given by Trace Method) are taken to better predict the curved path through the velocity field. The number of steps depends on the Maximum Steps and the CFL Condition.

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: Global clamp on how many path tracing steps can be performed. For extremely fast motion this may need to be increased, but it might be better to raise the CFL condition instead.

parameters.label: CFL Condition
parameters.description: Controls how large a step should be used when tracing through the velocity field. This is approximately how many voxels will be stepped during a single trace step. Lower values mean better stability, but lower performance. Higher values force the tracing to take larger steps, allowing it to finish faster.

parameters.label: Adaptive Step Size
parameters.description: When turned on, this dynamically changes the given step size through each tracing step, based on the number of maximum steps.

parameters.label: Scheme
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#method

parameters.label: Sharpen
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#sharpen

parameters.label: Enable Velocity Advection
parameters.description: The velocity VDB has to be advected specially, since it advects with respect to itself. It has its own controls, and can be turned off if you do not need to advect it. For example, if it has already been advected by another Pyro Advect COP.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#method

parameters.label: Sharpen
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#sharpen

inputs.description: A cable of all the VDBs to advect.

inputs.label: v
inputs.description: A vector VDB to advect the data VDBs by. Can also be optionally self-advected.

outputs.label: data
outputs.description: A cable of all the advected VDBs.

outputs.label: v
outputs.description: The vector VDB of the velocity, possibly self-advected.

entries.title: Pyro Advect by Map
entries.summary: Advects a VDB by a flow map.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Scheme
parameters.description: The method used to advect the VDB. BFECC: Perform backwards-forward error correction. This requires considerable time and memory, but does the best job of preserving the sharpness of features. Euler + Sharpen: Combines the simplest form of advection with a dynamic sharpen field that combats the diffusion introduced by the trilinear operation. Euler: The simplest and fastest form of advection, but tends to cause excessive blurring.

parameters.label: Sharpen
parameters.description: How much to sharpen the VDB. This is automatically adjusted per voxel based on how the VDB was sampled. While the sharpening kernel is clamped, a value that is too high will create grid artifacts.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: A vector or float VDB to advect.

inputs.label: fwdmap
inputs.description: A vector VDB map defining where voxels came from during forward advection.

inputs.label: revmap
inputs.description: A vector VDB map defining where voxels came from during backwards advection.

outputs.label: advect
outputs.description: The source advected.

entries.title: Pyro Axis Force
entries.summary: Applies a force around an axis to a velocity VDB.
entries.overview: The Pyro Axis Force node exerts a force around a specified line segment. The force can be applied to a vector VDB representing velocities, and can cause the velocities to do the following: - Move toward or away from the axis (_suction_ component) - Travel along the line segment (_axis_ component) - Spin around the axis (_orbit_ component) NOTE: _Axis_ and _orbit_ forces directly modify the velocity vectors, but the _suction_ force works on the output div Float VDB. This relies on wiring the div to the Pyro Block End COP's divergence input. _Axis_ and _orbit_ forces are applied in a cylindrical region around the line segment. Within this tube, a _speed_ is prescribed for each force, along with a _strength_ value. The Pyro Axis Force COP tries to drive the velocity field toward the goal vectors based on the _speed_, and the _strength_ determines how hard the force will work to reach this goal.

parameters.label: Start
parameters.description: Starting point of the line segment. This line segment is the axis for the force.

parameters.label: End
parameters.description: End point of the line segment. This line segment is the axis for the force.

parameters.label: Influence Distance
parameters.description: The forces are applied in a cylindrical region around the line segment. This parameter controls the radius of this cylinder. Increasing this value will extend the active region of this force.

parameters.label: Global Strength
parameters.description: A global strength multiplier for the force. _Suction_, _axis_, and _orbit_ components are affected by this strength. Increase this parameter to uniformly amplify the effect of this node.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the _axis_ and _orbit_ forces are applied to the velocity field. Directional Drag splits the incoming velocity vector into components that point in the axial and orbital directions, then modifies these parts independently. If one of the forces has 0 strength, this mode leaves the respective velocity component unchanged (this includes the part of the velocity vectors that point at the line segment). Full Drag first assembles the full goal velocity, then drives the incoming vectors toward the goal. When set to Force, the goal velocities instead act like an additive force. That is, the goal velocities are multiplied by the applicable strength, then scaled by the timestep, and added to the destination field. NOTE: Directional Drag and Full Drag define a goal velocity field in the active cylinder, then drive the incoming velocity values toward this goal. These modes are stable. They will not overshoot the goal. Force mode continuously adds to the velocity field and may give rise to very high speeds if left unchecked.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scale the effect of the force by the timestep. This ensures that the amount of force stays the same when substepping occurs, but if the instantaneous value needs to be computed, it can be turned off.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: Strength of the suction force that pulls toward the line segment. Positive values pull toward the axis, whereas negative values blow outward (away from the axis). Set this parameter to 0 to turn off the suction force. NOTE: The _suction_ force does not directly touch the v output, but is instead applied to the div output. This relies on div being wired to the divergence input of the Pyro Block End COP.

parameters.label: Pump Thickness
parameters.description: Specifies the thickness of the tube around the line where divergence values are set. This value should be larger than the voxel size of the simulation fields to avoid aliasing. Increasing this parameter will also amplify the strength of the suction force.

parameters.label: Suction Along Axis
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the amount of induced divergence (or strength of suction) along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to the Start Point and End Point, and the vertical axis spans from 0 to the Strength value.

parameters.label: Speed Range
parameters.description: The range of goal speeds in the direction of the line segment. Negative speed signals that the goal velocity points in the opposite direction (from the End Point toward the Start Point).

parameters.label: Speed Along Axis
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the goal axis speed along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to Start Point and End Point, and the vertical axis covers the given Speed Range.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: Strength of the axis force that generates motion in the direction of the line segment. When applied as drag, larger values of this parameter will align the incoming velocities more closely with the goal. When applied as force, increasing strength will increase the magnitude of the additive force. Set this parameter to 0 to turn off the axis force. NOTE: The final strength of the force at any point in the cylinder is the product of Strength with the two modifiers from the Strength Along Axis and Strength Away from Axis ramps.

parameters.label: Strength Along Axis
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the axis force along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to Start Point and End Point, respectively. The vertical axis spans 0 to 1, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for Strength.

parameters.label: Strength Away from Axis
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the axis force based on the distance to the line segment. The left side of this ramp represents the center of the active cylinder (distance of 0 to the axis), while the right side corresponds to its outer edge (at a separation of Influence Distance). The vertical axis spans 0 to 1, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for Strength.

parameters.label: Speed Range
parameters.description: The range of goal speeds around the line segment. With the axis directed from Start Point to End Point, positive speeds correspond to right-handed rotation around the line. Negative speeds generate rotation in the opposite direction.

parameters.label: Speed Falloff
parameters.description: Controls the relationship between orbital speed and orbital distance. When set to Constant, the speed is independent of distance. Orbital speed is directly proportional to distance in Scale by Distance mode (similar to a rotating rigid body). When Scale by Inverse Distance is selected, orbits are fastest at the line segment and gradually become slower as they get further away from the center of the active cylinder.

parameters.label: Speed Along Axis
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the goal orbit speed along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to Start Point and End Point, and this ramp's vertical axis covers the given Speed Range.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: Strength of the orbit force that generates rotational motion around the line segment. When applied as drag, larger values of this parameter will align the incoming velocities more closely with the goal. When applied as force, increasing strength will increase the magnitude of the additive force. Set this parameter to 0 to turn off the orbit force. NOTE: The final strength of the force at any point in the cylinder is the product of Strength with the two modifiers from the Strength Along Axis and Strength Away from Axis ramps.

parameters.label: Strength Along Axis
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the orbit force along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to Start Point and End Point, respectively. The vertical axis spans 0 to 1, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for Strength.

parameters.label: Strength Away from Axis
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the orbit force based on the distance to the line segment. The left side of this ramp represents the center of the active cylinder (distance of 0 to the axis), while the right side corresponds to its outer edge (at a separation of Influence Distance). The vertical axis spans 0 to 1, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for Strength.

parameters.label: Mask Range
parameters.description: Values in the Mask Field are remapped from this range to 0-1.

parameters.label: Remap Mask
parameters.description: When this checkbox is turned on, the remapped mask values (from Mask Range) are additionally passed through the Mask Ramp.

parameters.label: Mask Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp's vertical axis is the strength modifier and the horizontal axis is the remapped mask value.

inputs.label: v
inputs.description: A Vector VDB providing the initial velocities.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: A Float VDB controlling where the force will be applied.

outputs.label: v
outputs.description: A Vector VDB with the updated velocities from the axis force.

outputs.label: div
outputs.description: A Float VDB providing what the goal divergence of each voxel should be to drive the suction force. This should be wired to the divergence input of the Pyro Block End COP.

entries.title: Pyro Block Begin
entries.summary: Start of a Pyro simulation block.

parameters.label: Block Path
parameters.description: The path to the Pyro Block End COP, which is the final and closing node of this block. The Block End node must be at the same network level as this Block Begin node.

inputs.label: vdb_ref
inputs.description: VDB metadata to set the voxel size of the simulation.

inputs.label: density
inputs.description: A Float VDB providing how thick the smoke is at a voxel. Use the Source tab on Pyro Block End to control how this volume is mixed into the simulation.

inputs.label: temperature
inputs.description: A Float VDB providing the temperature at each voxel. Note that newly activated voxels will get a temperature of 0, so that value should usually be used as a baseline. Use the Source tab on Pyro Block End to control how this volume is mixed into the simulation.

inputs.label: v
inputs.description: A Vector VDB providing the wind speed of each voxel. Note that this does not include any Ambient Velocity. Use the Source tab on Pyro Block End to control how this volume is mixed into the simulation.

inputs.label: flame
inputs.description: A Float VDB of the current voxel flames. Use the Source tab on Pyro Block End to control how this volume is mixed into the simulation.

inputs.label: divergence
inputs.description: An optional Float VDB providing a goal divergence for the velocity, allowing the fluid to expand or contract. Use the Source tab on Pyro Block End to control how this volume is mixed into the simulation.

inputs.label: collision
inputs.description: An optional Float VDB providing a signed distance field (SDF) of a collider. Negative voxels will act like colliders.

inputs.label: collisionv
inputs.description: An optional Vector VDB providing a velocity for the collision objects. These are in world space, so they will be internally adjusted by Ambient Velocity.

inputs.label: feedback
inputs.description: A cable providing wires that will be fed back to the next iteration of the solve. It is important that the input's cable structure exactly matches the Pyro Block End COP's input. This is only read on the initial frame. Any feedback field can be resized and advected alongside the simulation.

inputs.label: passthrough
inputs.description: Optional cable providing layers and VDBs that should be computed outside of the simulation. They are read each frame, so can be used to inject animated sources, but cannot depend on the results of the simulation.

inputs.label: bounds_geo
inputs.description: Optional Geometry input. This is read each frame, and controls the maximum extend of the simulation domain.

inputs.label: source_points
inputs.description: Optional Geometry input for sourcing from implicit surfaces using Node:cop/pyro_sourceshape.

inputs.label: collision_points
inputs.description: Optional Geometry input to set up collision from implicit surfaces using Node:cop/pyro_collisionshape.

outputs.label: density
outputs.description: A Float VDB of the density that has been fed back to this frame.

outputs.label: temperature
outputs.description: A Float VDB of the temperature that has been fed back to this frame.

outputs.label: v
outputs.description: A Vector VDB of the velocity that has been fed back to this frame.

outputs.label: flame
outputs.description: A Float VDB of the flame that has been fed back to this frame.

outputs.label: divergence
outputs.description: A Float VDB of the divergence that has been fed back to this frame.

outputs.label: collision
outputs.description: A Vector VDB providing a velocity of the collision objects to this frame.

outputs.label: feedback
outputs.description: A Cable of the extra data that has been fed back to this frame.

outputs.label: passthrough
outputs.description: A Cable passing through the input, updated every frame from the input.

entries.summary: End of a Pyro simulation block.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: Clears the entire simulation cache.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Simulation doesn't save the results like other simulation types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Simulation button to pause and resume live simulation. See Cooking controls for more information.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: Sparse Simulation
parameters.description: When turned on, calculations are performed only in the areas of interest, where fluid exists. When turned off, you must provide a domain geometry (bounds_geo input) in which the calculations take place.

parameters.label: Voxel Size
parameters.description: The size of a voxel in world coordinates.

parameters.label: Advection Reflection
parameters.description: Advection-Reflection attempts to inject energy lost due to pressure projection back into the simulation. Turning on this option may exhibit better vortex retention in the flow. It performs a single pressure projection per timestep and adds the removed velocity components back at the next step. This requires an extra vector field to be carried between timesteps. :video: #src: /videos/pyro/pyro_advection_reflection.webm

parameters.label: Reflection Amount
parameters.description: Fraction of the projected velocities to re-inject. Values near 1 will do a better job of conserving energy, but may result in instabilities. :video: #src: /videos/pyro/pyro_single_project.webm

parameters.label: Cache
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/block_end#cacheenabled

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 24 to cache frames 24, 48, 72, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to disable checkpointing.

parameters.label: Clip by Bounds
parameters.description: When Sparse Simulation is turned on, use this to limit how far the fluid can extend.

parameters.label: Clip by
parameters.description: When Sparse Simulation is turned on, use this to limit how far the fluid can extend. If a bounds_geo input is provided, these settings are ignored. Bounding Box: Use Center and Size parameters to control the extent of the simulation domain. Separate Sides: Clip the domain between 6 clipping planes.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the domain box.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: Controls the center position of the domain box.

parameters.label: Reference Fields
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_activate#refvdbs

parameters.label: Reference Cutoff
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_activate#refcutoff

parameters.label: Activate Fields
parameters.description: The fields that are activated in each frame based on the reference fields and additional padding.

parameters.label: Activate Feedbacks
parameters.description: Additional fields inside the feedback cable to be activated.

parameters.label: Enable Collision
parameters.description: Turns on collision detection for the solver.

parameters.label: Velocity Scale
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_collisionshape#vscale

parameters.label: Correct Collisions
parameters.description: Zero out the density and temperature that are inside the collision SDF, avoiding any leaking of smoke.

parameters.label: Source Density
parameters.description: When turned on, the density input of the block is sourced into the density field.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns the effect of this sourcing on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Source Mode
parameters.description: Controls when the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Continuous : Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation and is applied on every solver step. Use this when you need a constant supply of density, temperature or other quantities. First Frame Only: Sourcing is applied only on the first simulation frame. This is useful when the fluid is already present when the simulation begins. If the source is animated, those animations are ignored after the first frame. Copy on First Frame: Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation, as in Continuous mode. On the first simulation frame, the source volume is copied into the target volume. On subsequent frames, the operation is determined by Operation.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Add: The result is the sum of the source and target values. Copy: The result is copied from the source volume. Maximum: The result is the greater of the source and target values. Average: The result is the average of the source and target values. Blend: The result is a blend between the source and target values, using Blend as the weight. Pull: Pushes source values toward the corresponding target values according to the Acceleration Strength and Deceleration Strength settings.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the source values before they are mixed with the target volume.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the effect of sourcing by the timestep. This ensures that the amount of sourcing remains consistent when substepping occurs. Turn off this parameter if you need the instantaneous source value.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the weight used to blend between the source values and the corresponding volume values.

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are smaller than the corresponding target values are pushed toward the target field.

parameters.label: Deceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are larger than the corresponding target volume values are pushed toward the target field.

parameters.label: Source Temperature
parameters.description: WWhen turned on, the temperature input of the block is sourced into the temperature field.

parameters.description: Turns the effect of this sourcing on and off. This is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the emitted divergence is mixed with the incoming divergence field. Add: The result is the sum of the values in the emitted divergence and the incoming divergence field. Maximum: The result is the larger of the values in the emitted divergence and the incoming divergence field. Average: The result is the average of the values in the emitted divergence and the incoming divergence field. Blend: he result is a blend of the values in the emitted divergence and the incoming divergence field, using the Blend parameter as weight. Pull: Values in the emitted divergence are pushed toward the corresponding incoming divergence field values, according to the Acceleration and Deceleration settings.

parameters.label: Expansion Scale
parameters.description: Scales the amount of divergence output from the flame, which is calculated by first remapping the flame field from Flame Range to 0-1 or optionally to the range given by Emission Range. When Cool Flame is turned on, this is further scaled by the flame cooling ratio before multiplying the divergence output by this number.

parameters.label: Flame Range
parameters.description: Controls the flame region to emit divergence from. The flame field is first fitted from this range to 0-1 or optionally to the range given by Emission Range. Turn on Use Ramp to change how the flame values scale between the minimum and maximum of this range.

parameters.label: Emission Range
parameters.description: When turned on, this maps the flame field from the minimum and maximum values of Flame Range to this range.

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: Where the emitted divergence values are smaller than the incoming divergence field values, controls how strongly those values are pushed toward the incoming divergence field.

parameters.label: Deceleration
parameters.description: Where the emitted divergence values are larger than the incoming divergence field values, controls how strongly those values are pushed toward the incoming divergence field.

parameters.description: Controls the weight by which to blend between the incoming divergence field and the emitted divergence values.

parameters.label: Trace Method
parameters.description: Controls the integration scheme used for a single trace step through the velocity field. This setting determines how closely the smoke follows turbulent flows and how well the simulation preserves detail over time. Options in this menu are listed in order of increasing accuracy and computational cost. Forward Euler: Predicts the next position based on its current velocity using a straight line. This is a 1st-order accurate method that has the fastest computation time, but it introduces more numerical diffusion, making the smoke look blurrier and can flatten turbulent flows. Average of Two: Predicts the future position, looks at the velocity there, and averages it with the current velocity. It is a step up from Euler, which helps smoke maintain its volume and shape during simple rotations. Explicit Midpoint: Samples the fluid velocity at a half-step forward to determine the full-step move. This is better at capturing vorticity (swirling). It prevents particles from spiraling outward away from the center of a vortex. Runge-Kutta 3: A 3rd-order method that takes three samples of the velocity field to calculate the path. Use this when you need high-fidelity "wispy" smoke details without the full performance hit of RK4. Runge-Kutta 4: A 4th-order method that samples the velocity field four times to find the most accurate "curve" through the fluid. This is essential for complex, turbulent simulations. It minimizes energy loss, ensuring that small eddies and swirls don't disappear prematurely.

parameters.label: Path Tracing
parameters.description: A single trace step is often not enough to preserve sharp details, wispy tendrils, and small vortices through turbulent or fast-moving velocity flows. When this is turned on, multiple trace steps (given by Trace Method) are taken to better predict the curved path through the velocity field. The number of steps depends on the Maximum Steps and the CFL Condition.

parameters.label: CFL Condition
parameters.description: Controls how large a step should be used when tracing through the velocity field. This is approximately how many voxels will be stepped during a single trace step. Lower values mean better stability, but lower performance. Higher values force the tracing to take larger steps, allowing it to finish faster.

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: Global clamp on how many path tracing steps can be performed. For extremely fast motion this may need to be increased, but it might be better to raise the CFL condition instead.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Simulation doesn't save the results like other simulation types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Simulation button to pause and resume live simulation. See Cooking controls for more information.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: Sparse Simulation
parameters.description: When turned on, calculations are performed only in the areas of interest, where fluid exists. When turned off, you must provide a domain geometry (bounds_geo input) in which the calculations take place.

parameters.label: Voxel Size
parameters.description: The size of a voxel in world coordinates.

parameters.label: Advection Reflection
parameters.description: Advection-Reflection attempts to inject energy lost due to pressure projection back into the simulation. Turning on this option may exhibit better vortex retention in the flow. It performs a single pressure projection per timestep and adds the removed velocity components back at the next step. This requires an extra vector field to be carried between timesteps. :video: #src: /videos/pyro/pyro_advection_reflection.webm

parameters.label: Reflection Amount
parameters.description: Fraction of the projected velocities to re-inject. Values near 1 will do a better job of conserving energy, but may result in instabilities. :video: #src: /videos/pyro/pyro_single_project.webm

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: When Simulate is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 24 to cache frames 24, 48, 72, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to disable checkpointing.

parameters.description: When turned on, the density input of the block is sourced into the density field.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns the effect of this sourcing on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Source Mode
parameters.description: Controls when the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Continuous : Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation and is applied on every solver step. Use this when you need a constant supply of density, temperature or other quantities. First Frame Only: Sourcing is applied only on the first simulation frame. This is useful when the fluid is already present when the simulation begins. If the source is animated, those animations are ignored after the first frame. Copy on First Frame: Sourcing remains active throughout the simulation, as in Continuous mode. On the first simulation frame, the source volume is copied into the target volume. On subsequent frames, the operation is determined by Operation.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the source volume is mixed with the target volume. Add: The result is the sum of the source and target values. Copy: The result is copied from the source volume. Maximum: The result is the greater of the source and target values. Average: The result is the average of the source and target values. Blend: The result is a blend between the source and target values, using Blend as the weight. Pull: Pushes source values toward the corresponding target values according to the Acceleration Strength and Deceleration Strength settings.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the source values before they are mixed with the target volume.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scales the effect of sourcing by the timestep. This ensures that the amount of sourcing remains consistent when substepping occurs. Turn off this parameter if you need the instantaneous source value.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the weight used to blend between the source values and the corresponding volume values.

parameters.label: Acceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are smaller than the corresponding target values are pushed toward the target field.

parameters.label: Deceleration
parameters.description: Controls how strongly source values that are larger than the corresponding target volume values are pushed toward the target field.

parameters.label: Trace Method
parameters.description: Controls the integration scheme used for a single trace step through the velocity field. This setting determines how closely the smoke follows turbulent flows and how well the simulation preserves detail over time. Options in this menu are listed in order of increasing accuracy and computational cost. Forward Euler: Predicts the next position based on its current velocity using a straight line. This is a 1st-order accurate method that has the fastest computation time, but it introduces more numerical diffusion, making the smoke look blurrier and can flatten turbulent flows. Average of Two: Predicts the future position, looks at the velocity there, and averages it with the current velocity. It is a step up from Euler, which helps smoke maintain its volume and shape during simple rotations. Explicit Midpoint: Samples the fluid velocity at a half-step forward to determine the full-step move. This is better at capturing vorticity (swirling). It prevents particles from spiraling outward away from the center of a vortex. Runge-Kutta 3: A 3rd-order method that takes three samples of the velocity field to calculate the path. Use this when you need high-fidelity "wispy" smoke details without the full performance hit of RK4. Runge-Kutta 4: A 4th-order method that samples the velocity field four times to find the most accurate "curve" through the fluid. This is essential for complex, turbulent simulations. It minimizes energy loss, ensuring that small eddies and swirls don't disappear prematurely.

parameters.label: Path Tracing
parameters.description: A single trace step is often not enough to preserve sharp details, wispy tendrils, and small vortices through turbulent or fast-moving velocity flows. When this is turned on, multiple trace steps (given by Trace Method) are taken to better predict the curved path through the velocity field. The number of steps depends on the Maximum Steps and the CFL Condition.

parameters.label: CFL Condition
parameters.description: Controls how large a step should be used when tracing through the velocity field. This is approximately how many voxels will be stepped during a single trace step. Lower values mean better stability, but lower performance. Higher values force the tracing to take larger steps, allowing it to finish faster.

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: Global clamp on how many path tracing steps can be performed. For extremely fast motion this may need to be increased, but it might be better to raise the CFL condition instead.

parameters.label: Adaptive Step Size
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_buildadvectionmap#adaptive

parameters.label: Scheme
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#method

parameters.label: Sharpen
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#sharpen

parameters.description: Turn this on to provide a different advection scheme for velocity self-advection.

parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#method

parameters.label: Velocity Sharpen
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/pyro_advectbymap#sharpen

parameters.label: Feather Blocks
parameters.description: Reduce the strength of the block correction over the farthest blocks. This helps avoid sharp transitions in the corrected velocity when strong impulses are present, but may require more iterations or computation time to fully remove divergence.

parameters.description: The output velocity VDB v will be scaled by timescale, ensuring it will motion blur correctly. However, if this is to be used by another simulation, you may want the raw velocity values.

parameters.label: Correct by Ambient Velocity
parameters.description: The output velocity VDB v will be adjusted by ambient velocity, ensuring it will motion blur correctly. However, if this is to be used by another simulation, you may want the raw velocity values.

entries.title: Pyro Buoyancy Force
entries.summary: Applies a Buoyancy force.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns the effect of this node on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: How to mix the force in with the incoming velocities. Set: Replace the velocities with the force value. This is useful for debugging purposes, but it will break your simulation. Add: Add the force to the incoming velocities.

parameters.label: Buoyancy Scale
parameters.description: A global scale on the amount of buoyancy to apply. Hot gas expands, causing it to rise due to lowered density. Acceleration due to buoyancy is calculated using the values of the ambient and reference temperatures, as well as the Gravity Acceleration scale. :video: #src: /videos/pyro/pyro_buoyancy.webm

parameters.label: Ambient Temp (K)
parameters.description: Temperature corresponding to value of 0 in the temperature field (in Kelvin). This represents the ambient temperature of the environment.

parameters.label: Reference Temp (K)
parameters.description: Temperature corresponding to a value of 1 in the temperature field (in Kelvin). The temperature range is used to calculate the strength of the buoyancy force. NOTE: In general, a value of T in the temperature field corresponds to a temperature of Ambient Temp (K) + T * (Reference Temp (K) - Ambient Temp (K)).

parameters.label: Equilibrium Temp
parameters.description: Hot gas rises in the buoyancy direction where temperature values are above this ambient temperature, and falls where they are below it. Since newly activated areas have zero temperature, this usually needs to be zero to leave dead-space unaffected. This is useful for simulating cloud formation where gases can rise and fall.

parameters.label: Gravity Acceleration
parameters.description: Acceleration due to gravity. Stronger gravity results in a stronger buoyancy force.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The direction in which temperatures hotter than the ambient temperature will be forced.

parameters.label: Threshold Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the threshold field. Threshold fields are intended to provide harsh on/off effects, but the range can be used to soften the transition.

parameters.label: Threshold Range
parameters.description: The value of the threshold field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0.01 to 0 range is designed to concentrate the effect on the edges and empty regions of the threshold field, but not inside it. When the threshold field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Threshold Ramp, to change how the threshold field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.

parameters.label: Threshold Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the threshold field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.

parameters.label: Control Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the control field. Control fields are usually used the same way as masks, and represent a smooth engagement of the effect.

parameters.label: Control Range
parameters.description: The value of the control field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0 to 1 range is designed to concentrate the effect on regions with higher control field values. When the control field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Control Ramp, to change how the control field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.

parameters.label: Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the control field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.

parameters.label: Angle Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect by the angle between the velocity field values and a direction vector.

parameters.label: Angle Direction
parameters.description: The reference vector used to calculate the angle deviation against the velocity field.

parameters.label: Spread Angle
parameters.description: The value of the calculated angle is mapped until this angle range to 1-0 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. At the default 90 degrees, the effect is strongest where the vectors align, and gradually diminishes to zero as the angle reaches this value.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Angle Control Ramp, to change how the angle deviation should scale the effect between the aligned vectors and the given Spread Angle.

parameters.label: Angle Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the angle deviation is mapped between the aligned vectors and the given Spread Angle.

parameters.label: Axis Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect along an axis direction. Rather than requiring the construction of VDBs to represent this, this allows direct specification of the world space range over which the effect is to be scaled.

parameters.label: Axis Direction
parameters.description: The reference vector along which the effect will be masked.

parameters.label: Axis Range
parameters.description: The position along the axis mask is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Axis Control Ramp, to change how the position along the axis should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.

parameters.label: Axis Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the position is mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.

entries.title: Pyro Buoyancy Force
entries.summary: Applies a Buoyancy force.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns the effect of this node on and off. This node is only active when this value is 1.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: How to mix the force in with the incoming velocities. Set: Replace the velocities with the force value. This is useful for debugging purposes, but it will break your simulation. Add: Add the force to the incoming velocities.

parameters.label: Buoyancy Scale
parameters.description: A global scale on the amount of buoyancy to apply. Hot gas expands, causing it to rise due to lowered density. Acceleration due to buoyancy is calculated using the values of the ambient and reference temperatures, as well as the Gravity Acceleration scale. :video: #src: /videos/pyro/pyro_buoyancy.webm

parameters.label: Ambient Temp (K)
parameters.description: Temperature corresponding to value of 0 in the temperature field (in Kelvin). This represents the ambient temperature of the environment.

parameters.label: Reference Temp (K)
parameters.description: Temperature corresponding to a value of 1 in the temperature field (in Kelvin). The temperature range is used to calculate the strength of the buoyancy force. NOTE: In general, a value of T in the temperature field corresponds to a temperature of Ambient Temp (K) + T * (Reference Temp (K) - Ambient Temp (K)).

parameters.label: Equilibrium Temp
parameters.description: Hot gas rises in the buoyancy direction where temperature values are above this ambient temperature, and falls where they are below it. Since newly activated areas have zero temperature, this usually needs to be zero to leave dead-space unaffected. This is useful for simulating cloud formation where gases can rise and fall.

parameters.label: Gravity Acceleration
parameters.description: Acceleration due to gravity. Stronger gravity results in a stronger buoyancy force.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The direction in which temperatures hotter than the ambient temperature will be forced.

parameters.label: Threshold Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the threshold field. Threshold fields are intended to provide harsh on/off effects, but the range can be used to soften the transition.

parameters.label: Threshold Range
parameters.description: The value of the threshold field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0.01 to 0 range is designed to concentrate the effect on the edges and empty regions of the threshold field, but not inside it. When the threshold field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Threshold Ramp, to change how the threshold field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.

parameters.label: Threshold Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the threshold field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Threshold Range.

parameters.label: Control Volume
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the control field. Control fields are usually used the same way as masks, and represent a smooth engagement of the effect.

parameters.label: Control Range
parameters.description: The value of the control field is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. The default 0 to 1 range is designed to concentrate the effect on regions with higher control field values. When the control field is a Vector VDB, this value represents the length of the given vector field.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Control Ramp, to change how the control field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.

parameters.label: Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the control field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Control Range.

parameters.label: Angle Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect by the angle between the velocity field values and a direction vector.

parameters.label: Angle Direction
parameters.description: The reference vector used to calculate the angle deviation against the velocity field.

parameters.label: Spread Angle
parameters.description: The value of the calculated angle is mapped until this angle range to 1-0 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale. At the default 90 degrees, the effect is strongest where the vectors align, and gradually diminishes to zero as the angle reaches this value.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Angle Control Ramp, to change how the angle deviation should scale the effect between the aligned vectors and the given Spread Angle.

parameters.label: Angle Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the angle deviation is mapped between the aligned vectors and the given Spread Angle.

parameters.label: Axis Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect along an axis direction. Rather than requiring the construction of VDBs to represent this, this allows direct specification of the world space range over which the effect is to be scaled.

parameters.label: Axis Direction
parameters.description: The reference vector along which the effect will be masked.

parameters.label: Axis Range
parameters.description: The position along the axis mask is mapped from this range to 0-1 and applied as a multiplier on top of Scale.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Turns on the Axis Control Ramp, to change how the position along the axis should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.

parameters.label: Axis Control Ramp
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the position is mapped between the minimum and maximum values of Axis Range.

entries.title: Pyro Configure
entries.summary: Configures a Pyro simulation.

parameters.label: Divisions
parameters.description: How to specify the resolution of the simulation. Voxel Size: Uses world space units. Works best for fully 3D simulations. Resolution: Voxel size is calculated according to the resolution of the default imaging plane. This is a 2-unit wide square. This is useful if producing effects in a canonical imaging plane, as you can tell how many voxels you have per pixel. Coverage: This is useful for fully 3D simulations, where the camera resolution and distance to the camera can dictate an optimal voxel size. This helps avoid simulating extra detail that would not otherwise be visible from the camera.

parameters.label: Voxel Size
parameters.description: The size of a voxel in world coordinates.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: The resolution the simulation will have if it fills the standard imaging plane. 2/Resolution is the voxel size.

parameters.label: Pixel Coverage
parameters.description: Controls the number of screen-space pixels that cover a single voxel. The default of 2.5 usually provides enough visual quality.

parameters.label: Min Vozel Size
parameters.description: When the voxel size is calculated, turn this on to ensure that voxels cannot be smaller than this size.

inputs.label: vdb_ref
inputs.description: Optional float VDB to set the voxel size.

inputs.label: camera_ref
inputs.description: Camera reference when Division is set to Coverage.

inputs.label: centroid_ref
inputs.description: A point geometry reference when Division is set to Coverage, representing the center of the simulation.

outputs.label: vdb_ref
outputs.description: A VDB reference to control the initial voxel size of the simulation.

entries.title: Pyro Disturbance
entries.summary: Applies disturbance to a velocity VDB to break up still air.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Set: The velocities are replaced by the disturbance values. This is useful for visualizing the effect, or controlling more precisely how it is applied. Add: The disturbance is added to the incoming velocity. Rotate: The values in the incoming velocity are rotated towards the randomly-generated directions without changing their length.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Controls the nature of the generated random vectors. :video: #src: /videos/pyro/pyro_disturbance_mode.webm Continuous: Every voxel gets an independently-assigned random vector. Block-Based: The random pattern is formed by composing several layers of blockwise-constant noise.

parameters.label: Disturbance
parameters.description: Controls strength of the applied force. NOTE: When Rotate is used, Strength governs how fast the vectors are rotated towards their goal.

parameters.label: Reference Scale
parameters.description: Variance of the aggregated noise field over a region of this size will be equal to Strength when Mode is set to Continuous. Provides a scale for normalizing the force against voxel size. A larger value for this parameter will increase magnitude of the applied force. TIP: You should set this parameter to a reasonable value for your scene scale and leave it there. Strength can be used to more finely control how much force is applied.

parameters.label: Block Size
parameters.description: Controls size of the biggest blocks in the generated noise pattern when Mode is set to Block-Based.

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.description: Length of time (in seconds) that the noise pattern is held fixed. This only applies when Mode is set to Block-Based. NOTE: The noise pattern changes on every frame in Continuous mode.

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.description: The maximum number of noise levels to compose in Block-Based mode.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.description: The ratio of block sizes between successive noise layers. For example, a value of 2 means that the first layer has blocks that are twice the size of the second layer; the second layer will in turn have blocks that are twice as large as the next layer. This parameter is only applicable in Block-Based mode.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.description: The ratio of amplitudes between successive noise layers. For example a value of 0.5 means that the second layer will have half the amplitude of the first one. This parameter is only applicable in Block-Based mode. TIP: Lower Roughness values will better preserve the block structure in the generated noise, whereas higher ones (nearing or exceeding 1) will yield more chaotic patterns resembling white noise.

inputs.label: v
inputs.description: A Vector VDB of the incoming velocities.

inputs.description: A Float or Vector VDB to use as a threshold field. If it is a Vector VDB, its length is used.

inputs.label: control
inputs.description: A Float or Vector VDB to use as a control field. If it is a Vector VDB, its length is used.

outputs.label: v
outputs.description: A Vector VDB of the disturbed velocities.

entries.title: Pyro Light Ambient
entries.summary: Builds a light field of ambient illumination of a VDB.

parameters.label: Exposed Color
parameters.description: The color of light that is exposed to the ambient surroundings. This is normally white, but can be used to tint the effective environment map.

parameters.label: Occluded Color
parameters.description: The color of light where the voxel is exposed to the ambient surroundings. Normally this is black, but setting this to white and the Exposed Color to a dark color will result in a self-lit look which works well for clouds.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.description: Controls the linear brightness of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: Controls the exponential brightness of the light. Each increase of 1 doubles the brightness.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: Scales the density VDB values, causing it to occlude light more quickly.

parameters.label: Environment Map Offset
parameters.description: Controls the angle used to rotate the environment map around the Y-axis

parameters.label: Steps Per MipMap
parameters.description: Controls how many tracing steps are performed before dropping to the next MipMap level when tracing occlusion rays. Lower values make the rays effectively thicker, causing them to become more like cones than rays.

parameters.label: Max Steps
parameters.description: Controls the maximum number of samples taken while tracing an occlusion ray. Since higher MipMap levels have larger step sizes, the distance covered will be larger than just the voxelsize times the maxsteps.

parameters.label: Environment Map Resolution
parameters.description: Because only a few rays are used to sample the ambient light, the environment map must be downsampled to avoid aliasing. This parameter controls the resolution to which it is resampled.

parameters.label: MipMap Level
parameters.description: Controls the starting mipmap level. Starting at MipMap level 1 computes the light in a half-resolution VDB and interpolates the result back to full resolution, making the operation more than eight times faster.

inputs.label: density
inputs.description: A Float VDB storing the density to occlude light. This is also the topology used to build a light field. The light field will only be present where density was activated.

inputs.label: mipmap
inputs.description: An optional Float VDB MipMap from a Packed MipMap COP. If not provided, it will be computed internally.

inputs.label: light
inputs.description: An optional Vector VDB storing the amount of illumination at each voxel. The new light will be added to this, allowing lights to be chained.

inputs.label: envmap
inputs.description: An optional RGB layer storing the environment map in polar coordinates.

outputs.label: light
outputs.description: The light that reaches each voxel from the ambient sources.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.description: When turned on, the light is considered to be at infinity and all light rays are parallel. When turned off, the lights are treated as point lights that emanate from their 3D positions.

parameters.label: Light Direction
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, specifies the direction of the light when it is directional.

parameters.label: Light Radius
parameters.description: Point lights have a singularity at their location, so if a point light is inside the volume it becomes infinitely bright at that location. parameters.label: Color

parameters.label: Exposure

parameters.label: Density Scale
