entries.title: Ray Trace
entries.summary: Performs ray tracing on an input mesh based on an origins and directions map.

parameters.label: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracer to use. This is an automatic menu that shows only available options based on your hardware. NOTE: Optix is available on only NVidia hardware.

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.description: The amount to offset a ray's origin from the origins map along the directions. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the tracing mesh along its normal.

parameters.label: Face Culling
parameters.description: The behavior of primary rays that interact with the geometry. No Culling: Use all polygons. Back Faces: Ignore primary rays that hit the backfaces of the geometry. Front Faces: Ignore primary rays that hit the frontfaces of the geometry.

parameters.label: Visibility Culling
parameters.description: The behavior of secondary rays that interact with the geometry. For example, secondary rays used to calculate ambient occlusion. No Culling: Don't ignore any secondary rays. Back Faces: Ignore secondary rays that hit the backfaces of the geometry. Front Faces: Ignore secondary rays that hit the frontfaces of the geometry.

parameters.label: Trace Direction
parameters.description: The direction that the rays travel relative to its origin and direction. Bidirectional: Two way, fire rays both forward and backward. Forward: Fire rays the same direction as directions. Reverse: Fire rays the inverse of the directions.

parameters.label: Ray Length Mode
parameters.description: The method used to set the maximum length of the rays. Custom: Use the Ray Length parameter or lengths input to manually set the ray length. Endless: Rays have no length limit. If the rays point towards somewhere they won't hit any geometry and therefore infinitely travel, they aren't fired.

parameters.label: Ray Length
parameters.description: The maximum length of the rays.

parameters.label: Trace Set Attribute
parameters.description: The attribute on the geometry to look for to match trace sets with the tracesets input. If one part of a mesh on the tracesets ID layer is 1 and the Trace Set Attribute on the geometry has a section with a value of 1, these two pieces are traced only to each other and ignore all other geometry.

parameters.label: Occlusion
parameters.description: Bakes the Occlusion map, which bakes the effect of indirect lighting and shadows from the geometry. When off, the occlusion output is a Null layer. Use ambient occlusion to fake shadows, particularly in areas where objects are close together.

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays to use when computing Occlusion. Increase this value if the resulting AOV is noisy.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Occlusion. A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.description: Bakes the Cavity map, which computes the concave details of the geometry. When off, the cavity output is a Null layer. Use this for masking indents or cracks in the geometry.

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays to use when computing Cavity. Increase this value if the resulting AOV is noisy.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Cavity. A small distance can speed up cavity shading at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The ray bias when computing Cavity.

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.description: Bakes the Curvature map, which bakes concavity and convexity. Concave details are brighter while convex details are darker. When off, the curvature output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays to use when computing Curvature. Increase this value if the resulting AOV is noisy.

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.description: The overall curvature strength.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing Curvature. A small distance can speed up curvature shading at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: The amount to shift the contrast to emphasize convexity (0.0) or concavity (1.0).

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Bakes the Thickness map, which generates a map based on the thickness of the geometry. Thicker areas create darker values and thinner areas create brighter values. When off, the thickness output is a Null layer.

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays to use when computing Thickness. Increase this value if the resulting AOV is noisy.

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.description: Bakes the Edge map, which creates a map of the edges on the mesh. When off, the edge output is a Null layer. Use this to fake beveled edges on hard surfaces.

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays to use when computing Edge. Increase this value if the resulting AOV is noisy.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius when computing Edge.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: The cusp angle when computing Edge.

parameters.label: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: Bakes the Rounded Normal map, which creates a normal map from the edges on the mesh. When off, the roundednormal output is a Null layer. Use this to fake beveled edges on hard surfaces.

parameters.label: Rounded Normal Samples
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays to use when computing Rounded Normal. Increase this value if the resulting AOV is noisy.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius when computing Rounded Normal.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.description: The cusp angle when computing Rounded Normal.

parameters.label: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: The number of custom attributes to rasterize.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to rasterize. This must match the attribute present on the geometry input. This can be Point, Vertex, or Primitive.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: The output type for the rasterized attribute. To be rasterized, an attribute must be either an integer or a float of four or less components. See Data types for more information.

inputs.label: geometry
inputs.description: The geometry to ray trace against.

inputs.label: origins
inputs.description: The RGB map of the positions from which to fire rays.

inputs.label: directions
inputs.description: The RGB map of the orientations along which to fire rays.

inputs.label: tracesets
inputs.description: The ID layer of the sets to evaluate on each hit of the geometry.

inputs.label: lengths
inputs.description: The mono layer of the ray lengths. The node doesn't use this input when Ray Length Mode is set to Endless.

outputs.label: intersections
outputs.description: The intersection data of the rays fired against the geometry.

outputs.label: normals
outputs.description: The geometric normal of the intersection point of the rays fired against the geometry.

outputs.label: occlusion
outputs.description: The map of the effect of indirect lighting and shadows from the geometry.

outputs.label: cavity
outputs.description: The map of the concave details of the geometry.

outputs.label: curvature
outputs.description: The map of the concavity and convexity of the geometry. Concave details are brighter while convex details are darker.

outputs.label: thickness
outputs.description: The map based on the thickness of the geometry. Thicker areas create darker values and thinner areas create brighter values.

outputs.label: edge
outputs.description: The map of the edge details of the geometry.

outputs.label: roundednormal
outputs.description: The map of the rounded edge normal of the geometry.

outputs.label: output#
outputs.description: The rasterized custom attribute. The amount of attribute outputs and their details are based on the Custom Attributes information.

entries.title: Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin
entries.summary: Start of a Reaction-Diffusion simulation block.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The signature mode to evaluate the activation input as. This also controls how the reaction initiates using the activation pattern. Activation (Mono): Use a mono input pattern to initiate the reaction with. In this mode, it's best to provide high contrast noise patterns to help the reaction start. Chemical (UV): Use a UV input, which causes the reaction to continue using the raw chemical values. Use this to stack multiple Reaction-Diffusion blocks. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Block Path
parameters.description: The path to the Reaction-Diffusion Block End COP that's the final and closing node of this block. The Reaction-Diffusion Block End node must be at the same network level as this Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin node.

parameters.label: Continuous Activation
parameters.description: Makes the simulation evaluate the activation pattern as if it were a constant source. When off, the simulation evaluates the activation pattern on only the first frame.

inputs.label: activation
inputs.description: The activation pattern with which the reaction initiates. NOTE: Unless Continuous Activation is on, this is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: alpha
inputs.description: An input to control the Alpha coefficient in the reaction. This is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: beta
inputs.description: An input to control the Beta coefficient in the reaction. This is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: gamma
inputs.description: An input to control the Gamma coefficient in the reaction. This is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: scale
inputs.description: An input to control the reaction scale. This is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: coefficient
inputs.description: An input to control the Diffusion Coefficients in the reaction. This is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: boundary
inputs.description: An input to control the boundary of the reaction. This causes the reaction to grow organically into the SDF shape. This is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: feedback
inputs.description: A cable with wires that are fedback to the next iteration of the solve. The input's cable structure must exactly match the Reaction-Diffusion Block End's input. This is read on only the initial frame.

inputs.label: passthrough
inputs.description: An optional cable with layers and VDBs that should be computed outside of the simulation. These are read each frame, so they can't depend on the results of the simulation, but you can use them to inject animated sources.

inputs.label: adjacency
inputs.description: An optional cable with adjacency data that should be computed outside of the simulation. These are read each frame, so they can't depend on the results of the simulation. When you wire in this input, it automatically runs over adjacency.

outputs.label: chemical
outputs.description: The raw chemical reaction.

outputs.label: feedback
outputs.description: A cable of the extra data that's been fedback to this frame.

outputs.label: passthrough
outputs.description: A cable that passes through the input, updating every frame from the input.

outputs.label: adjacency
outputs.description: An adjacency cable that passes rasterized geometry through the input, updating every frame from the input.

entries.title: Reaction-Diffusion Block End
entries.summary: Creates unique patterns by solving the reaction and diffusion of multiple chemicals as described by its inputs and parameters.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: Signature which controls the output of the node. Pattern (Mono): Mono output of the chemical pattern with various optional remappings and output correction applied. Chemical (UV): UV output of the raw chemical values. NOTE: Chemical output mode is outputting the raw values, and does not allow for any control for color customisation. Therefore results may be visually unfriendly.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The model to use to describe how the chemicals interact, which includes presets. Gray-Scott: Two chemicals reacting with two input parameters for how the chemicals interact. Kenjiro Maginu: Two chemicals reacting with three input parameters for how the chemicals interact.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Sets parameters to create Gray-Scott preset patterns. Small Waves: Smaller oscillating waves. Large Waves: Larger oscillating waves. Spots: Self-replicating cells. Blinking Blobs: Tiny oscillating waves that bounce against each other, creating a blinking effect. Worms: Long stretchy blobs that resemble worms or snakes. Labyrinth: Maze-like labyrinth pattern with many corners and loops. Negatons: Creates a subcritical cellular look. Chaos with Negatons: Reaction that fluctuates between a stable state and a chaotic state mixed with subcritical cells. Spatiotemporal Chaos: Reaction that fluctuates between a stable state and a chaotic state.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Sets parameters to create Kenjiro Maginu preset patterns. Blobs & Spots: Tiny cellular blobs amongst larger blobs. Wormy: Long wormy structures with singular cells broken up throughout. Abstract: Creates a blobby abstract look with large blobs containing smaller blobs. Noisy: Chaotic noisy pattern. Brusselator: Creates a fast oscillating spiral look. Foamy: Chaotic pattern with similarities to foam. Oily: Pattern that slowly diffuses from large blobs (given the input was already chaotic). Nearly Chaos: Chaotic pattern with stable areas and unstable areas. Moving Brusselator: A Brusselator pattern with a more chaotic structure and moving spirals.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Simulate: Turns on simulation so block outputs feed directly back into the inputs, which creates a feedback loop. This is useful for complex motion and simulations.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: Reset Simulation: When Simulate is on, this clears the entire simulation cache.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Amount of iterations to run in non-simulation mode.

parameters.label: Iterations per Step
parameters.description: Amount of iterations to take per step within non-simulation, simulation, or Live Simulation.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: Live Simulation: When Simulate is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Simulation doesn't save the results like other simulation types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: Toggle Live Simulation: When Live Simulation is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Simulation button to pause and resume live simulation. See Cooking controls for more information.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: Live Tick: When Live Simulation is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: Time Scale: When Simulate is on, this is the amount to scale the time inside the block. A value of 1 maintains the normal speed, a value greater than 1 speeds up the simulation, and a value less than 1 slows down the simulation. This value is used within the chemical reaction equations. NOTE:

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: Sets the amount of substeps for each simulated frame.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, the Start Frame, Cached Frames, and Checkpoint Rate parameters no longer apply.

parameters.label: Caching
parameters.description: Turns on caching of frames.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: Start Frame: When Simulate is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: Cached Frames: When Simulate is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: Checkpoint Rate: When Simulate is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 24 to cache frames 24, 48, 72, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to disable checkpointing.

parameters.label: Switch to Raw Values
parameters.description: Interprets the parameters and input layers as raw. NOTE: It's recommended that you keep this off since the normalized parameters and layers are warped to limit the possibility of instability, create the most artistically interesting results, and stop the reaction from dying out or overreacting.

parameters.label: Scale Multiplier
parameters.description: Changes the size of the patterns by altering the reaction rate relative to the diffusion rate. This leads to the reaction happening slower at extreme scales, and tiny scales freeze the reaction altogether. Therefore, having a larger scale may require letting the reaction run for more iterations/ticks to fully grow into the requested scale.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: Input layers for alpha, beta, and gamma on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP override these parameters. Input layers for scale and coefficient on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP multiply these parameters.

parameters.label: Alpha α (Feed)
parameters.description: Chemical A is added into the simulation at a given "feed" rate. This is scaled with (1.0f - A) so that A does not exceed 1.0.

parameters.label: Beta β (Kill)
parameters.description: Chemical B is removed from the simulation at a given "kill" rate. This is scaled with (kill + feed) * B so that it does not go below 0.0.

parameters.label: Alpha α
parameters.description: Controls the nonlinear self-activation of A. Essentially the reaction strength of A.

parameters.label: Beta β
parameters.description: Determines how strongly Chemical B reacts to the presence of Chemical A.

parameters.label: Gamma γ
parameters.description: Controls how strongly B is pulled back towards A. Essenially a damping or decay coefficient that prevents B from growing indefinitely.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: The coefficient input on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP multiplies these parameters.

parameters.label: Diffusion A
parameters.description: Controls how fast chemical A diffuses. Generally, the Gray-Scott model sits at 1.0 and the Kenjiro Maginu model sits at 1.0.

parameters.label: Diffusion B
parameters.description: Controls how fast chemical B diffuses. Generally, the Gray-Scott model sits at 0.5 and the Kenjiro Maginu model sits at 1.0.

parameters.label: Invert Boundary
parameters.description: Inverts the input boundary shape.

parameters.label: Boundary Threshold
parameters.description: The offset of the boundary shape. Higher values grow the shape and lower values shrink the shape.

parameters.label: Boundary Smoothing
parameters.description: The amount to blur the boundary shape, which causes the reaction to contract away from the border of the boundary. At lower Reaction Scales, high values of smoothing can sometimes cause instability.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the values of the output pattern.

parameters.label: Normalize Model
parameters.description: Remaps the range of the output to keep the values consistent across models. This is useful since some models and modes have 'weaker' values.

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.description: The minimum pixel value of the image.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.description: The maximum pixel value of the image.

inputs.label: chemical
inputs.description: The input chemical from the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP.

inputs.label: feedback
inputs.description: A cable of the current feedback data. This is fedback to the input. The structure of this cable must match the initial structure provided on the block begin.

outputs.label: product
outputs.description: The output pattern.

outputs.label: feedback
outputs.description: A cable of the current feedback data.

entries.title: Refract from Height
entries.summary: Refracts an image through a height layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the source image. The default value is Box. See Filters for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: Local: Use the source layer's local space for the view direction or position. World: Use world space for the view direction or position.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The format of the normal input. This is available when the normal input is wired. See Normals for more information. Signed (-1 to 1): Treat the normal input as signed normals, compatible with geometry attributes. Offset (0 to 1): Treat the normal input as offset normals, compatible with normal maps.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.description: Use a directional view ray. When this is off, the node uses a point view position.

parameters.label: View Azimuth
parameters.description: The horizontal angle of the directional view ray.

parameters.label: View Altitude
parameters.description: The vertical angle of the directional view ray above the horizon.

parameters.label: View Position
parameters.description: The point view position in the selected space.

parameters.label: Index of Refraction
parameters.description: The index of refraction of the transparent medium. The default value of 1.33 approximates water.

parameters.label: Height Offset
parameters.description: The value to add to the height layer before tracing rays. If the normal input is wired without a height input, this sets the flat surface height.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.description: The value to multiply the height layer by before tracing rays. This is disabled when a normal input is wired.

parameters.label: Compute Derivative outside Image
parameters.description: Allows the internal derivative calculation for the height surface to read outside the image bounds. This affects the surface normals used for refraction.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The kernel size for the internal derivative calculation on the height surface.

parameters.label: Index of Refraction
parameters.description: The index of refraction of the medium below the ground surface. The default value of 1.0 approximates air.

parameters.label: Ground Offset
parameters.description: The value to add to the ground height before tracing ray intersections.

parameters.label: Ground Scale
parameters.description: The value to multiply the ground height by before tracing ray intersections.

parameters.label: Ray Trace Iterations
parameters.description: The number of Newton iterations used to approximate where refracted view rays intersect the ground height layer.

parameters.label: Compute Derivative outside Image
parameters.description: Allows the internal derivative calculation for the ground layer to read outside the image bounds. This affects the ray-ground intersection solve.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: The kernel size for the internal derivative calculation on the ground layer.

parameters.label: Material
parameters.description: The transparent material used for spectral dispersion and absorbance. Use a higher Number of Colors value for smoother dispersion. Water: Uses water-like dispersion and absorbance. Glass: Uses glass-like dispersion and absorbance. Diamond: Uses diamond-like dispersion and uniform absorbance in the entire wavelengths.

parameters.label: Medium Color
parameters.description: The tint color of the transparent medium.

parameters.label: Light Absorbance
parameters.description: Controls how much light is absorbed as rays travel through the medium. Higher values make deeper or longer paths darker and more affected by the medium's material and color.

parameters.label: Dispersion
parameters.description: The amount of spectral dispersion. Higher values increase color separation.

parameters.label: Number of Colors
parameters.description: The number of wavelength samples used for dispersion. Higher values create smoother dispersion, but take longer to cook.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.description: The strength of the reflected environment.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.description: Controls the distribution of the reflection. Lower values spread the reflection more broadly across the surface, while higher values concentrate it near stronger Fresnel highlights.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: The tint color of the reflection.

parameters.label: Saturation Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the saturation of the reflected environment.

parameters.label: Environment Map Offset
parameters.description: Rotates the environment map projection used for reflection and refracted background lookup.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The Mono, UV, RGB, or RGBA layer to sample through the refractive surface.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: The height layer representing the surface of the transparent medium. If the normal input is wired, the node uses the normal input for surface normals instead of computing them from height derivatives.

inputs.label: ground
inputs.description: An optional height layer representing the ground surface where the source image is sampled.

inputs.label: normal
inputs.description: An optional RGB layer that stores the surface normals in either Signed or Offset format.

inputs.label: envmap
inputs.description: An optional environment map used for surface reflection and for the refracted background behind transparent source pixels.

outputs.label: result
outputs.description: The final RGB image with refraction and reflection.

outputs.label: refract
outputs.description: The RGB image containing the refracted source image.

outputs.label: reflect
outputs.description: The RGB image containing the reflected environment.

entries.title: Remap
entries.summary: Remaps a layer, VDB, or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA channels to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is 1, which means this node uses only the new value. See Mask for more information. Toggle RGB: Turns the Red, Green, and Blue channels on and off. Red: Applies this node's effects to the Red channel. Green: Applies this node's effects to the Green channel. Blue: Applies this node's effects to the Blue channel. Alpha: Applies this node's effects to the Alpha channel.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The method used to remap the layer, VDB, or attribute. Remap: Remap the layer, VDB, or attribute from an input range to an output range. Threshold: Remap the layer, VDB, or attribute based on a threshold and a width to an output range. The threshold is equal to the midpoint. Any values above 0.5 become 1 and any values below 0.5 become 0 if Threshold When is Greater, Threshold is 0.5, Width is 0, and the output is (0,1).

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.description: Sets the Input Min and Input Max parameters to the minimum and maximum values of the source input.

parameters.label: Input Min
parameters.description: When Operation is Remap, values lesser than or equal to this value are remapped to be Output Min. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Input Min.

parameters.label: Input Max
parameters.description: When Operation is Remap, values greater than or equal to this value are remapped to be Output Max. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Input Max.

parameters.label: Threshold When
parameters.description: When Operation is Threshold, this determines whether to remap values that're higher than, lower than, or equal to the threshold. Greater: Remap values greater than the threshold to the higher end of the output range. Greater or Equal: Remap values greater than or equal to the threshold to the higher end of the output range. Less: Remap values lesser than the threshold to the higher end of the output range. Less or Equal: Remap values lesser than or equal to the threshold to the higher end of the output range.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: When Operation is Threshold, this is the value of the input range that maps to the midpoint of the output range. A Threshold of 0.5 with a Width of 0.0 represents an input range of (0.5,0.5). TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Threshold.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: When Operation is Threshold, this is the range on both sides of the threshold that determines the input minimum and maximum. A Threshold of 0.5 with a Width of 0.2 represents an input range of (0.4,0.6).

parameters.label: Output Min
parameters.description: The lower end of the output range.

parameters.label: Output Max
parameters.description: The higher end of the output range.

parameters.label: Outside Range
parameters.description: When Operation is Remap, this determines how to treat values outside of the input range (Input Min and Input Max). Clamp at End: Values outside of the input range clamp within the input range. Repeat: Values outside of the input range loop through the input range. Extend: Values outside of the input range extend the output range.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.description: Applies the Ramp parameter and any connected ramp input.

parameters.label: Ramp
parameters.description: A mono ramp that shapes the remapped output. See Ramp parameters for more information.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The original layer, VDB, or attribute to remap.

inputs.label: input_min
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel layer, VDB, or attribute of the same type as the source that overrides the input_min parameter.

inputs.label: input_max
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel layer, VDB, or attribute of the same type as the source that overrides the input_max parameter.

inputs.label: output_min
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel layer, VDB, or attribute of the same type as the source that overrides the output_min parameter.

inputs.label: output_max
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel layer, VDB, or attribute of the same type as the source that overrides the output_max parameter.

inputs.label: ramp
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel remap ramp for the input, which overrides the Ramp parameter.

inputs.label: mask
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel mask amount that's scaled by the Mask parameter.

outputs.label: remap
outputs.description: The remapped source layer, VDB, or attribute.

entries.title: Resample
entries.summary: Performs image scaling by changing the width, height, and pixel sizes.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Size Control
parameters.description: The method used to control how resampling is done. Resolution: Control the number of pixels in the width or height. Aspect Ratio: Control the ratio between the width and height. Pixel Size: Control the size of the pixels.

parameters.label: Base Size
parameters.description: The base size to use as the final output's dimensions. Parameter: Set the base parameters directly using Base Resolution, Base Aspect Ratio, or Pixel Size. Size Input: Inherit the base parameters from the size_ref input or, if not wired in, the source input.

parameters.label: Base Resolution
parameters.description: When Size Control is Resolution and Base Size is Parameter, this is the base number of pixels for the final image's width and height.

parameters.label: Base Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: When Size Control is Aspect Ratio and Base Size is Parameter, this is the base aspect ratio for the final image.

parameters.label: Pixel Size
parameters.description: When Size Control is Pixel Size and Base Size is Parameter, this is the base pixel size for the final image. The base pixel size is square pixels, so this size is for both the width and height of a pixel.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The scale to apply to the Base Size. For Resolution, this scales the number of pixels in both dimensions. For Aspect Ratio, this scales the aspect ratio. For Pixel Size, this scales the pixel's dimensions.

parameters.label: Resolution Scale
parameters.description: When Size Control is Resolution, this scales the number of pixels in width and height respectively.

parameters.label: Fixed Dimension
parameters.description: When Size Control is Aspect Ratio, this determines which dimension stays constant from the input image. The other dimension changes to match the aspect ratio. Width: The width matches the input image's width. Height: The height matches the input image's height. Smaller Dimension: The smaller resolution matches the input image's smaller resolution. Larger Dimension: The larger resolution matches the input image's larger resolution.

parameters.label: Size Scale
parameters.description: When Size Control is Pixel Size, this scales the pixel's width and height respectively.

parameters.label: Reframe to Destination
parameters.description: Stretches the input image through resampling to conform to the entire boundary of the output and maintains the given pixel size. Specifically, this makes the display window match the data window. See Data and display windows for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filter used to sample. See Filters for more information. Point: Sets the pixel value to the pixel value of the nearest neighbor. Bilinear: Sets the pixel value through bilinear interpolation. Box: Sets the pixel value through a box filter, done by sampling all pixels within a box on the original image's matching pixel. Bartlett: Sets the pixel value through interpolating according to a triangular window or a Bartlett window, taking each pixel as a sample of this signal. Catmull-Rom: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Catmull-Rom spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter. Mitchell: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the Mitchell-Netravali filter. B-spline: Sets the pixel value through a bicubic spline known as the B-spline. This is a special case of the Mitchell-Netravali filter.

parameters.label: Stretch Behavior
parameters.description: Determine how the image stretches after the resample operation. Specifically, this determines how to stretch the display window. NOTE: If Reframe to Destination is on, this parameter has no effect since the display window doesn't stretch differently. Stretch to Fit: Stretches the pixels to fit within the new display window. The display window is scaled naively according to the same scale that the data window is scaled at. Fit Horizontally: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window's x dimension in relation to the data window's x dimension. Fit Vertically: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window's y dimension in relation to the data window's y dimension. Fit Maximally: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window according to the original image's data window's maximal dimension. Fit Minimally: Maintains the original pixel aspect ratio and aspect ratio by scaling the display window according to the original image's data window's minimal dimension.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The source image to resample.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

outputs.label: resample
outputs.description: The output image with the new resolution or pixel size.

entries.title: Ripple Block Begin
entries.summary: Start of a Ripple simulation block.

parameters.label: Block Path
parameters.description: The path to the Ripple Block End COP that defines the end of this block. The Block End node must be at the same network level as this Block Begin node.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: The initial wave height values. These define the starting wave height above the rest value.

inputs.label: rest
inputs.description: The equilibrium value that the simulation returns to over time.

inputs.label: wavespeed
inputs.description: A mask controlling how fast waves propagate across the image layer. This is multiplied against the Wave Speed parameter on the Ripple Block End COP.

inputs.label: conservation
inputs.description: A mask indicating how much of the wave energy is conserved over time. This is multiplied against the Conservation parameter on the Ripple Block End COP.

inputs.label: spring
inputs.description: A mask controlling the strength of the restoring force that pulls values toward the rest state. This is multiplied against the Rest Spring parameter on the Ripple Block End COP.

inputs.label: feedback
inputs.description: A cable providing wires that are fed back into the next iteration of the solve. The cable structure must match the inputs on the Ripple Block End COP. This input is only read on the initial frame.

inputs.label: passthrough
inputs.description: An optional cable providing wires that are evaluated outside the simulation. These are read each frame and can be used to inject animated sources, but cannot depend on the results of the simulation.

inputs.label: adjacency
inputs.description: An optional cable providing adjacency data that should be computed outside of the simulation. Adjacency nodes can be used to allow pixels to traverse across UV seams (when usually they are on opposite sides of the UV map). These are read each frame, so they can't depend on the results of the simulation. When you wire in this input, it automatically runs over adjacency.

outputs.label: height
outputs.description: The wave height.

outputs.label: feedback
outputs.description: A cable of the extra data that has been fed back into this frame.

outputs.label: passthrough
outputs.description: A cable passing through the input, updated each frame from the source.

outputs.label: adjacency
outputs.description: An adjacency cable passing rasterized geometry through the input, updated each frame from the source.

entries.title: Ripple Block End
entries.summary: End of a Ripple simulation block

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Simulate: Turns on simulation so block outputs feed directly back into the inputs, which creates a feedback loop. This is useful for complex motion and simulations.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: Reset Simulation: When Simulate is on, this clears the entire simulation cache.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: Time Scale: When Simulate is on, this is the amount to scale the time inside the block. A value of 1 maintains the normal speed, a value greater than 1 speeds up the simulation, and a value less than 1 slows down the simulation.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: When simulation is on, each frame is divided into this number of substeps. Increasing the number of substeps improves simulation accuracy and can help maintain stability when high-speed ripples would otherwise cause instability.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Amount of iterations to run in non-simulation mode.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: Live Simulation: When Simulate is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar. TIP: Live Simulation doesn't save the results like other simulation types in Houdini, so use a Stash COP to save results.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: Toggle Live Simulation: When Live Simulation is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation. TIP: You can also use the Icon:BUTTONS/live_disable Live Simulation button to pause and resume live simulation. See Cooking controls for more information.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: Live Tick: When Live Simulation is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.description: When Live Simulation is on, the Start Frame, Cached Frames, and Checkpoint Rate parameters no longer apply.

parameters.label: Caching
parameters.description: Turns on caching of frames.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: Start Frame: When Simulate is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: Cached Frames: When Simulate is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: Checkpoint Rate: When Simulate is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to 24 to cache frames 24, 48, 72, and such. This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to 0 to disable checkpointing.

parameters.label: Collision Threshold
parameters.description: When the collision input is used, this value sets the threshold at which the mask acts as a collider.

parameters.label: Wave Speed
parameters.description: Controls how fast the ripples travel from pixel to pixel. This is proportional to the change in image space when the buffer coordinate changes by one in either x or y.

parameters.label: Conservation
parameters.description: Controls how much wave velocity is kept over time. It directly affects how quickly the motion slows down. A value of 1 means no velocity is lost. A value of 0.5 means half the velocity remains after one second. A value of 0 removes all motion immediately. Values outside the 0–1 range are not valid and will be clamped.

parameters.label: Spring
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the spring force that pulls pixels toward their rest value. Wave motion is preserved by the wave speed, while the spring pulls values back toward the rest state. This can create additional ripples as the values settle.

inputs.label: height
inputs.description: Wave height.

inputs.label: feedback
inputs.description: A cable of the current feedback data. This is fed back to the input. The structure of this cable must match the initial structure provided on the block begin.

inputs.label: collision
inputs.description: An optional Mono layer providing a mask of a collider.

outputs.label: ripple
outputs.description: The output ripples.

outputs.label: feedback
outputs.description: A cable of the current feedback data.

entries.title: UV Sample
entries.summary: Samples an input layer using a UV layer or attribute.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: UV Space
parameters.description: The space that the UV input is in. This affects the required range of the UV input. Texture: Use texture space, which is 0 to 1 in the data window of the input. This provides normalized coordinates that're independent of the source's aspect ratio. For example, use this space when looking up into a latitude and longitude map. Image: Use image space, which is -1 to 1 in the display window of the input. This preserves square pixels for non-square aspect ratios. This space is invariant to cropping or overscanning.

parameters.label: Filter Scale
parameters.description: For non-identity UV maps, the input must be filtered to avoid aliasing. This value defaults to the size of the voxels, but can be increased or decreased to reflect the actual nature of the UV map. Note that attributes lack an intrinsic filter size so this likely has to be manually adjusted to the pixel size.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. The default value is Box. See Filters for more information.

inputs.label: uv

inputs.label: filterscale
inputs.description: An optional per-pixel filter scale multiplier, which multiplies the Filter Scale parameter. The provided uvmap may have seams and can't be inspected to determine the rate of change, so an explicit input is required.

inputs.label: texture

outputs.label: sample

entries.title: SDF Adjust
entries.summary: Modifies the values for a Mono SDF layer.

parameters.label: Iso Offset
parameters.description: Controls the crossing point of the signed distance field values that is considered the border of the shape. Higher values will enlarge the shape, while lower values will shrink the shape.

parameters.label: Outline
parameters.description: When turned on, the shape is made into a hollowed thin shape, and this value controls the thickness around the original border. This is achieved by taking the field's absolute value and subtracting this number from it.

parameters.label: Absolute Value
parameters.description: When turned on, this changes all negative values into positives. This will remove what would be considered the inside of the shape, only leaving a thin border of the shape.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: When turned on, this will swap positive and negative values, making the outside region to be considered the inside of the shape.

inputs.label: sdf
inputs.description: The SDF Mono layer to adjust.

outputs.label: sdf
outputs.description: The adjusted SDF Mono layer.

entries.title: SDF Blend
entries.summary: Combines two Mono SDF layers.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Controls the operation to combine the two signed distance fields. Union: Creates a new solid shape which encloses the combined shape(s) of the two inputs. Intersect: Creates a new solid shape which encloses any shared shape(s) between the two inputs. Subtract: Removes from the first input the shape(s) based on the second input. Difference: Removes the shared shape(s) of the two inputs.

parameters.label: Fillet
parameters.description: Controls how to join the input shapes at the intersection points. None: No fillet operation is applied. Smooth: The intersection points between the shapes will be smoothed. Round: Similar to the smooth, but it uses a quarter-circle to join the two shapes smoothly. Chamfer: The intersection points between the shapes will make a 45-degree chamfered edge.

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.description: Controls the amount of smoothing applied where the two input shapes join together.

parameters.label: Round
parameters.description: Controls the amount of rounding applied where the two input shapes join together.

parameters.label: Chamfer
parameters.description: Controls the amount of chamfer applied where the two input shapes join together.

parameters.label: Re-Normalize
parameters.description: When turned on, the signed distance field is re-calculated after the blend. This is needed as some operations do not preserve the correct field values.

inputs.label: sdfA
inputs.description: The first SDF Mono layer to combine.

inputs.label: sdfB
inputs.description: The second SDF Mono layer to combine.

outputs.label: sdf
outputs.description: The combined SDF Mono layer.

entries.title: SDF Shape
entries.summary: Builds a 2D signed distance field of a selected shape.

parameters.label: Shape Class
parameters.description: Shapes are organized into various groups. Basic shapes are consist of elementary algebraic shapes, while Marker and Compound contain shapes of various complexities.

parameters.label: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The list of available elementary algebraic shapes when Shape Class is set to Basic. See Basic Shapes for more information.

parameters.label: Markers
parameters.description: The list of available marker shapes when Shape Class is set to Marker. See Markers for more information.

parameters.label: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: The list of available complex shapes when Shape Class is set to Compound. See Compound Shapes for more information.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The radius of the circle. Use this parameter to control the size of the circle.

parameters.label: Arc
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than 1, the circle becomes an open arc, which can be used to create shapes of a sliced pie.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than 1, the circle becomes hollowed, which can be used to create ring-like shapes.

parameters.label: Round Ends
parameters.description: When both Arc and Thickness are turned on, use this to make the end of the ring shape rounded.

parameters.label: Quadratic Circle
parameters.description: When turned on, the circle changes into a quadratic circle shape.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the diamond shape.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Sets the length of the line, which is oriented horizontally at the center. Turn on Use Points next to this parameter if you need to control the exact positions for the start and end points of the line.

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the start and end points of the lines can be controlled by Start Point and End Point parameters.

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the start point of the line.

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the end point of the line.

parameters.label: Add Thickness
parameters.description: When turned on, the start and end thickness of the lines can be controlled by Start Thickness and End Thickness.

parameters.label: Start Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the start point.

parameters.label: End Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the end point.

parameters.label: Bulge
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the thickness at the center of the line. A value of 0 means no bulging. In this mode, only Start Thickness is on to control the same thickness at both ends of the line.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the rectangle shape.

parameters.label: Round Corners
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the roundness of the corners. With a value of 1 and both horizontal and vertical size is equal, the shape becomes a circle. When this is set to 0, the rectangle is not rounded. Use Separate Controls next to this parameter to control the roundness for each corner separately.

parameters.label: Separate Controls
parameters.description: When turned on, the roundness of each corner can be controlled separately.

parameters.label: Top Left
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top left corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Top Right
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top right corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Bottom Left
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom left corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Bottom Right
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom right corner of the rectangle. Value of 1 means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of 0 means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the polygon shape.

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the polygon. The larger the number the more the shape will resemble a circle.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the spiral shape.

parameters.label: Arc Bend
parameters.description: Controls how much each arc length segment should bend towards the center. When this value is set to 0 and the Number of Arcs is set to 4, the arc is a perfect circle.

parameters.label: Number of Arcs
parameters.description: Controls the number of components the spiral is made of. When Arc Bend is set to 0, a value of 4 creates a perfect circle.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for a squircle, which is a shape intermediate between a square and a circle.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.description: Controls the shape of the squircle. The value of 2 creates a perfect circle. Values above this will blend the shape more into a square. A value of 1 creates a diamond shape.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the star shape.

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the star. The larger the number, the more the shape will resemble a circle.

parameters.label: Angle Factor
parameters.description: Controls how much the center of the sides push towards the center of the shape. The angle factor of 2 will create a regular polygon shape instead of a star.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the trapezoid.

parameters.label: Bottom Length
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the bottom of the trapezoid.

parameters.label: Top Length
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the top of the trapezoid.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the bottom of the triangle.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the triangle.

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the three corners of the triangle are controlled by Point0, Point1 and Point2 parameters.

parameters.label: Point 0
parameters.description: Controls the bottom left corner position of the triangle.

parameters.label: Point 1
parameters.description: Controls the top corner position of the triangle.

parameters.label: Point 2
parameters.description: Controls the bottom right corner position of the triangle.

parameters.label: Arc
parameters.description: Controls the amount of distortion applied to the wave. Values closer to 0 will make the wave look like a flat line. The value of 0.5 closer resembles a sine wave, while a value of 1 will fold the wave pattern onto each other.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the wave pattern. Lower values will make smaller patterns.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The radius of the marker. Use this parameter to control the size of the shape.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal width of the arch. Increase this value to make the shape wider.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the arch. The value of 0 creates a half-circle.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Controls the overall length of the arrow, both shaft and head. After adjusting the length, use the Head Ratio to control the size of the head relative to the new arrow length.

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the start and end points of the arrow can be controlled by Start Point and End Point parameters.

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the start point of the arrow.

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the end point of the arrow.

parameters.label: Shaft Thickness
parameters.description: Sets the vertical thickness of the shaft of the arrow. Increase this parameter to make the shaft thicker.

parameters.label: Head Thickness
parameters.description: Sets the vertical thickness of the head of the arrow. Increase this parameter to make the head thicker.

parameters.label: Head Ratio
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal ratio between the head and the shaft of the arrow.

parameters.label: Cross Size
parameters.description: Controls the overall size of the cross shape.

parameters.label: Cross Inset
parameters.description: Controls the amount to chip away from the corners of a square. When this value is set to 0, the result is a perfect square. Increasing this value will chip away the shape starting from the corners of the square.

parameters.label: Cross Bevel
parameters.description: Controls the amount of rounding at the inner corner of the cross.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the egg.

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.description: Controls the roundness of the top edge of the egg. A value of 0 creates an egg shape with a sharp top edge, and increasing this value smooths the top edge. The value of 1 will create a perfect circle shape.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the fishscale shape. This shape is generally used for fishscale-like tile patterns.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The overall size of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Separation
parameters.description: Controls the arc length of the horseshoe. The value of 0 creates a perfect round shape, closing both ends of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.description: Controls the extent of each end of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Outter Radius
parameters.description: Controls the overall radius of the moon. For a generic moon shape, this parameter should be larger than Inner Radius.

parameters.label: Inner Radius
parameters.description: Controls the radius of the shape that will be cut out from the body of the moon given by Outter Radius.

parameters.label: Inner Offset
parameters.description: The horizontal position of the inner shape given by Inner Radius to control where to cut into the moon.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the octagon-dot shape. This shape is generally used for octagon-dot-like tile patterns.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: Controls the overall size of the cross. The value of 0 creates a perfect circle.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the cross.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the vesica.

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.description: Controls the vertical thickness of the vesica shape. Increasing this value makes the shape more rounded.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.description: The amount of horizontal and vertical translation. TIP: Click Icon:BUTTONS/layer_position_sample and then click a location in the image to set the Translate.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.description: The amount of rotation.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.description: The amount of shearing.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.description: The amount of uniform scaling.

inputs.label: size_ref
inputs.description: A representative layer that determines the size of the output image and controls the metadata.

outputs.label: sdf
outputs.description: The SDF Mono layer.

entries.title: SDF to Mono
entries.summary: Converts an SDF field to a mono image layer.

parameters.label: Background Value
parameters.description: Controls the value outside the shape defined by the signed distance field. To remap the distance field, change the menu on the right side of this parameter from Constant to Iso Distance.

parameters.label: Iso Range
parameters.description: Specifies the horizontal extent of the Remap Ramp, which is evaluated to transform the signed distance field to background value.

parameters.label: Number of Cycles
parameters.description: Controls the number of repetitions inside the signed distance range given by Iso Range. The menu on the right side of this parameter controls the method by which the repetition occurs.

parameters.label: Remap Ramp
parameters.description: Controls how the signed distance field values are remapped. The horizontal axis of this ramp spans Iso Range. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.

parameters.label: Draw Shape
parameters.description: When turned on, the shape defined by the signed distance field is drawn.

parameters.label: Shape Value
parameters.description: Controls the value inside the shape defined by the signed distance field. To remap the distance field, change the menu on the right side of this parameter from Constant to Iso Distance.

parameters.label: Iso Distance
parameters.description: Specifies the distance from the border of the shape. This is the horizontal extent of the Remap Ramp, which is evaluated to transform the signed distance field to shape value.

parameters.label: Remap Ramp
parameters.description: Controls how the signed distance field values are remapped. The horizontal axis of this ramp spans between the border of the shape and Iso Distance. For more information about using ramps, see Ramp parameters.

parameters.label: Draw Outline
parameters.description: When turned on, the outline of the shape defined by the signed distance field is drawn.

parameters.label: Outline Value
parameters.description: Controls the value of the outline at the border of the shape defined by the signed distance field.

parameters.label: Outline Width
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the outline. Increase this value to create a thicker outline.

parameters.label: Alignment
parameters.description: Controls if the outline is drawn inside or outside the shape, while touching the border of the shape defined by the signed distance field. Optionally, the outline can be centered around the border of the shape.

parameters.label: Draw Shadowing
parameters.description: When turned on, a shadow is drawn that is cast by the shape defined by the signed distance field.

parameters.label: Shadow Density
parameters.description: Controls the visibility of the shadow. Lower this value to make the shadow less visible.

parameters.label: Shadow Falloff
parameters.description: Controls the extent of the shadow. Increase this value to make the shadow cover larger areas.

parameters.label: Shadow Value
parameters.description: Controls the value of the shadow. Make sure this value is different from Background Value to display the shadow.

parameters.label: Iso Offset
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/sdfadjust#isooffset

parameters.label: Onion Skin
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/sdfadjust#onion

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the smoothness of the shape or outline. Increase this value to blur the shape.

parameters.label: Anti-Aliasing
parameters.description: When turned on, it reduces the jagged edges by smoothing the drawn shapes and outlines.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: #contentfrom: /nodes/cop/sdfadjust#invert

inputs.label: sdf
inputs.description: The SDF mono layer to convert.

outputs.label: mono
outputs.description: The converted mono layer.

entries.title: Segment by Connectivity
entries.summary: Segment a layer into connected components.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See Signatures for more information.

parameters.label: Connectivity
parameters.description: The rule that determines whether pixels are connected or unconnected. Below Threshold: Connect all pixels below the threshold. Above Threshold: Connect all pixels above the threshold. At Threshold: Connect pixels to their neighbors if they're on the same side of the threshold. At Levels: Connect pixels if they're in the same band of values. Each band is the Threshold size.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold for connectivity. When Connectivity is At Levels, this is the width of a band of connectivity. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Threshold.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: When Connectivity is At Levels, this is the global offset to adjust where the bands split.

parameters.label: Collapse IDs
parameters.description: Collapse the generated ID values so they range from zero to the number of segments. While the order is deterministic, it will vary depending on where the first pixel of each region is located, so should not be relied upon for an animated source.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The layer in which to detect connectivity.

outputs.label: id
outputs.description: The ID layer with a unique integer that's greater than or equal to 0 for each connected region. Regions that don't match the connectivity region get an ID of -1.

outputs.label: alpha
outputs.description: The mono layer, which is 1 if the pixel met the connectivity rule and 0 if it didn't.

entries.title: Segment by Value
entries.summary: Segment a mono layer into bands of similar value.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to specify the bands of similar value. Width and Offset: Specify the width of the band and an offset from zero. Number of Segments: Specify the number of segments that fit inside the provided range.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.description: When Method is Width and Offset, this is the maximum difference in value to belong to the same segment.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: When Method is Width and Offset, this is the offset of where to start the first segment.

parameters.label: Segments
parameters.description: When Method is Number of Segments, this is the number of segments to fit in the provided minimum to maximum values.

parameters.label: Segment Location
parameters.description: The method used to convert the value into a segment integer. Starts at Value: Floor to convert the value into a segment integer. Centered at Value: Round to convert the value into a segment integer.

parameters.label: Minimum Value
parameters.description: The minimal input value to use. Values outside of this follow the Values Below rules. When Method is Number of Segments, this is the start of the interval. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Minimum Value.

parameters.label: Maximum Value
parameters.description: The maximal input value to use. Values outside of this follow the Values Above rules. When Method is Number of Segments, this is the end of the interval. TIP: Click Smallicon:BUTTONS/layer_sample and then click on the layer to set the Maximum Value.

parameters.label: Values Below
parameters.description: The method used to treat values below the Minimum Value. Extend: Convert and round values with no clamping. Invalid (-1): An explicit -1 is output for the segment ID. Clamp: Clamp values to the minimal value. Wrap: Wrap values, which means segment values repeat cyclicly.

parameters.label: Values Above
parameters.description: The method used to treat values above the Maximum Value. Extend: Convert and round values with no clamping. Invalid (-1): An explicit -1 is output for the segment ID. Clamp: Clamp values to the minimal value. Wrap: Wrap values, which means segment values repeat cyclicly.

inputs.label: source
inputs.description: The layer to segment.

outputs.label: id
outputs.description: The ID layer that stores the generated segment numbers.
